result.redesign:
Replace the single portrait 260x350 SVG of unlabeled boxes with a landscape SVG (viewBox about 0 0 420 250, drawing filling >=80% of it) that shows a different labelled scene per stage and visibly changes at every one of the 60 steps. Every part gets an in-place text label (>=11 px rendered, --sans, leader lines for thin parts), and the element added by the current step is outlined in --accent with a small 'this step' tag; earlier parts stay at full color, future parts are absent.

Scenes by stage:
1. Design & masks (steps 1-4): a chip floorplan grid labelled 'RTL -> gates' (1), 'placed & routed blocks' (2), a frozen GDSII sheet labelled 'tape-out' (3), and a reticle rectangle with a pellicle labelled '6-inch mask, one of 70-100+; set $20-30M' (4).
2. Materials (5-10): a left-to-right chain that lights up one node per step: quartz lump '98% SiO2' -> submerged-arc furnace with electrodes 'MG-Si, ~2,000 C' -> fluidized bed 'TCS' -> distillation column '9N-11N' -> Siemens bell jar with glowing U-rods '~1,100 C, 3-5 days' -> crushed chunks in a bag 'polysilicon'.
3. Crystal (11-13): a CZ puller: chamber outline, graphite susceptor, quartz crucible, melt (11, label '~400 kg Si, 1,420 C, Ar'), seed + Dash neck + shoulder + 300 mm body growing (12), then the cropped/ground ingot with a notch and 'resistivity test' (13).
4. Wafer (14-18): ingot with diamond-wire lines and '1,500-2,000 wafers, 150 um kerf' (14), a wafer edge profile rounding (15), a two-sided polish pad and 'sub-nm roughness' (16), a wafer with laser mark + thin epi layer (17), a FOUP with 25 wafers 'to fab' (18).
5. Device cross-section (19-43), drawn along the fin (source-gate-drain view): Si substrate with edge label '300 mm, 775 um' and a zero-layer mark (19); Si/SiGe superlattice stripes 'GAA only' (20); fin/nanosheet stack with hard mask (21); STI oxide either side, distinct fill, labelled (22); dotted well/Vt doping (23); grey dashed dummy gate straddling the channel (24); thin spacers on both sidewalls (25); recessed S/D + inner spacers (26); raised green S/D epi touching the channel on both sides 'SiGe:B / Si:P' (27); ILD0 fill up to the dummy-gate top (28); dummy gate replaced by purple HKMG gate 'HfO2 + WFM + W' (29); gate cut + SiN cap (30); two contact trenches down to S/D (31); orange S/D contacts 'Co/W/Ru' (32); gate contact + V0 via (33); M0/M1 lines with vias into the contacts (34); a bracketed bundle of Mx lines with vias labelled 'Mx x15-18, pitch 24 nm -> um' (35); wide top metal/RDL (36); passivation with a pad opening (37); optional backside rail under a thinned substrate 'A16-class only' (38); a CD-SEM/probe icon over the stack 'metrology' (39); probe needles touching pads 'wafer sort' (40); Cu pillar/microbump in the opening '40 um pitch' (41); substrate height shrinks '775 -> ~100 um' (42); two saw kerfs and 'known-good die' (43).
6. HBM (44-48): a DRAM die with TSV dots (44), base logic die (45), thinned die '~30 um' with backside bumps (46), stack growing to 8/12-high with labels 'TC-NCF / MR-MUF / hybrid' (47), a tester tick 'KGSD' (48).
7. Packaging (49-54): ABF substrate with 10-20 layer stripes (49), silicon interposer with TSVs and 3-4 Cu layers (50), GPU die + two HBM stacks bonded on the interposer wafer '40 um pitch, underfill' (51), interposer thinned/bumped/diced (52), CoW module on the substrate '130-150 um C4' (53), lid + TIM + BGA balls (54).
8. System (55-60): package in an ATE socket 'burn-in, binning' (55), running a workload 'SLT' (56), package on an SXM PCB with VRMs (57), 8 packages on an HGX board / 4 on a GB200 tray with cold plates (58), a rack of 18 compute + 9 switch trays with an NVLink spine '72 GPUs, ~120-140 kW' (59), a row of racks with cooling and fabric (60).

Readouts: fix the metal-layer counter (0 -> 1 at 34 -> '~15-18' at 35 -> '15-18 + RDL' after 36, frozen), rename the first group 'Design' and add 'HBM', span the fab clock over the wafer-fab steps only, and give the 60 dots tooltips, a hover style, and >=14 px targets.

defects.what: There is no schematic of the real thing. The widget is a bar chart plus a bare sine wave with three unlabeled grey boxes. Nothing shows a reticle, diffraction orders, the projection lens/pupil (what NA is), the immersion water, the resist/wafer, or the focus band (what DOF is). Two of the three controls (wavelength select, NA slider) change only numbers: the bar chart uses fixed per-generation NAs and the aerial image depends only on k1, so dragging NA from 0.9 to 1.35 leaves both drawings pixel-identical (shots 193i-na-min vs default). Fails criterion 1 and most of 2.
defects.where: site/widgets/rayleigh.js lines 49-96 (paintBars, paintAerial)
defects.fix: Redraw per the redesign below: an optics cross-section (illumination -> reticle grating -> diffraction orders -> lens pupil scaled by NA -> water layer when immersion -> resist/wafer with the aerial image drawn in place and a DOF band), all parts labelled in place and all three levers visibly moving something.

defects.what: Printed-line rectangles are physically wrong: they are centred on the intensity threshold crossings. Probe at 100% contrast: rect x=30..136.7 while the curve peaks at x=30 and troughs at x=136.7, so each 'printed line' spans half-bright/half-dark. A non-expert reading 'printed lines' would learn the wrong relationship between image and resist. Also the threshold is at the mean, so the crossing width is constant regardless of contrast; narrowing the boxes with k1 contradicts the geometry drawn above them.
defects.where: site/widgets/rayleigh.js lines 90-93 (cx0 = X0 + (i + 0.25) * period)
defects.fix: Centre the resist line on a trough (positive tone: resist stays where it is dark) using cx = X0 + (i + 0.5) * period, and derive its width from the threshold crossing. Put the threshold above the mean (e.g. I = 0.5 + 0.5*mod*cos, threshold 0.7) so a low-contrast image never crosses it and no line prints, which is the real failure mode; draw the lines inside a labelled resist layer, not floating in blank space.

defects.what: DOF uses k2 = 1, giving 105.9 nm at the default (193i, NA 1.35). The module's worked example and Key Numbers table use k2 = 0.6: 'DOF = 0.6 x 193.4 / 1.35^2 = ~64 nm total (+/-32 nm)' and '~60-65 nm total'. The widget's headline DOF disagrees with the course by 65%.

result.redesign: Replace the 'Aerial image (schematic)' panel with a full-width cross-section of the projection optics (viewBox width = container px width, height ~ 340 px; at < 560 px stack the optics above the bar chart). Layout, top to bottom: (1) ILLUMINATION: one or two arrows entering from the top labelled 'illumination'; draw them on-axis when k1 >= 0.5 and tilted (off-axis / dipole) when k1 < 0.5, with a small label 'off-axis: 0th order pushed to the pupil edge'. (2) RETICLE: a horizontal bar with a chrome line/space grating, labelled 'reticle (mask), lines at 4x wafer pitch'. (3) DIFFRACTION ORDERS: from the grating centre draw three rays labelled '-1', '0', '+1'. Use sin(theta) units mapped to horizontal offset at the pupil plane: pupil half-width = NA (scaled so NA 1.35 fills ~45% of the width), order spacing = NA/(2*k1), illumination tilt = 0 for k1 >= 0.5 else NA/(2*k1) - NA so the 0th order sits at one pupil edge and the +1 at the other; draw any order outside the pupil dashed in var(--bad) with the label 'lost (does not reach the lens)'. This makes k1 = 0.5 (two orders just fit on-axis) and k1 = 0.25 (the floor) visible geometry. (4) PROJECTION LENS: a lens outline with the pupil aperture drawn as a gap whose width scales with NA; label 'projection lens, NA = n sin(theta) = 1.35' and draw the acceptance cone half-angle theta from the wafer point. When the ArF immersion source is selected draw a thin blue band between lens and wafer labelled 'water, n = 1.44'; when EUV is selected label the block 'mirrors (drawn as a lens)'. (5) WAFER: a substrate slab labelled 'wafer' with a thin resist layer on top labelled 'resist ~100 nm'. Directly above the resist draw the aerial image I(x) = 0.5 + 0.5*mod*cos(2*pi*x/p) over three periods, with a dashed 'threshold' line above the mean; fill the resist only where I(x) < threshold (positive tone), centred on the dark fringes, so at low contrast the lines get narrow and then vanish. Dimension one period 'pitch = 80.1 nm' and one line 'CD = 40.1 nm' with arrows. (6) DEPTH OF FOCUS: a vertical bracket beside the resist showing the focus band, height proportional to DOF relative to the 100 nm resist (band ~0.64x the resist at 193i NA 1.35, ~6x at i-line NA 0.6), labelled 'DOF = k2 lambda / NA^2 = 64 nm (+/-32 nm)'. All labels in place, 12 px sans for labels and 11-12 px mono for numbers, tokens only. What animates/changes: order angles and pupil width with NA and k1, the water band and lens label with the source, the fringe pitch and line width with CD, the DOF bracket height with lambda/NA. Keep the bar chart below it, fixed as above (1000 nm axis, caption in the heading, 'your setting' marker line, hover tooltips, click-to-select), and make the needs table highlight the reachable rows.

defects.where: site/widgets/upw-mask-cost.js lines 8, 84-96 (STAGES, drawTrain)
defects.what: The 'schematic' is seven identical rounded boxes labelled with undefined abbreviations (RO, EDI, UV, POU) joined by faint arrows. defects.where: site/widgets/upw-mask-cost.js lines 50-52, 68, 104 (defaults 80/25/39, prices $300k/$80k/$25k)
defects.what: Per-layer prices contradict the module. Non-critical DUV is priced at $25k while the widget's own note quotes the module range as $5-20k; the module's worked example uses $400k / $100k / $15k. The default split (25 EUV layers = a 2 nm-class set) therefore evaluates to $11M, and the chart then places 'your setting' inside the '7 nm $10-15M' band — teaching the learner that a 25-EUV-layer set is a 7 nm chip, the opposite of the module's $15M base / $20-30M all-in for that same split. Per-wafer default is $110 vs the module's ~$250.
defects.fix: Use the module's prices ($400k EUV, $100k critical ArFi PSM, $15k KrF/i-line) and defaults (95 layers: 25 EUV, 50 critical, 20 non-critical; 100,000 wafers) so the first frame reproduces the worked example ($15.0M, $150/wafer base, and $20-30M all-in shown as a bracket). Optionally expose the per-layer price as a select within the module range.

defects.what: The chart has no axis, no tick marks and no unit ($M) — a listed common failure — and 'your setting' is drawn as a 2 px vertical stripe (lo == hi) rather than a bar, so the cost split the third readout reports (EUV / critical / non-critical) is never visualised.

result.redesign:
Keep the two-panel calculator, but replace both drawings so they show the mechanism the sliders control, and make them responsive.

PANEL A - Ultrapure-water plant as a live flow schematic (viewBox ~620x240 at desktop; a stacked/vertical variant or container-width viewBox when the box is < 480 px so all text stays >= 11 px on screen). Left to right, as pipes whose stroke width is proportional to flow (m3/day written on each pipe, updating with the sliders):
1. 'City / fresh water' inlet arrow from the far left, labelled 'fresh intake  X m3/day' (this is the number the intake readout shows).
2. 'Pretreatment' block (subtitle: 'filters + carbon: removes chlorine, 5 um particles').
3. 'RO - reverse osmosis' block drawn as a membrane cartridge; from its underside a downward arrow 'reject 20 %  Y m3/day' to a small 'drain' symbol. Label the feed into RO 'RO feed = demand / 0.80'.
4. A compact chain of blocks with one-line subtitles: 'Degas (strips CO2, O2)' -> 'EDI - electrodeionization (ions)' -> 'Mixed bed (to ~18 MOhm-cm)' -> 'UV 185 nm (burns organics, TOC)' -> 'Polish bed (last ions, ppt metals)' -> 'UV 254 nm + ultrafilter (bacteria, 10 nm particles)'. Order must follow the module.
5. Output pipe labelled '18.2 MOhm-cm UPW  demand m3/day' into a 'Fab tools (point of use)' block on the right, with '~1,000 rinse steps per wafer' inside it.
6. Below the tools, a return path 'rinse water to drains' that splits: a loop arrow curving back left into the RO feed labelled 'reclaim R %  Z m3/day' (width follows the reclaim slider), and a downward arrow 'discharge (1-R) %'. When the reclaim slider moves, the reclaim loop thickens and the fresh-intake arrow thins, so the intake formula becomes visible.
7. Optional: animated dots along the pipes at speed proportional to flow (rAF, paused under prefers-reduced-motion, stopped when off-screen).
Hover/focus on any block highlights it (accent outline) and shows a 1-sentence tooltip. Put the spec strip ('18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 1 ppb, particles ~100-1000 / L above 20 nm') under the output pipe at >= 11 px rendered.

PANEL B - Mask set as a stacked cost bar plus amortization:
1. Stacked horizontal bar 'your set': three segments coloured EUV (euv/accent2 token), critical ArFi PSM (si), non-critical KrF/i-line (line2), each labelled 'n x $400k = $10.0M' etc., total at the end.
2. Reference stacked bar 'Module 04 worked example (2 nm-class)': 25 x $400k + 50 x $100k + 20 x $15k = $15M, with a hatched extension/bracket to $20-30M labelled 'pellicles, respins, qualification'. An x-axis with $M ticks and the unit label.
3. Amortization strip beneath: per-wafer mask cost vs wafers shipped on a log axis 1k-1M, with a dot at the current volume and a dashed reference line at the ~$27k N2 wafer price, annotated '2,000 wafers -> ~$12,500/wafer (half the wafer)' and '100,000 wafers -> ~$250/wafer'.
4. Optional icon: a small stack of 6025 reticle squares (count = layers, coloured by type) next to the bar to make 'a mask set' concrete.
Use the module's prices and defaults (95 layers: 25 / 50 / 20; 100,000 wafers) so the first frame equals the worked example; shorten slider labels/outputs and give range inputs min-width so nothing collapses at 360 px.

defects.where: site/widgets/scale-ladder.js mount(): fixed viewBox '0 0 680 820' with font-size 10/10.5/11.5 — qa/shots/scale-ladder-360-dark.png and -360-light.png
defects.what: At 360 px the whole SVG scales to 286 px wide (scale 0.42) so every label renders at 4.2–4.8 px; the drawing is completely unreadable on a phone. Harness tinyText misses it because it only checks HTML elements.
defects.fix: Make the layout responsive instead of scaling: observe the container width with ResizeObserver and rebuild the SVG with viewBox width == container CSS width, so 11–12 px font sizes are real pixels. At any width put the axis near the left (x≈64 at 360, x≈150 at 760), decade labels in a gutter left of the axis, and all items on the right (icon + label + value); let SVG height = items × 32 + 60 and grow as needed.

defects.where: readout 'A ÷ B' stat and w-formula 'ratio = size(A) / size(B)' — shot reversed-bond-vs-rack.png (A = 0.235 nm, B = 2 m shows 8 510 638 298×)
defects.what: The code always divides larger by smaller, so when A < B the stat labelled 'A ÷ B' and the formula both state a value that is the reciprocal of what they claim (true A ÷ B is 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁰).
defects.fix: Either label the stat 'larger ÷ smaller' and write the formula as ratio = max(A,B)/min(A,B), or show the honest A ÷ B (e.g. '1 / 8.5 × 10⁹' when A < B) and keep the sentence in the note in the larger/smaller form.

defects.where: update(): stRatio and note formatting (fmt(ratio,0) for ratio ≥ 1000, roundSig(…,3) for the note)
defects.what: Ratios print with 7–10 significant figures ('1 208 333×', '8 510 638 298×') from inputs with 1–3 sig figs, and the note prints a different number ('~1 210 000') than the stat right above it.
defects.fix: Format the ratio with 2–3 significant figures everywhere: < 10 → 2 decimals; < 1000 → 0–1 decimals; ≥ 1000 → mantissa × 10ⁿ ('1.2 × 10⁶') or words ('1.2 million×'). Use the same string in the stat and the note. Add a fourth stat 'decades apart = log₁₀(ratio)' (e.g. '6.1 decades') since that is exactly what the band height on the log axis shows.

defects.where: drawSide(): leader lines from LX+8 to AX at y=label, and decade labels at x=AX-11 anchor end — zoom of 760 renders shows '1 m', '100 mm', '100 µm', '10 µm', '10 nm' crossed by dashed leaders

Text-over-line collision; the harness only checks text-text overlap.
defects.fix: Put decade labels in a reserved gutter on the opposite side from the items (all items right of the axis, ticks left), or give each tick label a paint-order:stroke halo in var(--panel) and stop leaders 40 px short of the axis in the tick gutter. Draw a faint full-width gridline at each decade so the 'ladder' rungs read as structure.

defects.where: SVG text font-size attributes: DECADES labels font-size 10, item values font-size 10.5 (rendered 10.1 px and 10.6 px at 760 px)
defects.what: Text below the 11 px minimum at the rendered desktop size (and 4–5 px at 360 px).
defects.fix: Use font-size ≥ 11 for values/ticks and 12 for item names, with the responsive viewBox above so they stay ≥ 11 px at every width.

defects.where: the whole SVG: 19 dots + text on a line, ~40 % of the drawing area blank (columns beyond labels, decades 10 mm–1 mm and 1 µm–100 nm empty)
defects.what: Nothing recognisable is drawn — no rack, server, wafer, die, bump array, fin or lattice — so a reader who has never seen these objects gets a re-typeset table, not a schematic; two whole decades are empty although module 21's scale table has rungs for them.

defects.what: Wrong number: a DGX B200 is 10U = 445 mm tall (module 21 table, 'DGX B200 is 10U'); 0.9 m is roughly its depth, not its height.

defects.fix: Use 30 µm for the HBM die (note 'HBM3E; 20–25 µm for HBM4 16-high, Module 15') and note the die as '~26 × 31 mm, 814 mm², Module 19'.

defects.where: nodeEls dots (no cursor, no title, no listeners) — shot hover-first-dot.png identical to previous frame
defects.what: No hover state and no click on the dots or labels; the only way to pick items is two unlabeled-output selects, and each item's `note` string ('EUV max field, 26 × 33 mm', 'interfacial SiO₂ under the high-k' …) is defined but never displayed anywhere.

defects.where: update(): selected dot r=6 in var(--accent) — shots default-die-vs-mp.png and near-pair-reticle-vs-die.png
defects.what: The enlarged selected dot covers neighbouring dots 1–3 px away (H100 die 29 mm hides Reticle field 33 mm), so the reticle's leader appears to start at the highlighted dot and the reader cannot tell which of the two is selected; with reticle vs die both selected, the two merge into one blob.

defects.where: axis: LOG_MAX = 0.4 (2.5 m) with the top tick at '1 m'; stroke 'var(--line2)'

result.redesign:
Keep the vertical log₁₀ axis (it is the right idea) but rebuild the SVG so it is a responsive, illustrated ladder rather than text on a line.

LAYOUT (rebuild on ResizeObserver, viewBox width = container CSS width W so fonts are true pixels): axis at x = 64 (W < 520) or 150 (wider); decade tick labels ('1 m' … '0.1 nm', mono 11 px, var(--muted)) left of the axis at x = axis − 10, anchor end, each with a faint full-width horizontal gridline (var(--line), opacity 0.5) so the decades read as ladder rungs; all items on the RIGHT of the axis: a 24 × 24 pictogram at axis + 20, then the name (sans 12 px 600 var(--ink)) and value (mono 11 px var(--muted)) at axis + 52; horizontal dashed leader from the dot to the icon. Sort items by size, declutter with a 32 px minimum gap, SVG height = items × 32 + 60 (scrolls with the page; never shrink text). Highlight band = full width, behind everything.

ITEMS (fill the empty decades from the module 21 table): NVL72 rack 2 m; HGX baseboard 0.5 m; DGX B200 10U 445 mm; 300 mm wafer; SXM module 140 mm; GPU package 90 mm; reticle field 33 mm; H100 die ~29 mm (814 mm²); HBM stack footprint 11 mm; wafer thickness 775 µm; HBM stack height 720 µm; C4 bump pitch 150 µm; human hair 70 µm; µbump pitch 40 µm; HBM die thickness 30 µm; TSV diameter 7 µm; hybrid bond pitch 6 µm; RDL line/space 2 µm; top BEOL pitch 1.5 µm; RDL CoWoS-R 0.4 µm; CPP 46 nm; Cu mean free path 39 nm; killer particle 25 nm; metal pitch 24 nm; gate length 14 nm; EUV λ 13.5 nm; fin/sheet 6 nm; gate oxide IL 1 nm; Si lattice 0.543 nm; Si–Si bond 0.235 nm; Si atom 0.22 nm. Keep each item's note and show it for the selected A and B.

PICTOGRAMS (24 × 24, stroke var(--ink) 1.2 px, fills from tokens): rack = tall rect with 6 tray lines; HGX board = rect with 2 × 4 small squares; server = wide flat rect with 2 dots; wafer = circle with a notch; SXM/package = square with a centre die square (var(--si)) and 8 small HBM rects around it; reticle/die = plain square / square with corner marks; HBM stack = 4 stacked thin rects (side view); wafer thickness = thin wide slab with a ↕ dimension; hair = wavy thin line; C4 bumps = 3 half-circles under a bar; µbumps = 6 smaller dots under a bar; hybrid bond = two rects meeting with 4 short Cu (var(--cu)) vias crossing the seam; TSV = slab with 3 vertical Cu channels; RDL = 3 parallel Cu lines; top BEOL = 2 thick Cu lines; killer particle = blob bridging two lines; metal pitch = 4 Cu bars with a ↔ between two; CPP / gate length = 2 gate bars with ↔ / 1 bar with ↔; EUV = sine wave (var(--euv)) with λ; fin = thin tall rect on a base; gate oxide = thin line between two blocks; lattice = square cell with corner + centre atoms; bond = two circles joined by a line; atom = one circle.

INTERACTION: every item (dot + icon + label) is a clickable <g> with cursor:pointer and a <title> carrying the note: first click sets A, second sets B (selects stay in sync). Hover: dot grows to r 5 and label underlines. Selected: label + icon in var(--accent), hollow accent ring on the dot, mono 'A' / 'B' tag beside it; if A and B are within 8 px draw a bracket instead of a band.

RATIO VISUAL (the actual teaching moment): under the axis draw a full-width horizontal bar representing the larger item; if ratio ≤ 40 draw that many tick marks (B's laid end to end); otherwise draw one box per decade ('×10 ×10 ×10 … ×3.7') so the reader sees '6 decades and a bit'. Readout stats: larger, smaller, 'larger ÷ smaller' as 2–3 sig figs ('1.2 × 10⁶'), and 'decades apart = log₁₀(ratio)' ('6.1'). Note text: 'About 1.2 million metal pitches (24 nm) laid end to end span one H100 die (29 mm) — 6.1 decades on the ladder.' Same-item → 'Pick two different items.' Fix the formula box to match whichever ratio direction is displayed.

defects.where: site/widgets/deal-grove.js build() — the only drawing is the x(t) chart (gplot, viewBox 0 0 720 300)
defects.what: No schematic of the real thing (QA criterion 1). A first-time viewer sees a thickness-vs-time curve but nothing showing what thermal oxidation physically is: no wafer cross-section, no SiO2 layer, no Si/SiO2 interface where the reaction happens, no oxidant diffusing through the oxide, and no picture of the 0.44x silicon consumed that the 'silicon consumed' readout reports. A, B, B/A and the three fluxes have no visual referent.
defects.fix: Add a wafer cross-section panel that scales with the current result (see redesign): gas ambient on top, SiO2 layer of height proportional to x, dashed 'original Si surface' line, Si substrate below, brackets for 0.56x above / 0.44x consumed, arrows for the gas-transport, diffusion and interface-reaction fluxes with the rate-limiting one highlighted per regime. Keep the chart alongside it.

defects.where: deal-grove-360-dark.png / deal-grove-360-light.png — SVG renders 286 x 119 px; every <text> measures ~5 px tall (10.5-11 unit fonts x 0.40 scale)
defects.what: Chart is illegible at 360 px wide (criterion 5 and 4). Axis ticks, regime labels, 'x = A' and the point label all render at ~4 px; the whole plot is a 119 px tall postage stamp.
defects.fix: Make the SVG layout responsive: observe el's width with ResizeObserver and rebuild with a 'narrow' layout when width < ~480 px (viewBox ~360 x 520, cross-section stacked above the chart, all font-size >= 12 user units so rendered text is >= 11 px, taller plot area, fewer x ticks: 0 / 5 / 10 h). At desktop keep font-size >= 11 units in a 720-wide viewBox.

defects.where: build(): xOfMin() maps log10(minutes) to x; x-axis ticks 1 min..10 h; regime labels at lines 85-86
defects.what: Log time axis makes the 'parabolic' (diffusion-limited, rate falling as 1/x) part of the curve look like it is accelerating upward, which is the opposite of the physics the module teaches. The axis is not labelled as logarithmic and neither axis has a title (only a bare 'nm' at top-left), so a non-expert will read the picture as 'growth speeds up in the parabolic regime'.
defects.fix: Default to a linear time axis (0-10 h, ticks every 2 h) so the square-root flattening is visible and the linear/parabolic distinction is obvious; optionally add a 'log time' checkbox. Add axis titles 'time (h)' and 'oxide thickness (nm)' (or um when max > 1000 nm).

defects.where: build() lines 121-129 (current-point label) and 114-119 (x = A marker); seen in worked-example (101 nm), wet-1000C-1h (390 nm), wet-900C (490 nm), dry-1200C (644 nm), default (58 nm) shots
defects.what: The point label collides with the curve, the horizontal gridline or the dashed 'x = A' crossover line in almost every non-default state: '58 nm' sits on the 68 nm gridline and the curve grazes it; '101 nm', '644 nm' and '490 nm' have the curve running through the digits; '390 nm' and '490 nm' are cut by the crossover line.
defects.fix: Draw the label on a small rect filled var(--panel) (with 3 px padding) so it is always readable, place it on the side of the point away from the curve's direction (above-left when the curve rises to the right and the point is right of centre; below-right when near the top), and nudge it horizontally if its box intersects the crossover line x position.

defects.where: build() lines 85-86 (fixed-position regime labels) and 114-119 (crossover marker); wet-1200C-10h and wet-800C-1min shots
defects.what: Regime labels are pinned to the top-left/top-right corners regardless of where the x = A boundary lies. At 1200 C wet the whole plot is parabolic yet 'linear regime (x << A)' is printed over it with the crossover line slicing through the words; at 800 C wet A = 3664 nm is never reached in 10 h yet 'parabolic regime (x >> A)' is still shown; at 900 C wet (111) the crossover line runs through 'parabolic regime'. The 0.08-opacity shading is nearly invisible in dark theme so the labels are the only cue and they are wrong.
defects.fix: Place each regime label centred inside its own shaded band and omit it when the band is narrower than ~70 px; label the boundary 'x = A (crossover)' on a line below the band labels; raise the band opacity to ~0.15 (or draw a 6 px coloured strip along the top of each band).

defects.where: readout stTau / stRegime and the static w-note; dry-800C-1min shot (25 nm, tau = 17.1 h) and wet-800C-1min shot (0.38 nm)
defects.what: Model behaviour is unexplained (criterion 3 and 7). Dry O2 at 800 C for 1 min reports 25 nm because tau is derived from a 25 nm initial offset, but nothing says so; 'tau (time offset)' is never defined; wet 800 C for 1 min reports 0.38 nm, below the ever-present ~1-2 nm native oxide and inside the range the module says Deal-Grove does not cover (< 20-30 nm), with no warning. The regime readout is a single word with no sentence explaining what limits growth in that state.
defects.fix: Add a one-line dynamic state sentence under the readouts: linear -> 'Reaction-limited: oxidant reaches the interface faster than Si can react; x ~ (B/A)(t+tau)'; parabolic -> 'Diffusion-limited: oxidant must cross <x> nm of oxide; x^2 ~ B t'; mixed -> 'Both terms matter (A x ~ x^2)'. Explain tau in the note ('tau is the time the model pretends it took to grow the ~25 nm that dry O2 forms anomalously fast; it is ~0 for wet'). Show a var(--warn) line when x < 30 nm: 'Below ~30 nm Deal-Grove under-predicts; real thin oxides are grown by RTP/radical methods and calibrated empirically.'

defects.where: readouts stSi, stA, stBA, stThick (ctx.fmt drops trailing zeros); dry-1100C-10min shot ('22 nm' beside '49.9 nm'), '83 nm', '88 nm'; dry-800C shot B/A = '0.002 um/h'
defects.what: Inconsistent precision: values switch between 0 and 1 decimals depending on whether the last digit is zero, and B/A at 800 C is shown as 0.002 um/h (one significant figure). Thicknesses above 1000 nm are printed as '2 807 nm' instead of um.
defects.fix: Format with fixed decimals (Number.toFixed then thin-space grouping) so all thickness readouts share the same precision; show B/A in nm/h when < 0.01 um/h (or use 3 significant figures); switch thickness readouts and the y-axis to um when the value exceeds 1000 nm.

defects.where: build() lines 96-100 (y ticks at xMaxNm * i/4)
defects.what: Y-axis tick values are arbitrary quarters of the max (272 / 204 / 136 / 68; 3 259 / 2 444 / 1 630 / 815), which reads as noise.
defects.fix: Compute 'nice' ticks (1-2-5 x 10^n step chosen so 4-6 ticks fit) and set the axis max to the next nice value above 1.15 x x(10 h).

defects.where: w-readout with 7 w-stat items; worked-example and wet shots
defects.what: The readout grid reflows between a 5+2 and a 4+3 layout whenever the regime text changes to 'mixed (near crossover)', so the stats jump around as the user drags a slider.
defects.fix: Shorten the regime value to 'linear' / 'mixed' / 'parabolic' and move the qualifier into the state sentence; or give the regime w-stat a fixed min-width.

defects.where: gplot SVG — no pointer handling; hover-point shot identical to idle
defects.what: The chart has no hover read-along, so the only way to read thickness at another time is to move the slider; the plotted curve is otherwise inert.
defects.fix: Optional: on pointermove over the plot draw a vertical cursor line and a small panel-filled label showing t and x(t) at that time (keyboard users still have the slider).

result.redesign:
Keep the controls, readouts, formula box and the x(t) maths (params/xOfT are correct). Redraw the SVG as a two-panel figure, responsive to width.

DESKTOP (viewBox 720 x 330): LEFT PANEL (x 0-250) = wafer cross-section, drawn to scale with the current result. Highlight the rate-limiting flux for the current regime in var(--accent) and dim the others to var(--muted): linear -> F3, parabolic -> F2, mixed -> both at half weight. Add a 100 nm scale bar (or 10 nm/1 um chosen from the axis max) so the drawing's scale is explicit.

RIGHT PANEL (x 280-720) = the thickness chart with a LINEAR time axis 0-10 h (ticks every 2 h) titled 'time (h)', y axis titled 'oxide thickness (nm)' (um above 1000 nm) with 1-2-5 nice ticks; the two regime bands shaded at ~0.15 opacity with each label centred inside its own band and suppressed when the band is < 70 px; boundary labelled 'x = A (crossover)'; the current point with a panel-backed label placed away from the curve; a faint dotted reference line x = (B/A)(t+tau) so the viewer can see the curve peel away from the linear law. defects.where: drawStack(): delta labels at x = BX1+16 = 576 and the footnote at y = 186 (harness: 'svg text clipped: −1.5 µm', 'bar length exaggerates…')

defects.where: drawStack(): STAGES proportional rescale (total * s.amt / STAGE_TOTAL)

defects.where: site/widgets/cz-puller.js draw(): yMelt = H*0.58+3 is fixed while meltTop drops with meltFrac (lines 154-160, 170)
defects.what: From mid-body onward the crystal is drawn hanging in mid-air above an emptying crucible: its bottom stays at the crucible rim while the melt surface sinks to the crucible floor (see 760-dark-phase4-body-mid, phase5-tail-start, end-of-run). The core idea of CZ (the crystal grows out of the melt interface) is visually contradicted; at the end the ingot floats over an empty cup with an orange strip at the bottom.
defects.fix: Do what the note already says the machine does: keep the melt surface fixed at the interface and animate crucible lift (crucible+susceptor rise on the crucible shaft as the melt volume shrinks, i.e. draw the crucible floor moving up so the melt column gets shorter but its top stays at the interface). Draw the meniscus / interface as an explicit line where crystal meets melt so they always touch.

defects.where: draw(): canvas has no text at all; legend only names melt / Dash neck / crown-body-tail
defects.what: Nothing in the drawing is labelled in place. Chamber, isolation valve (dashed line), graphite heater (thick yellow frame), susceptor (grey box), quartz crucible (1 px stroke), seed, cable, rotation arrows are all unlabelled anywhere; the heater is painted in the same --warn colour as the melt so it reads as more melt. A first-time viewer cannot tell what the concentric rectangles are. Fails criterion 1 (labelled in place, not legend-only).
defects.fix: Redraw as SVG (see redesign) with leader-line labels for every part: chamber (water-cooled), pull chamber / isolation valve, argon in/out, heat shield, graphite heater, susceptor, quartz crucible, melt, meniscus/interface, seed, Dash neck, crown, body, tail, seed cable, crucible shaft (lift + rotate). Give heater, susceptor, crucible distinct fills (e.g. heater --cu, susceptor --line2 with hatch, crucible --panel2 wall with visible thickness).

defects.where: canvas sizing: maxWidth 230px, cssW = clamp(160..230, el.clientWidth*0.4) (lines 79, 256, 262)
defects.what: At 760 px the drawing is a 200 x 340 px box centred in ~65% empty space; at 360 px it is 160 x 260 px. The ingot is ~35 px wide at full size and the Dash neck (the module's headline concept) renders as a 2.5 x 11 px speck; crown is 3 px tall (verified by zoom on phase2-neck-mid). Fails criterion 2 ('drawing fills its space', 'shapes smaller than their labels').
defects.fix: Use a full-width responsive SVG (viewBox ~ 760 x 420, .w-svg) with the puller cross-section on the left ~60% and a magnified inset of the seed/neck/crown region on the right (scale break) so the neck is drawn at least 6-8 px wide with a diameter callout '3 mm'. Use a non-linear length scale or a 'body compressed' break so neck (150 mm) and crown (40 mm) are each at least 20-30 px tall.

defects.where: diaOf(v) = 306 * (0.8/v)^0.15 and the w-formula line (lines 15, 104)
defects.what: Invented physics: the widget claims steady-state body diameter is a function of pull rate (355 mm at 0.3 mm/min, 279 mm at 1.5 mm/min). Module 02 says diameter is a set point (~305-310 mm) held by ADC; pull rate is chosen for v/G and throughput, and the pull-rate/diameter coupling is only a fast transient correction. Total time also goes to 124 h at 0.3 mm/min, far outside the module's 30-50 h growth.
defects.fix: Hold diameter at 306 mm regardless of pull rate. Let the slider change what really changes: body growth time (2000 mm / v), throughput, and optionally the v/G regime (vacancy-rich vs interstitial-rich, Voronkov ~1.3-2e-3 cm^2/(min K)) as a readout. Restrict range to the module's 0.5-1.5 mm/min (or 0.5-1.0 for 300 mm) and replace the formula box with real ones: body time = L / v; crucible lift = v (r_crystal/r_melt)^2 (rho_s/rho_l); mass = rho_s * pi r^2 L.

defects.where: massSoFarKg vs CHARGE_KG at low pull rate (shot 760-dark-pullrate-min-0.3-tail-start)
defects.what: At v = 0.3 the 355 mm x 2 m body alone weighs ~461 kg > 400 kg charge: readout shows '0 kg melt remaining', the crucible is drawn completely empty, and the crystal keeps growing another 150 mm of tail from nothing. Mass conservation broken for v < ~0.48 mm/min. At v = 1.5 the run ends with 107 kg (27%) left, vs the module's 5-10%.
defects.fix: Fixing diameter to 306 mm removes the overflow (343 kg body + ~15 kg crown/tail leaves ~40 kg, matching the module's worked example). Additionally start the tail when remaining melt reaches a fixed ~8% of charge rather than at a fixed body length, so the residual is always sane.

defects.where: Phase 1 'Charge & meltdown' (progressAt / draw seed logic, lines 23-24, 191-193)
defects.what: For the first 9 sim-hours (~6.4 s of real time at default speed, longer than the standard's 3-6 s play window) the only motion is the seed square sliding down through an already fully liquid melt; no charging, no chunk melting, no slumping. The first frame (and the reduced-motion first frame) is an empty chamber with a speck. Fails criterion 2.
defects.fix: Start the animation mid-body (e.g. simH at 40% of body) so the first frame shows neck+crown+body in the melt; or make phase 1 short (1-2 s) and draw it: chunk polygons in the crucible that turn into liquid as heater colour ramps up, then seed dip at the end of the phase. Show 'meltdown 6-10 h' as a label rather than animating it in real proportion.

defects.where: legend row 4 (lines 88): h('span', {class:'w-legend-item'}, '↺ seed ', seedRpmSpan, ' rpm  ·  ↻ crucible ', crucRpmSpan, ' rpm (counter-rotating)')
defects.what: At 360 px the inline-flex legend item breaks into separate flex children on different baselines: '↺ / seed' stacked, '15' alone, 'rpm · ↻ / crucible' stacked, '10', 'rpm (counter-/rotating)' — unreadable (verified in 360-dark and 360-light zoom).
defects.fix: Put the whole sentence in one text node / single inner span (rebuild textContent on update) so it wraps as normal prose, or label the rotation arrows directly on the drawing ('seed 15 rpm', 'crucible 10 rpm') and drop this legend row.

defects.where: light theme rendering (760-light-*, 360-light)
defects.what: Chamber outline (line2 1.5 px) and valve dashed line (line) are nearly invisible on the light ground; the quartz crucible stroke (--si 1.2 px) cannot be distinguished from the susceptor fill; the empty part of the crucible is filled with susceptor grey so the crucible reads as a solid slab with the crystal standing on it (see light-phase5-tail-start, light-pullrate-min-0.3-tail-start).

defects.where: phase dots (.w-step-dot buttons) and phase card (lines 99-101)
defects.what: No visible hover state or tooltip on the dots (hover-dot3 shot is identical to idle), no Prev/Next buttons, and the nav row has no step counter — the count only appears in the title text. Criterion 6.

defects.where: tick() always re-schedules requestAnimationFrame and re-allocates canvas.width every frame (lines 129, 241-242)
defects.what: The rAF loop never stops: while paused, after the run ends, or when the IntersectionObserver reports not visible, the widget still redraws at 60 fps and reallocates the canvas backing store each frame. Spec rule 5 says stop the loop when paused/not visible.
defects.fix: Only call requestAnimationFrame while st.playing && visible; cancel the loop on pause/end and restart it from the Play handler and the IO callback. Only resize the canvas when cssW/cssH or dpr actually change.

defects.where: crucible rotation slider (lines 72, 248) and readouts
defects.what: The rotation slider changes nothing except the legend text and arrow speed; the note promises it is an oxygen lever but there is no oxygen readout, so the control feels dead. Elapsed time is floor(hours) with no minutes ('0 h' for the whole first hour).

defects.where: crystal proportions in draw(): maxBodyPx = W*0.16, trackPx ~ 176 px for 2340 mm
defects.what: Finished ingot is drawn ~4.9:1 length:width; a real 2.34 m x 306 mm ingot is ~7.6:1, and the crown is a straight cone rather than the shallow shoulder described in the module.

result.redesign:
Replace the 230 px canvas with a full-width SVG cross-section (viewBox about 760x440, class w-svg, sans labels >= 12 px, mono for numbers) laid out as two panes.

LEFT PANE (~62% width) - the puller, drawn to rough scale. From outside in: (1) double-walled chamber rectangle with a visible wall band, labelled 'water-cooled steel chamber'; a horizontal dashed line with a small gate symbol labelled 'isolation valve' separating 'pull chamber' (top) from 'furnace chamber' (bottom); small arrows 'argon in' at the top (purge tube around the crystal) and 'argon + SiO out' at the bottom. (2) Hot zone: a U-shaped graphite heater drawn as a thick meander/hatched band in --cu labelled 'graphite heater, ~150 kW, 1,500-1,600 °C', a carbon-felt insulation band outside it, and a conical heat shield hanging above the melt around the crystal labelled 'heat shield'. (3) A bowl-shaped fused-silica crucible with visible wall thickness (fill panel2, stroke si) labelled 'quartz crucible (32-36 in)', sitting inside a 'graphite susceptor' (line2 fill, hatched) that carries the load; a vertical 'crucible shaft' below it with arrows 'lift + rotate 5-15 rpm'. (4) Melt: gradient warn->bad, label 'Si melt 1,420 °C'. Its top surface stays fixed at the interface; as the run proceeds the crucible+susceptor rise (crucible floor moves up) so the melt column visibly shortens — label the movement 'crucible lift keeps melt surface at the heater'. (5) Crystal grown from the interface upward: seed holder + 'seed cable (rotates 10-20 rpm)' from the top, seed, Dash neck in accent2, crown, body in --si with four faint habit lines, tail cone at the end; a bright short 'meniscus' line where crystal meets melt, labelled once. Body drawn ~0.35 of crucible inner diameter; length proportional but with a scale-break so the whole 2.3 m fits. Labels with leader lines placed in the left/right margins of the pane, never over shapes. Heater/susceptor/crucible/melt/crystal must be five distinct colours.

RIGHT PANE (~38%) - a magnified inset 'seed end, 10x' showing the seed (10-20 mm), the 3 mm Dash neck (drawn >= 8 px wide, callout '3 mm × 150 mm, pulled 3-6 mm/min') with tiny dislocation lines gliding out to the surface, and the crown flaring to 306 mm (callout). Below the inset a small time bar showing the five phases as proportional segments (meltdown 6-10 h | neck ~0.6 h | crown ~1 h | body ~42 h | tail ~2 h) with a moving cursor.

ANIMATION: start at ~40% of the body so the first frame already shows neck, crown, body in the melt with the crucible partly lifted; phase 1 should be short and show chunks becoming liquid; during body growth the crystal rises, the crucible rises, the melt column shortens, and rotation arrows spin. Controls: Play/Pause, phase dots with tooltips plus Prev/Next and a 'Phase n / 5' counter, pull-rate slider 0.5-1.5 mm/min affecting time only (diameter fixed 306 mm), crucible rotation slider mapped to an indicative oxygen readout. Readouts: elapsed h:mm, ingot length, mass grown, melt remaining (never below ~30-40 kg at default), crucible lift so far. Formula box: body time = L/v; lift rate = v (r_c/r_m)^2 (ρs/ρl); mass = ρs π r² L; neck stress = mg/(π r²) ≈ 400 MPa at 300 kg.

defects.where: site/widgets/ald-cycle.js paintChamber (lines 32-66)
defects.what: The schematic does not teach. The 'chamber' is an empty 472x192 rectangle with a grey bar and eight identical lollipops; the upper ~60% of the SVG is blank in every state (see ald-cycle-760-dark.png, -play-6s, -purge-end). Nothing of a real ALD reactor is drawn or labelled: no gas inlets/valves for TMA, H2O, N2, no showerhead, no wafer, no heated chuck, no pump port. No film ever accumulates on the substrate: after 2 cycles the drawing is pixel-identical to cycle 0 except dot colour, while the readout says 0.22 nm.
defects.fix: Redraw as a labelled single-wafer reactor cross-section with a growing film stack and a zoomed surface inset (see redesign).

defects.where: applyStep (24-28) + paintChamber animation branch (47-59)
defects.what: Animation causality is backwards: applyStep flips every site to its post-reaction state before the pulse animation starts, so in anim-tma-p0.15.png the TMA molecules are still 100 px above sites that are already labelled CH3, and in anim-h2o-p0.15.png H2O falls onto sites already labelled OH. The learner sees the product before the reactant lands.
defects.fix: Derive termination from step index for the static state, and during a pulse flip each site (colour + label) at the instant its molecule reaches y~120 (p~0.55); draw the byproduct rising from that moment.

defects.where: mount(): renderAll()/schedule() at 177-179; playAnim() at 68-74
defects.what: First frame is empty and the first step is never animated: playAnim() is not called on mount, so for the first 1.5 s (whole first TMA step) there are no molecules (anim-t0.15s.png). Under prefers-reduced-motion (the harness default and any user with that setting) paintChamber(1) paints the end state, where the CH4 puffs are at opacity 0, so no pulse is ever depicted in any of the 4 steps.
defects.fix: Call playAnim() after the initial renderAll; under reduced motion paint a static mid-pulse composite (p~0.35: molecules in flight, half the sites reacted) instead of p=1.

defects.where: chamber viewBox 0 0 480 200, doseChart viewBox 0 0 400 150; font-size 9-13
defects.what: At 360 px every SVG label is illegible: measured rendered heights 5.7 px (CH3/OH), 7.7 px (chamber title), 6.5 px ('substrate surface'), ~7 px chart ticks (ald-cycle-360-dark/light.png). The dose slider track collapses to 27 px wide because the label 'Precursor dose (x saturation)' eats the .w-ctl grid.
defects.fix: Use font sizes >= 12 in viewBox units with a viewBox no wider than ~480, and at container width < 480 px switch to a compact viewBox (e.g. 360x300) with 5 sites; put the dose control's label on its own line or shorten it to 'Dose' so the slider keeps >= 150 px.

defects.where: goto() 87-93, prevBtn handler 94, applyStep 24-28
defects.what: Prev leaves the surface in the wrong termination for the step: Prev from H2O pulse to 'Purge (after TMA)' shows OH sites (anim-prev-to-purge1.png); Prev from TMA to 'Purge (after H2O)' shows CH3 sites (anim-prev-to-purge2.png). Cycle counter increments on Next across 4->1 but never decrements on Prev across 1->4, so toggling Prev/Next inflates 'film thickness so far'.
defects.fix: termination = step < 2 ? capped : OH, computed from the index; cycles = max(0, cycles-1) when Prev wraps 1->4.

defects.where: STEPS array (6-11), legend (116-119), chamber title (38)
defects.what: The Film selector only swaps the GPC number. With HfO2 (TEMAH + H2O) selected, the chamber still says 'TMA pulse - Al(CH3)3', the step titles/captions still describe TMA and -CH3, and the legend still says '-CH3 capped site' and 'CH4 byproduct' (film-hfo2.png). For TEMAH the ligand is -N(Et)Me and the byproduct is HN(Et)Me.
defects.fix: Parameterise STEPS/legend by film: {precursor: 'Al(CH3)3 (TMA)'|'Hf[N(Et)Me]4 (TEMAH)', ligand: '-CH3'|'-NEtMe', byproduct: 'CH4'|'HNEtMe'} and rebuild labels on change.

defects.where: colours: TMA var(--accent), CH4 var(--warn), H2O var(--si), OH site var(--si)
defects.what: Different species share indistinguishable colours: --accent (#F2B13B) vs --warn (#F0B429) makes TMA and CH4 the same amber (anim-tma-p0.45.png), and H2O molecules use --si, identical to the -OH site they land on (anim-h2o-p0.15.png).
defects.fix: Give each species its own token: e.g. TMA/TEMAH = --accent2 (violet), Al/Hf atom = --cu, -OH site = --ok, H2O = --si, byproduct = --muted, N2 purge = --line2; keep the legend in sync.

defects.where: cycleTimeSlider (102), formula (115), w-note (176)
defects.what: Cycle-time slider is 1-3 s (default 2 s) but Module 06 says a single-wafer cycle is 2-10 s and its worked example is 0.3 s + 3 s + 0.2 s + 4 s = 7.5 s/cycle (150 s for 20 cycles). The note's claim that 'the slider models the 1-3 s/cycle regime used in the module's throughput example' is false. The formula row cites 'time = cycles x (pulse + purge + pulse + purge)' but no pulse/purge terms exist anywhere in the UI.
defects.fix: Replace with four inputs (TMA pulse 0.3 s, purge 3 s, H2O pulse 0.2 s, purge 4 s) whose sum drives the time readout (default 20 cycles -> 150 s), or a 2-10 s slider defaulting to 7.5 s; rewrite the note to cite the module's numbers.

defects.where: paintChamber purge branch (60-65)
defects.what: The purge step is a lone 26 px grey arrow crossing an empty box with the caption 'sweeping out excess precursor / byproduct'. Nothing is being swept, there is no inlet the gas comes from and no pump it goes to (anim-purge-p0.4.png, purge-end.png).
defects.fix: Leave 2-3 unreacted precursor + byproduct dots floating after each pulse, then stream N2 dots from the inlet across to a drawn 'to pump' port, carrying those dots out so the chamber is visibly clean by the end of the purge.

defects.where: doseChart (124-145) and doseSlider
defects.what: The 'self-limitation' chart has no y-axis values (only 'GPC (nm)'), no readout of GPC at the current dose, switching film changes nothing visible because the curve is normalised, and the dose slider has zero effect on the chamber drawing, so the actual mechanism (extra precursor bouncing off a saturated surface) is never shown.

result.redesign:
Replace the empty rectangle with a two-part drawing (viewBox ~480x330 at desktop; compact 360x330 with 5 sites below ~480 px container width, chosen via ResizeObserver or matchMedia; all text >= 12 viewBox units).

TOP HALF - single-wafer thermal ALD reactor, cross-section, parts drawn and labelled in place: (1) a lid with a perforated SHOWERHEAD plate across the top centre (label 'showerhead'); (2) three inlet valves along the top-left feeding the showerhead, each a small box with a label - 'TMA' (or 'TEMAH' for HfO2), 'H2O', 'N2 purge' - the active valve highlighted in its species colour with short flow lines into the showerhead, the others dimmed; (3) a WAFER (thin flat slab, label 'wafer') sitting on a HEATED CHUCK (thicker slab with a few zig-zag heater lines, label 'heater 150-300 C'); (4) a PUMP PORT at the bottom right with an arrow and label 'to pump'; (5) on top of the wafer a FILM STACK that visibly thickens: each completed cycle adds one thin stripe (alternating tints of --accent2/--si) with a dimension bracket at the right reading 'N x 0.11 nm = x.xx nm', and a small scale note 'monolayer ~0.3 nm ~ 3 cycles'. The chamber interior is where the animation happens: during a pulse, molecules (drawn as labelled circles in that species' colour) stream out of the showerhead down toward the surface; during purge, N2 dots (--line2) stream from the N2 valve through the showerhead across the chamber and out the pump port, carrying the leftover precursor/byproduct dots with them.

BOTTOM HALF - 'surface, zoomed in' inset (a dashed callout from a small region of the wafer top): 6-8 surface sites drawn as chemistry, not lollipops. Start: an O atom on the substrate with an -OH group (--ok). TMA pulse: a TMA molecule (Al centre --cu with three small CH3 circles --accent2) descends; on contact the site becomes O-Al(CH3)2 (Al circle labelled 'Al' bonded to the O, two CH3 circles above) and a CH4 puff (--muted, label 'CH4') rises and drifts toward the pump port. Extra TMA molecules beyond the site count (dose > 1) hit capped sites and bounce back up with a small 'no -OH left' tag - this is the self-limiting demo, tied to the dose slider. Purge: N2 dots sweep left-to-right carrying the CH4 puffs and any unreacted TMA out. H2O pulse: H2O molecules (--si, label 'H2O') descend, each -CH3 becomes -OH (--ok) with another CH4 puff rising. Purge again. Cycle counter increments and one film stripe is added on the wafer in the top half at the end of step 4.

STATE RULES: surface termination is a pure function of the step index (steps 1-2 capped, steps 3-4 hydroxylated); during a pulse each site flips at the moment its molecule arrives (p~0.55), never before. Prev decrements the cycle counter when wrapping 1->4. First frame: mount already playing mid-TMA-pulse (or, under reduced motion, a static composite at p~0.35 with molecules in flight and half the sites reacted); call playAnim() on mount.

LABELS/COLOURS: every species gets a distinct token and appears in the legend AND in place: TMA/TEMAH --accent2, Al/Hf atom --cu, -OH --ok, H2O --si, byproduct (CH4 / HNEtMe) --muted, N2 --line2, film stripes alternating --accent2/--si tints. Film selector must swap precursor name, ligand name, byproduct name in the chamber title, step captions, and legend.

CONTROLS/NUMBERS: replace the 1-3 s cycle-time slider with the module's four timing terms (TMA pulse 0.3 s, purge 3 s, H2O pulse 0.2 s, purge 4 s -> 7.5 s/cycle, 20 cycles -> 150 s) so the formula 'time = N x (pulse + purge + pulse + purge)' matches what is on screen; default target 2 nm. Dose chart: y ticks 0/0.05/0.10 nm, a readout 'GPC = 0.11 nm at 1.0x dose', film name on the curve, and the slider drives the number of extra/bouncing molecules in the pulse animation. Fix the step-description min-height so the drawing does not jump between steps.

defects.where: site/widgets/sadp.js buildSteps() SAQP branch (steps 'Spacer 2 ALD', 'Spacer 2 etch-back', 'Mandrel 2 pull'); shots sadp-760-*-saqp-s6/s7/s8
defects.what: SAQP geometry is physically wrong and self-inconsistent. Mandrel 1 and spacer 1 are both P/4 (20 nm), so mandrel 2 is 20 nm wide on a 40 nm pitch with a 20 nm gap; spacer 2 at P/8 = 10 nm on both sides fills that gap completely. Steps 6-7 therefore render as one solid purple slab with no space between spacer pairs, and the spacer-2 centres are at c±15 (intra-pair 30 nm, inter-pair 10 nm), yet step 8 regenerates uniformly spaced spacers with centersAtPitch(P/4) — the lines teleport to positions that do not follow from step 7. The step-3 text in SAQP mode also still says spacer 1 thickness is 'the desired final line width' (20 nm) although the SAQP final line is 10 nm.
defects.fix: Derive every step's rectangles from the real stack, never from centersAtPitch on the result. For SAQP use mandrel-1 width = 3P/8, spacer-1 thickness = P/8, spacer-2 thickness = P/8 (uniform final pitch P/4 with P/8 lines: spacer-2 centres at c±(P/8+P/16) give equal 20 nm spacing). For SADP keep mandrel = spacer = P/4. Compute positions once per step from the previous step's features so mandrel pull removes shapes in place, and fix the SAQP step-3 sentence ('thickness P/8 = 10 nm, the final SAQP line width').

defects.where: draw(): 'wrap' kind, step 3 'Conformal spacer ALD' (shots *-sadp-s3-spacer-ald, *-saqp-s6-*)
defects.what: The 'conformal' spacer is drawn only around the mandrel (top + sidewalls); the floor between mandrels is bare hard mask. The very next step says the etch 'strips the spacer from ... the floor', which the viewer never saw coated. A non-expert cannot understand why an anisotropic etch-back is needed.
defects.fix: Draw the ALD film as one continuous path following the topography: floor, up each sidewall, across each mandrel top, with the same thickness everywhere (round the outer corners slightly). Step 4 then visibly removes only the horizontal parts, leaving the sidewall fillets.

defects.where: draw(): 'transfer' kind, step 'Pattern transfer etch' (shots *-sadp-s6-transfer, *-saqp-s9-transfer)
defects.what: Frame is ~80% empty: the whole feature band (viewBox y 34-182) is blank except a small dimension bar; the etched lines are 14 px stubs with 7 px spacer caps (shapes smaller than their labels). The caption says 'the target film is etched' but only the hard mask is patterned and nothing is etched into the film below.

defects.where: drawCut() and step 'Cut mask' (shots *-s7-cut-mask, *-saqp-s10-cut-mask)

The description's whole point (spacers form closed loops around mandrel ends, so line-ends must be cut) is invisible: five straight parallel bars, no loop ends. Footer 'line-ends created without a second full patterning pass' contradicts the table, which counts the cut as an exposure (SADP = 2 exposures), and the module, which says cuts at 40 nm pitch need LELE/LELELE.
defects.fix: Draw 3 spacer loops in plan view (two long bars joined by rounded ends where each mandrel ended, faded mandrel ghost inside), place dashed red cut boxes over the loop ends and one mid-line cut, label 'loop end — spacer wraps around the mandrel' and 'cut mask (a 2nd litho exposure) removes these'. Make the orientation text match the drawing and use the final pitch to space the bars.

defects.where: draw(): pitch window total = 3*P (renderAll calls draw(step, 3*st.P)); shots *-s3-P160-max vs *-s3-P60-min
defects.what: The Litho pitch slider has no visual effect: the window is always 3 pitches wide so the drawing at P = 60, 80, 160 nm is pixel-identical; only text changes. The main control does not teach anything visually.
defects.fix: Use a fixed nm-to-px scale (e.g. 400 nm window at 760 px) so P visibly changes line count and width: 5 mandrels at 80 nm, 2-3 at 160 nm, ~7 at 60 nm. Also add a mandrel-width and spacer-thickness dimension so the P/4 and P/8 relationships are seen, not just read.

defects.where: draw(): only 'substrate' is labelled in the SVG; resist, mandrel, spacer, hard mask appear only in the .w-legend

defects.where: draw(): svg text font-size 10.5 (substrate, pitch label), viewBox 640 wide; shots sadp-360-dark/light

result.redesign: Rewrite draw() as a real cross-section rendered in CSS pixels (ResizeObserver sets viewBox `0 0 W 300`, W = container width; fonts 12–13 px; fixed nm→px scale ≈ W/400 so the P slider visibly changes feature count and width). Layout, bottom-up: (1) target film band ~50 px, labelled 'target film (low-k / Si)'; (2) hard mask ~16 px, labelled 'hard mask (TiN)'; (3) in step 1 a continuous mandrel film (a-C) ~60 px with resist lines on top at pitch P and width P/2, with '193i exposure' down-arrows and a P dimension bar drawn ~12 px above the resist; (4) step 2: mandrel film etched into lines, resist gone, mandrel width dimension 'P/4 = 20 nm (etch trim)'; (5) step 3: ONE continuous conformal SiN path over floor, sidewalls and tops, thickness t = P/4 with a 't = 20 nm' dimension and 'ALD precursor' arrows from all sides; (6) step 4: only sidewall fillets remain, 'anisotropic etch' ion arrows straight down; (7) step 5: mandrel removed in place (faded dashed ghost), free-standing spacers; dimension 'P/2 = 40 nm pitch' and two space labels 'space A (mandrel CD)' / 'space B (P − m − 2t)'; (8) SAQP steps 6–8 with mandrel-1 = 3P/8, spacer-1 = P/8, spacer-2 = P/8 so spacer pairs have visible gaps and mandrel-2 pull leaves lines at exactly P/4 in the positions they already occupied; (9) transfer: spacer stubs on hard-mask lines with trenches etched down into the target film, etch arrows, 'final pitch' dimension; every material named in place with a leader line (legend rebuilt per step). Cut step: plan view of 3 spacer loops (two parallel bars joined by rounded ends around a faded mandrel ghost) at the final pitch, dashed red cut boxes over each loop end plus one mid-line cut, labels 'loop end — the spacer wraps around the mandrel' and 'cut mask (a 2nd litho exposure) removes these'; header text must match the drawn orientation. Add a .w-formula ('final pitch = P/2ⁿ, line width = ALD thickness t = P/2ⁿ⁺¹') and a 'final line width' stat; clamp the slider to 76–160 nm; disable Prev/Next at the ends and give dots title tooltips.

defects.where: site/widgets/euv-stochastics.js lines 60-120 (3x3 canvas grid) - all shots, both themes
defects.what: The main drawing does not teach. It is nine identical 60x60 uniform Poisson-noise textures with a faint 1-px circle drawn on top. Photons are spread evenly over the whole patch instead of being concentrated in the hole by the aerial image, so nothing looks like a contact-hole exposure; there is no resist, no hole, no photon labelled in place (only a heading above the grid); a 'failed' hole looks identical to a passing one apart from a red border; the circle is nearly invisible at CD 15 nm and in light theme at high dose. The grid is capped at 330 px so the right half of the widget is empty at 760 px.
defects.fix: Redraw per the redesign: one large labelled patch with an aerial-image-weighted photon map, a blurred/thresholded developed outline that visibly closes when the hole fails, in-place labels (target CD circle, developed edge, resist), plus a small strip of extra samples. Fill the width.

defects.where: defaults st = {dose:30, cd:30, absorb:18, thresh:15}; chart yProb floor 1e-12 - base 760/360 shots
defects.what: First frame is uninformative: defaults give P(fail)=1.1e-14, so the red 'stochastic cliff' curve is flat on the 1e-12 floor from ~26 to 80 mJ/cm2 and the batch shows 0/9 failed. The lesson (failures rise exponentially as dose drops) is not visible until the user finds an extreme. The module's worked example uses the 16x16 nm edge pixel (~750 photons at 30 mJ/cm2), not the whole hole (2590).
defects.fix: Model the count that decides the edge (photons in the outer ~3 nm annulus or a 16x16 nm edge pixel, N~750 at defaults, matching the module) and pick defaults so the current-dose marker sits on the slope with P(30 mJ/cm2) ~1e-6..1e-9 and P(10 mJ/cm2) ~1e-2; e.g. CD 20 nm, absorption 14 % as in the module-example shot, which already shows a full-range curve.

defects.where: stWph readout and wphLine: REF_WPH*REF_DOSE/d - dose-min-10 and worst-case shots
defects.what: Throughput readout '480 wph' at 10 mJ/cm2 is impossible; the module says the relation is not linear because of fixed per-wafer overhead and the fastest tool (NXE:3800E) reaches ~220 wph. The dashed curve climbs to 480 at the left edge.
defects.fix: Use an overhead-limited model 1/wph = 1/wph_max + k*dose, calibrated to 160 wph at 30 mJ/cm2 with wph_max ~230 (gives ~215 at 10, ~100 at 60, ~80 at 80); label the legend 'source-limited + fixed overhead'.

defects.where: chart text '160 wph @ 30 mJ/cm2' at fixed (xOf(30)+6, yWph(160)-6) - cd-min-15, absorb-min-5, module-example shots, both themes
defects.what: The red failure curve passes straight through the fixed '160 wph @ 30 mJ/cm2' label whenever P(fail) is in the 1e-6..1e-9 band at 30-50 mJ/cm2; text collides with a chart line.
defects.fix: Move the reference annotation out of the plot area (into the legend: 'reference: 160 wph @ 30 mJ/cm2', or a small caption below the x-axis) or place it at bottom-right of the plot where neither curve can pass; do not leave a fixed label inside a region the curves move through.

defects.where: chart svg viewBox 340x200 with font-size 9.5 (y ticks, wph ticks) and 10 (x ticks, wph label) - 360-dark/light shots; harness tinyText x11
defects.what: At 360 px the chart is ~285 px wide (scale 0.84) so tick labels render at ~8 px and the wph annotation at ~8.4 px: blurry and illegible (confirmed by zoom). The harness flags 11 tiny-text items.

At 760 the same 340-unit viewBox stretches 2.1x, making tick text ~20 px and the chart oversized; consider viewBox 560x260 with 12-13 px text so it looks proportionate at both widths.

defects.where: paint(): strokeStyle = t.ink, lineWidth 1, alpha = min(1, c/5) - light dose-max-80, absorb-max-40, best-case, cd-min-15 shots

The alpha mapping saturates so every patch turns solid purple at high dose and 'brightness' no longer shows counts.

defects.where: stFail readout: pfail < 1e-4 ? pfail.toExponential(1) - best-case, thresh-max-30, dose-max-80, absorb-max-40 shots
defects.what: Readout prints '0.0e+0', '6.4e-53', '5.8e-36', '2.7e-30' - meaningless precision far below the chart floor and below anything the model can claim.

defects.where: h5 heading '60 x 60 nm resist patches ... brightness = photons landed there' - light shots
defects.what: In light theme more photons make a pixel darker/more saturated, so 'brightness = photons landed there' is backwards.
defects.fix: Reword to 'colour intensity = photons absorbed there', or paint the patches on a fixed dark ground in both themes.

defects.where: w-formula string line 47-49 and readout labels lines 53-55
defects.what: Formula names the per-hole total 'N_absorbed = N_incident x absorption x pi(CD/2)^2' while the readouts use 'absorbed photons / nm2' for N_incident x absorption and 'N' for the hole total; f in 'P(fail) = Phi(-f*sqrt(N))' is never defined.
defects.fix: Write 'N_abs/nm2 = N_inc x A; N = N_abs x pi(CD/2)^2; sigma = sqrt(N); P(fail) ~ Phi(-f*sqrt(N)), f = failure threshold'.

defects.where: labels[i].textContent = 'sample n - failed' - worst-case shots, both themes
defects.what: The failed label wraps to two lines ('sample 5 -' / 'failed'), making that grid row taller than its neighbours so rows shift when a failure appears.
defects.fix: Use white-space:nowrap with a short badge ('5 - closed') or a fixed-height label; render 'open/closed' inside the patch instead.

defects.where: chart axes - all shots
defects.what: Left axis (failure probability) and right axis (wafers per hour) have tick numbers but no axis title/units; only the legend hints at what 0-500 means.
defects.fix: Add 'P(fail) per hole' above/along the left axis and 'wafers / hour' along the right axis in >=11 px text.

defects.where: caption; grid cells; chart - hover-cell and hover-chart shots
defects.what: Nothing responds to hover (samples, chart) and the caption states what to notice but not what to do.
defects.fix: Caption: 'Drag dose and CD; watch N and the failure curve.' On hover, a sample shows its own N and deviation from the mean; the chart marker could show P at the hovered dose.

defects.where: N_SAMPLES = 9 batch and 'failed holes in this batch' counter
defects.what: At any realistic setting P(fail) < 1e-4, so nine samples never fail; the counter reads 0/9 in every shot except the all-min extreme. The sampling therefore teaches nothing about real failure rates.
defects.fix: Add a readout 'expected failures among 10^10 contacts on this layer = P x 10^10' next to the batch counter, and base the batch on the edge-pixel count so occasional failures appear near the cliff (e.g. at 15-20 mJ/cm2).

result.redesign:
Replace the 3x3 anonymous noise grid with a labelled schematic that shows what an EUV contact-hole exposure actually is, and make the chart legible at both widths.

1. Main drawing (full width, ~2:1 aspect, SVG + one canvas), two panels side by side (stack at 360 px):
   a. LEFT - cross-section 'what the light does'. Draw the wafer/underlayer as a bar, a 30 nm resist film on top (label 'resist film, 30 nm CAR - absorbs ~14 % (18 % default slider)'), 6-10 short downward arrows above it labelled '13.5 nm photons, 92 eV each', with more arrows over the hole centre than the edges to show the aerial image (a bell-shaped intensity curve drawn above the film, label 'aerial image'). A horizontal dashed line across the film at the 'clearing threshold' (label 'dose needed to dissolve the resist'). The developed hole drawn as a trapezoidal opening in the film, labelled 'contact hole, CD = 30 nm' with a dimension line. Under it, a note 'a 16 x 16 nm pixel at the edge gets ~750 photons at 30 mJ/cm2 -> sigma = 27 (3.6 %)', the numbers live from the sliders.
   b. RIGHT - plan view 'what the developer sees', one large patch (>= 220 px, 60 x 60 nm, 1 nm/px). Photon counts are Poisson-sampled per pixel with the aerial-image weighting (bright disc of radius CD/2 with a ~3 nm soft edge, dark outside), drawn as dots/intensity on a fixed dark ground in both themes. Blur the count map by the 2-4 nm secondary-electron blur and threshold it at the clearing dose to get the DEVELOPED outline: draw that jagged contour in --ok when it forms a connected opening of at least (1 - f) x target area, in --bad when it is closed or undersized. Overlay the target as a dashed circle labelled 'target CD 30 nm'; label the contour 'developed edge'; put 'N = 2 590 absorbed in hole (edge pixel 750)' in the corner. The failed state must look different: the contour visibly pinches shut or shrinks.
   c. Below: a strip of 6 small samples (same rendering, same outline logic) each marked 'open' / 'closed', with a counter 'closed: 1 / 6' and a Resample button; keep labels on one line.

2. Animation: 'Play' makes photons arrive one by one on the big patch (dots appearing, count rising to the target dose over ~4 s), the developed contour re-thresholded as the count grows so the viewer sees the edge stabilising with dose. Start mid-exposure (~60 % of dose) so the first frame already shows a partly formed hole; start paused under prefers-reduced-motion; stop the rAF loop when off-screen or on cleanup.

3. Model and defaults: base the failure statistic on the edge count (annulus of width ~3 nm or a 16 x 16 nm edge pixel, N_edge ~750 at 30 mJ/cm2, 14 % absorption, CD 30 nm, exactly the module's worked example) so P(fail) at 30 mJ/cm2 lands around 1e-6..1e-9 and the curve spans the plotted 1..1e-12 band. Show in readouts: incident /nm2, absorbed /nm2, N in hole, N in edge pixel, sigma and %, P(fail) (clamped to '< 1e-12'), expected failures among 10^10 contacts, and throughput from an overhead-limited model (1/wph = 1/230 + k*dose, 160 wph at 30).

4. Chart: viewBox ~560 x 260, all text >= 13 viewBox units (>= 11 px at 360), axis titles 'P(fail) per hole' (left) and 'wafers / hour' (right), 'dose (mJ/cm2)' bottom; reference annotation moved to the legend so curves never cross text; current-dose marker on both curves; keep the log grid at 1, 1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9, 1e-12.

5. Text: caption 'Drag dose, CD and absorption; watch how few photons decide the hole edge and how fast the failure curve climbs when dose drops.' Define 'stochastic', 'aerial image' and 'secondary-electron blur' once in the note. Fix the formula naming (N_abs/nm2, N, f = failure threshold).

defects.where: site/widgets/etch-profile.js buildTrench()/cavityPath() and the SVG layout (viewBox 0 0 620 400, substrate rects 270 px wide, no clipPath)
defects.what: Slider extremes push the geometry off the canvas. Ion 100 / radical 100 / passivation 0 / 120 s (shot ion-chem-nopass-120s): both cavities run past the bottom and both sides of the SVG, only a small triangle of substrate is left, and the 'narrow opening, 30 nm' label is overprinted by the cavity outline. Ion 0 / radical 100 / 120 s (chem-only-120s): the isotropic cone extends past x=0 and x=620, the two cavities cut through each other's substrate block, and the masks float over nothing. The model integrates depth with no cap and the lateral undercut is only clamped on the inside (-0.92·w0), never on the outside.
defects.fix: Give the film a finite thickness (e.g. 150 nm) and stop the etch at an etch-stop layer (show 'etch stop reached, over-etch N %'); choose SY so the maximum reachable depth fits the canvas; clamp lateral offset to at most half the distance to the neighbouring trench; wrap each trench group in a <clipPath> equal to its substrate rect so nothing can be drawn outside it.

defects.where: SVG drawing as a whole (buildTrench, render)
defects.what: The schematic does not teach: two dark blobs in a flat blue block. No part is labelled in place (mask, film, substrate, opening, depth, passivation, ions, radicals, undercut, bow, foot, notch are all absent or legend-only); no ions or radicals are drawn so nothing shows WHY one knob makes the wall vertical and another makes it bulge; at the default state the trenches occupy ~25 % of the 370 px-tall block and the remaining two thirds is empty blue; when the mask erodes to 0 (NAND, ion-only, notch shots) the top quarter of the SVG is empty too.
defects.fix: See redesign.

defects.where: cavityPath(): bosch branch
defects.what: Bosch preset shows no scallops. The bosch path uses a constant bulge on every interior point, producing a plain rectangle with chamfered corners, while the note promises 'periodic sidewall scallops'.
defects.fix: Build the wall from N cycles (N = round(depth / cycleDepth), 5–10 cycles), each a semicircular bite: for cycle i draw points along x = w0 + s·sin(π·u) with u in [0,1] over that cycle's depth span, so the wall shows visible ripples of amplitude s (~4–6 nm at the exaggerated x-scale) and the average wall stays vertical.

defects.where: cavityPath(): off = ... + footNm * footShape(t) ...
defects.what: Footing is drawn inverted. footNm ADDS to the lateral offset near the floor, so over-passivation flares the trench wider at the bottom (all-max and pass-max-120s shots show a bell-bottom). Module 09 defines footing as material LEFT at the base (a fillet that narrows the feature).
defects.fix: Subtract the foot term (off -= footNm * footShape(t)) so the cavity narrows into a rounded fillet at the base; keep the notch term positive but give it a rounded shape.

defects.where: render(): mechNote.textContent = regime(P); PRESETS[i].note
defects.what: The per-preset explanations (p.note for Oxide contact, Silicon fin, Wet HF, 3D NAND) are never displayed; only the Bosch note reaches the screen via regime(). The Silicon-fin preset shows the generic 'trench tracks the mask opening closely' while the drawing shows undercut under the mask and A = 0.72. Criterion 7 (each state has a 1–2 sentence explanation) is not met for four of five presets.
defects.fix: In render(), if presetActive() returns a preset, show that preset's note (optionally followed by the regime sentence); otherwise show regime(P).

defects.where: paramsFor(), PRESETS, readout row
defects.what: Readouts contradict the module and the presets' own notes. Oxide contact: AR 1.5:1 (note says ~9:1; module 8–10:1), selectivity 2:1 (module 4–10:1 to carbon, >20:1 SAC), 4.4 keV. 3D NAND: AR 3.1:1 (note says 60–100:1), 11.5 keV. Bosch: 102 nm/min (module 5–30 µm/min, a ×50–300 slip), AR 1.7:1 (module 30–50:1), selectivity 7:1 (module >100:1), A = 0.78. Silicon fin: A = 0.72 (module: >88° sidewall, A ≈ 0.97+), selectivity 6:1 (module >100:1 for HBr/O2). Ion energy at slider max = 20 keV (module: 'several keV' max). All-min (ion 0, radical 0) still reports 20 nm/min and A = 1.
defects.fix: Give each preset its own opening width, film thickness, vertical scale and mask selectivity so depth/opening in the drawing equals the AR the note quotes (e.g. NAND: 100 nm hole, 8 µm deep with a labelled vertical scale bar; Bosch: µm/min and 30:1), or remove the numeric claims from the notes. Use ionEV = 20·250^ion (20 eV–5 keV). Make rate = 0 when both ion and radical are 0 and show A as '–'. Raise the fin/Bosch anisotropy by lowering undercutFrac when pass > 0.5.

defects.where: SVG text elements (font-size 11 and 12 in a 620-wide viewBox)
defects.what: At 360 px the SVG renders ~290 px wide (scale 0.47) so 'narrow opening, 30 nm', 'wide opening, 80 nm' and the 'horizontal scale exaggerated' caption render at ~5–6 px and are illegible (confirmed by 3x zoom of the 360 shot). The harness only checks computed font-size, so it missed it.
defects.fix: Either move these labels into HTML below the drawing, or observe the SVG width with ResizeObserver and set font-size = 12 * (620 / clientWidth) so rendered text stays ≥ 11 px.

defects.where: render(): caption text at y=16 vs mask polygons (top = TOPY − maskRemNm·SY = 10 when mask is intact)
defects.what: When the mask is at full thickness (ion 0: Wet HF, all-min, defaults-time-min) the mask blocks rise to y = 10 and draw straight through the 'horizontal scale exaggerated relative to depth' caption (strike-through visible in wet-hf and all-min shots, both themes).
defects.fix: Reserve a text band: move TOPY down (e.g. 110) or place the caption below the drawing / in an HTML w-note.

defects.where: buildTrench(): mask polygons (outerX = cx ± (mw+100)) and substrate rect (cx ± 135)
defects.what: Mask is drawn as four overlapping tiles: the narrow trench's right tile and the wide trench's left tile overlap so a stray vertical stroke splits the band at x≈257 and x≈307 (visible seam in every shot); the wide trench's right tile extends to x=633 (clipped) and overhangs the substrate, which ends at x=580; nothing is drawn in x<40 or x>580.
defects.fix: Draw the substrate as one full-width rect and the mask as a single path spanning the full width with two openings; drop the per-trench tiles.

defects.where: buildTrench(): mask facet polygon when maskRemNm = 0
defects.what: When the mask is fully eroded the facet point (innerX, top+faceNm) still dips below the surface, leaving small triangular teeth hanging at each trench corner (zoom of the NAND shot).
defects.fix: Skip the mask polygons (or set faceNm = 0) when maskRemNm ≤ 0; clamp faceNm ≤ maskRemNm·SY.

defects.where: cavityPath(): notchShape term
defects.what: The notch renders as a paper-thin horizontal spike ~20 nm long at the floor (ion-only shot), reading as a glitch, and there is no etch-stop layer in the drawing so the stated cause (charging on an exposed insulator) is invisible.
defects.fix: Draw an etch-stop layer under the film and render the notch as a small rounded gouge (bump shape over the last ~10 % of depth, radius ≈ 0.15·w0) at the floor corner, with an in-place 'notch' label when active.

defects.where: cavityPath(): undercutFrac term (linear in depth − d)
defects.what: The isotropic (Wet HF, chem-only) profile is a straight-sided cone; an isotropic etch produces a rounded, roughly quarter-circular undercut of radius ≈ depth under each mask edge.
defects.fix: Use off = undercutFrac · sqrt(max(0, depth² − d²)) so the wall is a circular arc centred at the mask edge.

defects.where: render(): stIonEV for the Wet HF preset
defects.what: The wet etch (no plasma) shows 'approx. ion energy 20 eV'.
defects.fix: Show 'none (wet)' when ion = 0, or hide the stat for wet presets.

defects.where: render(): anisotropy A computed from lateralExtent / rN.depth
defects.what: A changes with etch time at fixed chemistry (0.77 at 5 s, 0.81 at 45 s for the defaults) because bowNm/notchNm are constants divided by a growing depth, while the caption formula defines A from rates.
defects.fix: Compute A from the model's lateral and vertical RATES (A = 1 − r_lat/r_vert) so it is time-independent, and use a separate readout for the geometric bow/notch width.

defects.where: legend + light theme cavity fill (var(--ground))
defects.what: In light theme the etched-away region is near-white and visually merges with the page beyond the SVG when the cavity reaches the canvas edge; and no text ever names 'undercut', 'bowing', 'footing', 'notch', 'facet' on the drawing, so the caption's promise ('watch undercut, bowing, tapering or an etch stop show up') has no visual anchor.
defects.fix: Give the cavity a faint stroke in var(--muted) plus a subtle hatch/tint (e.g. var(--panel)), and add leader-line callouts that appear when each defect term exceeds a threshold.

result.redesign:
Redraw the SVG as a labelled cross-section of a plasma etch, one full-width scene (viewBox about 640×420), with every part named in place:

1. Top band (~70 px): the plasma. Fill with a faint var(--accent2) tint and label 'plasma: radicals (neutral, isotropic) + ions (accelerated across the sheath)'. Draw 6–8 vertical arrows in var(--accent) coming straight down into the two openings — their count/length scale with the Ion energy slider (label 'ions, ~632 eV', live) — and 6–8 short random-direction arrows in var(--accent2) whose count scales with the Radical slider (label 'F / Cl radicals'). A thin horizontal line under the plasma labelled 'sheath (dark space)'.

2. Mask: one continuous layer across the full width (var(--line2)), 40 nm thick, with two openings; label 'hardmask (carbon / SiN) – 23 nm left' at the left end, live thickness; dimension brackets over each opening reading '30 nm' and '80 nm'; facets drawn only while mask remains and labelled 'facet' when ion energy is high.

3. Film + etch stop + substrate: film to be etched (var(--si)), 150 nm thick, labelled 'film (SiO2 / Si)'; below it a 6 nm etch-stop layer (var(--cu) at 0.6 opacity) labelled 'etch stop (SiN / gate oxide)'; below that the substrate (var(--si) at 0.5 opacity) labelled 'substrate'. Size the vertical scale so the full film thickness fills the drawing: the deepest possible etch just reaches the stop, and any further time becomes an 'over-etch N %' readout instead of more depth. Nothing can leave the canvas: clip each trench to its own half.

4.
