result.redesign:
Layout: replace the w-grid2 (SVG | table) with (1) controls, (2) a full-width landscape SVG (viewBox ~ 420x300, fonts >= 13 viewBox units so 360 px still renders >= 11 px), (3) readouts + formula, (4) the JEDEC generation table full-width in its own .table-scroll below. Both grid children (if a grid is kept) get min-width:0.

Cross-section (left ~65% of the SVG), drawn to a vertical scale where the JEDEC ceiling sits at ~85% of the frame height so the stack always fills the drawing:
- Bottom: a wide 'Si interposer (CoWoS)' slab, label inside the slab.
- On the interposer, left: the HBM stack; right: a partial 'GPU die' block (label in place) ~2-4 mm away, with a short double arrow between the base die and the GPU labelled 'PHY <-> PHY, 1,024 / 2,048 wires'. This shows why HBM sits on an interposer next to the GPU.
- Across the top: a flat 'lid / heat spreader' bar resting on the GPU and on the stack top, labelled 'one flat lid must touch GPU and all 8 stacks'. The dashed JEDEC ceiling line is the lid underside (label 'JEDEC 720 um' or '775 um' at the right end of the line, inside the viewBox). When the stack exceeds it, hatch the overrun in var(--bad) and print 'over by N um'.
- Base die: a taller var(--accent2) block labelled in place 'base / logic die (PHY, TSV routing, DA test port)'; beneath it a row of small semicircle microbumps on the interposer labelled 'microbumps ~55 um pitch, ~30 um'.
- Core dies: N var(--si) slabs with a right-hand bracket 'N core DRAM dies x t_die um'. Draw 3-4 continuous copper TSV columns (var(--cu)) that pass straight through every die AND through every bond layer, with a tiny bump circle at each gap, so the vertical wire is visible; leader label 'TSV (Cu, ~5 um dia., thousands per die)'.
- Bond layer rendering must change with the radio choice: TC-NCF = a grey film band (NCF) with bumps embedded, label 'NCF epoxy film + Cu-pillar/SnAg bump ~15 um, bonded one die at a time'; MR-MUF = bumps in a darker EMC fill that also wraps the stack sidewalls as a mold body, label 'EMC molded underfill ~10-12 um, all joints reflowed at once'; Hybrid = thin var(--ok) Cu-Cu line, no bumps, no mold, label 'Cu-Cu hybrid bond ~2 um, no gap'.
- Left dimension bracket for the whole stack: 'N x (t_die + t_gap) + t_base + t_solder = XXX um' in var(--ok) or var(--bad).

Height-budget bar (right ~35% of the SVG): one vertical stacked bar with segments 'silicon N x t_die', 'bond gaps N x t_gap', 'base die', 'bottom solder', each segment labelled with its um value, beside a tick for the JEDEC ceiling and a printed 'free: +X um' or 'over: -X um'. This is the number the widget is really about and it must be readable without squinting at the stack.

Numbers (Module 15 §4.4): t_die 60/50/35/30 um for 4/8/12/16-high; gaps TC-NCF 15, MR-MUF 12 (8-high) / 10 (12- & 16-high), hybrid 2; base 60; solder 30; ceilings 720 (HBM2E/3/3E), 775 (HBM4). Fix the generation-lag bug (st.gen must be set before refreshOptions). Correct the note so the Samsung delay is attributed to heat/warpage, with the height budget explained as the reason dies must be thinned to ~30-35 um.

Interaction: label the radio group 'Bonding method'; keep live values on every control; optionally highlight the hovered layer and show its thickness in a small w-note rather than in the SVG.

defects.where: site/widgets/cowos-flow.js sideView() (steps 3–12)
defects.what: The cross-section does not teach. µbumps, C4 bumps and BGA balls are all drawn as continuous solid bars (µbump bar 190 wide is even wider than the 170-wide interposer; C4 and µbump are identical yellow bars; BGA is an orange slab). The four HBM stacks are unlabeled plain bars in the same colour as the interposer. There is no RDL, no pads, no passivation, no backside RDL, no TIM1, no stiffener ring; the lid is a floating slab that never touches the substrate; the mold compound is a cap painted over the die tops (module says it fills gaps between dies and is ground back so die backs are exposed) and overhangs the interposer (210 vs 170). Step 7 'Backside grind to reveal TSVs' never reveals a TSV: the Cu lines stay buried at 15–85% of the slab, the slab only thins 26→18 px (775→100 µm is an 87% reduction), and the stack never flips face-down as steps 6–7 describe. Step 10 'singulation' is a red dashed rectangle around the whole SVG (including the 'C4 bumps' label) that persists through steps 11–12 and encloses the substrate and BGA balls, which were never on the wafer.
defects.fix: Redraw per the redesign below: discrete bump/ball rows (circles), HBM drawn as stacked slices and labeled, mold only between/around dies flush with die tops, flip the stack at step 6, thin the interposer properly and let TSV tips protrude at step 7, draw kerf lines + saw at step 10 (no whole-SVG box), lid as a hat with stiffener blocks and TIM1 band, every part labeled in place.

defects.where: sideView() T() font-size 10 and waferView() font-size 11 in a 320-wide viewBox
defects.what: At 360 px the SVG renders 286 px wide (scale 0.89): every side-view label measures 8.9 px and both wafer labels 9.8 px — below the 11 px minimum and visibly illegible in cowos-flow-360-dark-step12-lid-last.png. The harness only checked the wafer view at 360 so it missed this.
defects.fix: Size text so that font-size × (286 / viewBoxWidth) ≥ 11 (e.g. viewBox width 400 with 16 px labels, or 320 with 13 px and shorter labels). Keep long descriptions in the step text, use short in-place labels (GPU, HBM ×8, µbumps, Si interposer, TSV, RDL, C4, ABF substrate, BGA, lid, TIM1, mold, underfill).

defects.where: GPU_PRICE = 450, HBM_PRICE = 150, IP_PRICE = 500 and the w-note claiming '(Module 17 economics)'
defects.what: Prices contradict the module: it gives ~$500–600 per GPU die, ~$300–500 per HBM3E stack ($500–700 for 12-high), and a B200 assembly worth ~$5,000–7,000 in parts with TWO GPU dies and eight stacks. The widget shows '$2 150' at risk with N=8 — a third of the module's figure — and models one GPU die while the default N=8 is the two-die Blackwell configuration.
defects.fix: Use GPU ≈ $550, HBM3E ≈ $400, interposer ≈ $450 (CoWoS-S wafer $6–8k ÷ 16), add substrate ≈ $350, and either add a 'GPU dies (G)' control (default 2) or fix G=2 and show it in the formula; default readout should land in the module's ~$5–7k range. Update the note to quote the module's numbers.

defects.where: updateYield(): rRisk.textContent = '(1 in ' + fmt(1 / (1 - p), 0) + ' fails)'
defects.what: Slider extremes break the readout: with every slider at 100% it prints '$1 550 (1 in – fails)' (fmt swallows Infinity), and at all-minimum (P=9%) it prints '(1 in 1 fails)', which reads as 100% failure when 91% fail.
defects.fix: Replace '1 in N' with P(fail) = (1−p) as a percentage plus expected loss per package = (1−p)·$risk, e.g. '$5 450 at risk · 14% fail · $760 expected scrap per package'; guard p=1 explicitly ('0% fail').

defects.where: sideView(): 'interposer, ground to ~100 µm' label, 'epoxy mold compound' label, C4 bar placement
defects.what: Text collides with drawing: from step 7 on the interposer label is painted across the five TSV lines (orange ticks show through the letters, both themes); at step 5+ the mold label's descenders sit on the HBM tops and the semi-opaque mold rect hides the top ~8 px of the HBM stacks; at steps 11–12 the C4 bump bar is drawn over the top of the ABF substrate instead of between interposer and substrate.
defects.fix: Give each layer its own row so nothing is painted over a neighbour; put TSVs in their own band away from the label or move the interposer label to a leader line at the side; place C4 circles in a dedicated row between interposer and substrate.

defects.where: sideView() mold fill 'var(--panel2)', carrier 'var(--line2)', lid label fill 'var(--panel)' on 'var(--muted)' @0.55; legend swatches
defects.what: Mold compound is nearly invisible in both themes (--panel2 is the widget's own background tone) and its legend swatch is a blank square; the carrier legend swatch is likewise near-invisible; in light theme the 'stiffener + lid (TIM1)' label is white text on pale grey (cowos-flow-zoom-light-step12.png).
defects.fix: Draw mold with an outlined rect (stroke var(--line2)) plus a diagonal hatch pattern or --line2 at 0.6 opacity; draw the lid in --muted at full opacity with --ground/--ink text chosen per theme via a tokens() lightness check; give every legend swatch a 1px --line2 border.

defects.where: sideView() die row: n = 4 hard-coded; waferView() 7×7 grid (~37 sites)
defects.what: The drawing contradicts its own numbers: the 'HBM stacks (N)' slider says 8 (or 12) but the cross-section always shows 4 stacks and one GPU; the wafer map shows ~37 sites while step 10 says 'about 16 per wafer' at 3.3× reticle.
defects.fix: Draw N HBM stacks (and G GPU dies) from state, re-rendering the cross-section on slider input; lay the wafer map out as ~16 sites (e.g. 4×4 clipped by the circle with 3.3× reticle rectangles) so it matches the text.

defects.where: waferView() viewBox 320×205 vs sideView() viewBox 320×~60–150
defects.what: The SVG height jumps from ~460 px (steps 1–2) to ~150 px (step 3) and grows again as layers are added, so the legend, yield controls and everything below shift by up to 300 px as the user steps; the side view leaves the drawing tiny in a wide box.
defects.fix: Use one fixed viewBox for all steps (e.g. 0 0 400 260) and draw both the wafer mini-map and the cross-section inside it; reserve the full height from step 1 so nothing reflows.

defects.where: st.gpuY = 0.85 default; 'GPU die KGD' slider
defects.what: A known-good die that has passed wafer sort does not fail 15% of the time; with this default P(package good) = 74.6%, i.e. one in four CoWoS packages scrapped, while the module cites >98% yield for the 5.5× product and uses 95% CoW yield as a pessimistic example.
defects.fix: Default GPU KGD ≈ 98% (test escape 1–3%), assembly ≈ 97%, interposer ≈ 97%, HBM ≈ 99.5%, so the default lands near 85–90%; or relabel the slider 'GPU die yield incl. sort escapes' with a note that KGD test makes it high.

defects.where: sideView() underfill: R(cx - totalW/2 - 4, cy + row.h - 5, totalW + 8, 5, ok, 0.6)
defects.what: Underfill is a 5-px green band drawn over the bottom of the dies (inside the die rectangles) and floating above the bump bar rather than filling the 25–35 µm bump gap; steps 3 and 4 are almost indistinguishable.
defects.fix: Draw underfill as fillets in the bump-gap row: a band the height of the µbump row spanning between/around the bump circles, plus small triangular fillets climbing the die edges.

defects.where: waferView() inset and legend
defects.what: The enlarged-site inset has no in-place labels (Si, TSV, RDL, pads), and its purple RDL band is the same token the legend calls 'GPU die', so the only 'labelling' available actively misleads. Step 2 draws round yellow bumps although the text and module say the interposer gets flat UBM pads (the µbumps are on the dies).
defects.fix: Label Si (775 µm), TSV (10 × 100 µm, blind), RDL (4–5 layers) and UBM pads inside the inset with leader lines; draw pads as flat yellow rectangles; remove the RDL/GPU colour clash (use --line2 hairlines for RDL).

defects.where: dotsWrap buttons (aria-label only)
defects.what: Hovering a step dot shows nothing (cowos-flow-760-dark-hover-dot3.png): no tooltip and no hover style, so the 12 unlabeled dots are not discoverable.
defects.fix: Add title: s.title to each dot (native tooltip) and an inline :hover/focus style (e.g. border-color var(--accent)) via a small style rule in the widget.

defects.where: updateYield(): rProb.textContent = fmt(p * 100, 1) + '%'
defects.what: Precision is inconsistent: '74.6%' at defaults but '9%' and '100%' at extremes because fmt drops trailing zeros.
defects.fix: Use (p*100).toFixed(1) + '%' for the probability readout.

result.redesign:
Keep the 12-step nav, descriptions and yield stack; redraw the SVG as ONE fixed-size scene (viewBox 0 0 400 260, labels ≥ 16 px so they stay ≥ 11 px at 286 px rendered) with two panes that persist across all steps.

LEFT PANE (x 0–110): 'where on the wafer' mini-map — a 300 mm wafer circle tiled with ~16 rectangular 3.3×-reticle sites, one highlighted; at step 10 draw saw kerf lines between sites and a small blade; from step 10 on show only the single cut-out module. Caption '300 mm wafer, ~16 modules'.

RIGHT PANE (x 120–400): the cross-section at exaggerated but ordered thicknesses, drawn bottom-up with every part labeled in place (short label + leader line where the part is thin). Rows, from the bottom at the final step: BGA balls (row of ~9 circles r≈6, label 'SAC305 BGA balls, ~1 mm pitch'); ABF substrate (wide slab with a thicker centre band = glass core and 3 hairlines each side = build-up layers, label 'ABF substrate: core + 10–12 layers/side'); C4 bumps (row of ~11 circles r≈4 in their own row, label 'C4 bumps, 130–180 µm pitch') with underfill fillet around them from step 11; Si interposer (slab; 5 vertical Cu bars = TSVs labeled 'TSV 10×100 µm'; a thin band with 2–3 hairlines on the die-facing side = 'RDL, 4–5 Cu layers'; flat yellow UBM pads on top from step 2); µbumps (row of ~20 tiny circles r≈1.5 under each die, label 'µbumps 40–55 µm'); dies: G GPU dies (G=2 default) and N HBM stacks driven by the yield sliders, HBM drawn as a base die plus 8–12 thin stacked slices so it is recognisable, labeled 'GPU' and 'HBM ×N'; underfill as green fillets filling the bump-gap row and climbing the die edges; mold compound (hatched, outlined) ONLY in the gaps between and around dies, flush with die tops; TIM1 thin band on die backs; lid drawn as a hat (top plate + side walls down to the substrate) with stiffener-ring blocks at the substrate edge, labels 'Cu lid', 'TIM1', 'stiffener ring'.

Per-step animation of that scene: 1 thick interposer (775 µm, TSVs blind in top ~15%, RDL band) · 2 pads appear · 3 dies + µbump rows drop into place (bonder head outline optional) · 4 underfill fillets appear · 5 mold fills between dies (note 'ground back, die backs exposed') · 6 whole stack flips 180° so the interposer backside faces up and a glass carrier appears underneath, annotated 'backside up' · 7 grinding wheel/arrows at the top, interposer thins from ~60 px to ~12 px, Cu TSV tips protrude 2 px proud, label '775 → ~100 µm' · 8 passivation band + backside RDL hairline + C4 circles on the exposed backside · 9 carrier removed, stack flips back dies-up · 10 mini-map kerfs + dashed vertical kerf lines at the module edges only · 11 substrate slides in beneath, C4 circles wet to it, interposer underfill fillet · 12 stiffener blocks, lid hat, TIM1 band, BGA circles. Show a µm scale hint (e.g. 'thicknesses not to scale; interposer 100 µm, dies ~700 µm, substrate ~2–3 mm').

Yield stack: prices from the module (GPU ~$550 ×G, HBM3E ~$400 ×N, interposer ~$450, substrate ~$350 → ~$5–7k), default GPU KGD ~98%, readout 'P(good) · P(fail) · expected scrap $ per package', no '1 in N' text, one-decimal precision; cross-section re-renders when N or G changes.

defects.where: site/widgets/package-xsection.js draw() lines 104-170 (xsec SVG)
defects.what: The cross-section has no in-place labels at all (zero <text> elements). Every layer is an anonymous coloured stripe; the only naming is the button row below the drawing (legend-only labelling). A first-time viewer cannot tell PCB from lid, interposer from HBM, or C4 from microbumps.
defects.fix: Add an SVG label for every row (font-family var(--sans), font-size ~11 in a ~380-wide viewBox so it renders >=11 px at 360 px) placed in a left/right margin with a short leader line to the layer; label repeated dies once ('HBM3E x6', 'GPU die', 'SoIC stack').

defects.where: draw() flat mkRect calls; LIB entries balls/c4/ubump/buildup/lid/tim
defects.what: Parts are drawn as featureless bars, so nothing is recognisable: BGA balls, C4 bumps and microbumps are solid rectangles (and the C4 bar is wider than the die it should sit under); the build-up substrate is a plain block with no core, build-up layers or vias; the lid is a flat bar floating above a TIM strip that is narrower than the die group (cowos-s/-l); underfill (the subject of the CTE note) is never drawn.
defects.fix: Draw balls as a row of circles, C4 and microbumps as rows of small dots confined to the footprint of the part above them, the substrate as a thicker core band with 2-3 thin Cu/ABF lines each side, underfill fillets at die edges, TIM spanning all dies, and the lid as an inverted-U cap whose feet reach the substrate edge.

defects.where: draw() wirebond branch lines 150-162; PKGS qfp stack line 29-30; LIB.mold color var(--panel2)
defects.what: QFP drawing is physically wrong: bond wires start on the die top and arc UP to the top edge of the drawing ending in mid-air (toX,cy is the top of the band, not a leadframe finger); the epoxy mold compound is a near-invisible strip (panel2 on panel) drawn ABOVE the wires instead of encapsulating die+wires; the leadframe is one full-width bar with no die paddle, lead fingers or gull-wing leads.
defects.fix: Draw the leadframe as a die paddle plus separate finger segments at die level that exit the mold and bend down as gull-wing leads onto PCB pads; route wires from die-top pads down to the finger tips; draw the mold as a filled body (e.g. var(--muted) at 0.25 + a hatch) that surrounds die, paddle and wires.

defects.where: PKGS info stack line 33-34; LIB.rdlF wf 0.55, LIB.mold
defects.what: InFO shows no fan-out: the RDL (wf 0.55) is narrower than the ball array (wf 0.86), the mold is an invisible sliver above the die, and no TIVs are drawn although the die label mentions them. CoWoS-L is visually identical to CoWoS-S except the interposer colour; the LSI bridges that define CoWoS-L are absent.
defects.fix: InFO: mold body beside the die at die height, TIV pillars through the mold, RDL as a thin multi-line layer spanning the full package width under die+mold, balls under the whole RDL width. CoWoS-L: embed two small labelled 'LSI bridge' rectangles under the GPU-HBM edges and draw TIV pillars through the RDL.

defects.where: mkRect stroke 'var(--panel)' line 126; select() lines 176-178
defects.what: Selection/hover highlight on the drawing is invisible: the highlighted stroke (width 2.2) is var(--panel), the same colour as the widget background (.widget{background:var(--panel)}), so hovering a rect or clicking a button only erodes the rect edge slightly. Verified in cowos-s-hover-interposer-rect and fcbga-click-balls shots.
defects.fix: Outline the selected element with stroke var(--accent) width 2 (and/or raise its fill-opacity while dimming the others), keep var(--line) as the resting separator stroke.

defects.where: CTE calculator inputs lines 70-72
defects.what: Defaults do not reproduce the module's worked example: inD defaults to 15 mm (the half-side of a 30 mm die, though labelled 'half-diagonal'; module uses DNP = 21.2 mm) and inDT has value 192 with step 5, which Chrome snaps to 190 K in every render. Widget shows 35.3 um / 50 % while Module 16 states ~50 um / ~70 %.
defects.fix: inD: min 5, max 30, step 0.1, value 21.2, label 'Distance to neutral point d (half-diagonal)'; inDT: step 1, value 192. Then delta = 50.5 um, gamma = 72 %, matching the module.

defects.where: LIB colors: mold var(--panel2), resist var(--line), rdlL/rdlF var(--cu) op 0.3 vs buildup var(--accent) op 0.25, interposer & hbm both var(--si), pcb var(--line2) & lid var(--muted)
defects.what: Colour pairs are indistinguishable or invisible: mold compound (panel2 on panel) is invisible in both themes; solder resist (line) is invisible in light theme; organic RDL vs build-up substrate look the same pale tan in light theme; HBM stacks and the Si interposer share the same colour; PCB and lid are both grey in light.

defects.where: render() button row lines 185-190; flatten() keys line 99
defects.what: The button row lists one button per drawn instance, producing 6-8 identical 'HBM3E stack' / 'HBM3E/4 stack' buttons and four identically truncated 'XCD-on-IOD hybrid-bo...' buttons (base/top tier indistinguishable); labels >22 chars are cut with an ellipsis ('Lid / integrated hea...').
defects.fix: One button per layer type ('HBM3E stack x6', 'SoIC stack: base tier', 'SoIC stack: top tier'), no truncation (let buttons wrap), and highlight all instances of that type in the drawing.

defects.where: cteCtl label 'ΔT (assembly → use)' line 76; 360 px render
defects.what: At 360 px the ΔT control overflows the widget box by 14 px (harness: 'output exceeds box by 14px') because the long label + range intrinsic width + 64 px output exceed the row; the drawing also collapses to ~165 px tall with 13 px-wide HBM slivers.

defects.where: No per-preset explanation; select change handler line 197
defects.what: Switching presets changes only the stripes and numbers; there is no 1-2 sentence explanation of what each package family is or why it exists (criterion 7).
defects.fix: Add a w-note under the select that shows a preset-specific sentence, e.g. 'CoWoS-S: GPU and six HBM stacks sit on a passive silicon interposer whose 0.4-2 um wiring is 20-50x denser than the substrate; TSVs carry signals down to C4 bumps.'

defects.where: PKGS interposerArea/ubumps strings lines 37-40; dims readout lines 62-67
defects.what: Readout <b> values contain sentences instead of numbers: 'RDL: whole package; LSI bridges ~0.4 µm class', '~100,000+; SoIC bond pads ~28,000/mm² at 6 µm', '0 (gull-wing leads, 32–300)', which wrap awkwardly in 18 px mono especially at 360 px.
defects.fix: Keep only the number in <b> (e.g. '~2,800 mm²', '~100,000+') and move qualifiers into the <span> label or a note.

defects.where: LIB.rdlF thickness 'no substrate, no TSVs' line 13
defects.what: The 'thickness' field for the InFO RDL holds a non-thickness remark, so the detail line reads 'thickness: no substrate, no TSVs'.
defects.fix: Set thickness to '~2-3 RDL layers x ~5-10 µm polyimide/Cu' and move 'no substrate, no TSVs' to the material or a note.

result.redesign: Replace the stripe stack with a labelled schematic cross-section (viewBox about 380 x 260, width 100%) drawn in mounted orientation, bottom to top, with every part named in place via SVG text (>=11 px rendered, var(--sans), leader lines to a left/right label gutter) and a distinct token per material. Common bottom: PCB slab (var(--line2), one thin Cu trace line, label 'PCB'); a row of solder-ball circles at ~1 mm pitch under the full substrate width (var(--cu), label 'BGA balls'); thin solder-resist strips top and bottom of the substrate (var(--ok) 0.5); build-up substrate drawn as a thicker core band with 2-3 thin alternating Cu/ABF lines each side and a few via stubs (label 'Build-up substrate: ABF on BT core'). FCBGA: a row of small C4 dots only under the die, underfill fillets at both die edges (label 'underfill'), die (var(--accent2), label 'CPU/GPU die, flip-chip'), TIM1 strip across the die, and a lid drawn as an inverted-U cap whose feet sit on the substrate edge (label 'Lid / IHS'). CoWoS-S: C4 dots under a Si interposer slab (var(--si) 0.6) that shows 3-4 vertical TSV ticks and 2 horizontal RDL lines (label 'Si interposer: RDL + TSVs'), microbump dots under each die, GPU die plus HBM stacks drawn as a base die with 4-8 thin stacked DRAM slices (label 'HBM3E x6' once), underfill fillets, TIM across all dies, lid cap. CoWoS-L: same but the interposer is an organic RDL slab (var(--cu) 0.55) with two small dark 'LSI bridge' rectangles embedded under the GPU-HBM edges and 'TIV' pillars through it. SoIC-on-CoWoS: same as CoWoS-S but the logic stack is two tiers with a thin 'hybrid bond, 6-9 µm pitch' line between them and no bump dots between tiers. QFP: leadframe as a die paddle under the die plus separate lead fingers at die level that exit the mold and bend down as gull-wing leads onto PCB pads (label 'leadframe', 'gull-wing lead'); bond wires from die-top pads arcing down to the finger tips (label 'bond wire'); epoxy mold body (var(--muted) 0.25 + hatch) enclosing die, paddle and wires (label 'mold compound'). InFO: die with mold body beside it at die height, TIV pillars through the mold on both sides, RDL as a thin multi-line layer spanning the full package width under die+mold (label 'fan-out RDL'), balls under the whole RDL width so the fan-out is visible. defects.where: site/widgets/wafer-price.js drawB(), lines 126–130 (minP/maxP padding and yticks)
defects.what: Y-axis ticks are generated over 0..maxP in 5 steps and then filtered to >= minP, so the price-vs-utilization chart gets only 1–2 gridlines: with the module's own numbers the only label is '$40 000'; at the all-min extreme the only label is '$3 000'. defects.where: site/widgets/wafer-price.js setReadout() lines 167–172 and Panel C readout layout
defects.what: Readout values put provenance text inside the 18 px mono <b> ('$230B (actual (Mod. 20))' has double parentheses; '$675B (guided, ~$630–725B)' is long), which makes the 4-stat row reflow between one and two rows as you hover different years (layout jump) and nearly overflows at 360 px.
defects.fix: Keep <b> to the number ('$230B') and put the provenance in the <span> label ('top-4 hyperscaler capex · actual, Module 20'); give each .w-stat a min-width so the row does not reflow on hover.

defects.where: site/widgets/wafer-price.js line 12 (USABLE_AREA = 60000) and noteA text 'Density assumes usable area ≈ 60,000 mm² … (Module 20)'
defects.what: Module 20's price-per-transistor column assumes a 70,000 mm² usable wafer, so the widget's $/billion-transistor bars ($3.33 at 28 nm, $1.92 at 2 nm) are ~17% above the module's figures ($2.8 and $1.6 per billion) while claiming to follow it.
defects.fix: Set USABLE_AREA = 70000 (and say '70,000 mm²' in the note), or keep 60,000 but drop the 'per Module 20' attribution. Consider labelling the axis '$ per 100 M transistors' to match the module table exactly.

defects.where: site/widgets/wafer-price.js Panel C drawC() — stacked bars, and the w-note (line 205)
defects.what: TSMC capex is stacked on top of hyperscaler capex, which visually implies the two sum to a meaningful total (they are supply vs demand, not parts of one budget). The note then has to explain that 'the TSMC segment is a thin sliver'. The note itself is four lines long.
defects.fix: Draw grouped (side-by-side) bars per year, or hyperscaler bars with TSMC as a line/dots on the same $B axis; label each bar's value on top; cut the note to one or two sentences ('TSMC's ~$54B of 2026 capex is ~7% of what its four biggest end customers are spending — Module 20's point about who captures the value').

defects.where: site/widgets/wafer-price.js line 27 (caption) and section notes
defects.what: Caption describes the three panels but does not say what to do or what to notice (criterion 7: 'states what to do and what to notice').
defects.fix: e.g. 'Toggle $/wafer vs $/transistor, drag utilization to see why a half-empty 2 nm fab loses its margin, and hover a year in the capex chart.'

defects.where: site/widgets/wafer-price.js Panel B sliders (lines 82–87)
defects.what: Capex and wafer starts are independent, so extremes give physically meaningless fabs ($40B for 20,000 wspm = $2B per 1,000 wspm, 4x the module's maximum; or $5B for 200,000 wspm). Nothing warns the reader that the module's governing ratio is capex per 1,000 wspm (~$100M at 28 nm to ~$500M at 2 nm).
defects.fix: Show a derived readout 'capex per 1,000 wspm' and colour it var(--warn) when outside ~$80–600M, or tie the sliders through node presets as described above.

result.redesign: No full redraw needed: for an economics widget the three charts (bar chart of wafer price by node, price-vs-utilization curve, capex bars) are the right kind of picture and render cleanly at 760 px in both themes with correct formulas. The required rework is (1) a responsive redraw so chart text stays >= 11 px at 360 px, (2) defaults/presets that reproduce the Module 20 worked example ($20B, 40,000 wspm, $5,500 other → ~$32k), (3) a range-based y-axis for the curve, and (4) one added teaching element in Panel B: a stacked cost bar [depreciation | cash cost | gross margin] summing to the price, plus a 'gross margin at the node's current price' readout so the margin collapse at low utilization (58% → 38%) is visible, which is the lesson the module states.

defects.where: site/widgets/yield-cascade.js lines 117, 123, 141-142 (drawFunnel scrap, update totalScrap)
defects.what: ×1000 unit slip: 'lost' is already units per 1,000 starts, but scrap = (lost/1000) * s.value, so the '$ scrapped / 1,000 starts' column shows $105 for 350 lost × $300 (should be $105 000) and the total shows $333 instead of ~$333 000. Module 18's worked example (~$260k per 1,000 sorted die) is off by three orders of magnitude from what the widget displays.
defects.fix: scrap = lost * s.value; totalScrap += (counts[i]-counts[i+1]) * STAGES[i].value; format as '$' + fmt(scrap/1000, 0) + ' k' (e.g. '$105 k', total '$333 k') and keep the column heading 'per 1,000 starts'.

defects.where: site/widgets/yield-cascade.js lines 111-116 (fallout wedge polygon)
defects.what: Every fallout wedge is a degenerate polygon: all three points use x = xOut (measured bbox width 0.00 for all 7), so no red fallout is drawn at all. The drawing is just a tapering band with red numbers floating below it; nothing shows where units leave the chain, which is the whole point of the widget.
defects.fix: Draw each loss as a real stream: a path from the band's lower edge between xIn and xOut curving down into a scrap bin, e.g. points (xIn, midY+halfH(before)) (xOut, midY+halfH(after)) (xOut, binY) (xOut - streamW, binY) where streamW = max(6, lost/1000*segW*0.8); fill var(--bad) opacity .6. See redesign.

defects.where: drawFunnel lines 118-119: font-size 10 in a 720-unit viewBox
defects.what: All stage names and loss labels render at 9.5 px at 760 px width and 4 px at 360 px width (measured: svg width 286 px at 360). The 360 px funnel is completely illegible; fails the ≥11 px rule and 'works at 360 px'.
defects.fix: Use font-size ≥ 12 viewBox units at 720 wide, and below ~480 px container width switch to a vertical layout (viewBox ~360×640, band flowing top-to-bottom, stage names on the left) via a ResizeObserver on el, or set the viewBox width to the measured container width so text stays ≥ 11 CSS px.

defects.where: drawFunnel line 118 (label y = midY + hb + wedgeH + 13) and H = 240
defects.what: Loss labels sit at a different height for every stage (−13 at y≈152, −32 at y≈160, −350 at y≈226) with nothing connecting them to the band, and the lower half of the SVG (y 145-240) is blank except for the stray '−350'. Looks broken and wastes half the drawing area.
defects.fix: Put all loss counts on one baseline row directly under their scrap stream/bin; size H to the content (no wedgeH-dependent offsets); fill the freed space with the $-at-risk staircase described in the redesign.

defects.where: w-note, line 154
defects.what: Note says '125 °C burn-in vs. 55 °C field use gives AF ≈ 78, so a 24 h burn-in screens roughly 5 months of field operation' — the readout directly above it says 24 h → 1 863 field-h ≈ 2.6 months, and Module 18 says 24 h ≈ 2.6 months, 48 h ≈ 5 months.
defects.fix: Change to '…so a 24 h burn-in screens ≈ 2.6 months and 48 h ≈ 5 months of field operation (Module 18)'.

defects.where: inTu slider, line 68 (min 40, max 70)
defects.what: T_use maxes at 70 °C, so the module's own comparison (85 °C use → AF ≈ 10, 48 h covers only ~3 weeks) cannot be reproduced; scenario 'tuse-85-bi-min' clamped to 70 °C.
defects.fix: Set T_use range 25-95 °C (step 1). Guard AF < 1 when T_use ≥ T_stress (clamp or show 'no acceleration').

defects.where: STAGES values, VALUE_CHAIN, h5 heading line 149, fallout table
defects.what: Heading promises the 'rule of tens' but the '$ / unit at risk' column is flat ($2 800 for four rows, then $4 300, $9 300); the value-chain table ends at '$39 300 (+$30 000 rack share)' yet the rack row uses $9 300, so the two tables contradict each other and the last chain row feeds nothing. Module 18 also says board/rack failures are repaired, not scrapped, so '$ scrapped' at rack level is the wrong concept.
defects.fix: Merge into one table (Stage · Yield · Units lost / 1 000 starts · $ per unit at risk · $ lost / 1 000 starts · Outcome). Use consistent values (sort ~$350, package $2 800, module $4 300, board ~$25 k share, rack ~$45 k cumulative) and mark board/rack rows 'repaired, not scrapped: cost = find-and-fix'. Show the $ per unit ladder in the drawing (log-scaled bars) so the order-of-magnitude climb is visible; shorten the heading to 'Cost of fallout: the rule of tens'.

defects.where: falloutTable / chainTable at 360 px
defects.what: Money cells wrap mid-number ('$2' on one line, '800' on the next) because the thousands separator is a breaking space; the last column header '$ SCRAPPED / 1,000 STARTS' is clipped at the scroll-container edge (harness: table exceeds box by 11 px).
defects.fix: Add white-space: nowrap on all td/th (inline style or a per-cell style), keep the .table-scroll wrapper; abbreviate the last header to '$ lost / 1 000 starts'.

defects.where: drawFunnel line 118

defects.fix: Skip the label (and the stream) when lost < 0.05, or format as '0'.

defects.where: drawFunnel lines 127-128 (fill var(--panel))
defects.what: In the light theme '1,000' and '578.3' are white on the 75 %-opacity amber band (~2.6:1 contrast).
defects.fix: Use fill var(--ink) with paint-order: stroke and a 3 px var(--panel) stroke, or place the counts just outside the band ends.

defects.where: fmt calls throughout

defects.fix: Use fixed decimals (toFixed-style) per field: yields 2 dp, counts 1 dp, Ea 2 dp; use fmt(1000,0) for the start count; roll months over to years above 24 months.

defects.where: funnel SVG

defects.where: VALUE_CHAIN line 14-20, STAGES value 300
defects.what: Illustrative values drift from Module 18: sort die $300 (module ~$350); board share $5 000 → $9 300 cumulative vs module's $200-500 k per 8-GPU board (~$25-60 k per GPU).

result.redesign: Replace the single tapering trapezoid with a labelled test-chain Sankey that shows units AND dollars, in a viewBox 720×320 on desktop and a vertical 360×660 layout when the container is narrower than ~480 px (ResizeObserver on el, redraw with the same data). Layout, left to right: (1) a top row of seven stage boxes (rounded rect ~88×36, fill var(--panel2), stroke var(--line)) labelled in 12 px sans in place: 'Wafer sort', 'CoWoS assembly', 'FT1', 'Burn-in + FT2', 'SLT', 'Module test', 'Board / rack test', each with its live yield underneath in 11 px mono ('95.0 %'), and a tiny pictogram per box (probe card over a wafer; die on substrate; ATE socket; oven with 125 °C; SLT slot; SXM module; rack) so a newcomer sees what each screen is. (2) Under the boxes the survivor band (fill var(--accent)) flows through all seven stages; its height is proportional to surviving units, starting at 1 000 and ending at the shipped count; both counts printed at the ends in var(--ink) with a var(--panel) paint-order stroke, plus an 'in: 1 000 starts' / 'shipped' label. (3) At each stage's right edge a red stream (var(--bad), opacity .6, cubic path) peels off the band's lower edge and drops into a scrap bin drawn on one common baseline; stream/bin width ∝ units lost (min 6 px); each bin carries two labels on shared baselines: '−32 units' above and '$89 k' below (units × $/unit, per 1 000 starts), 11-12 px. (4) Beneath the bins a log-scaled '$ at risk per unit' staircase: one thin bar per stage, height ∝ log10($/unit), value printed ('$350', '$2.8 k', '$2.8 k', '$2.8 k', '$2.8 k', '$4.3 k', '$45 k'), with the caption 'value of one unit when it fails here (rule of tens)'. Board/rack bar labelled 'repaired, not scrapped'. (5) Hover or focus on a stage box or its stream highlights both (stroke var(--accent2)), highlights the matching table row, and shows an SVG tooltip: 'FT1 · 32 of 650 fail (5 %) · $2 800 each → $89 k per 1 000 starts'. Animation: a 300 ms morph of the band/streams when a slider moves (skip under prefers-reduced-motion). Merge the two HTML tables into one (Stage · Yield · Units lost / 1 000 starts · $ per unit at risk · $ lost / 1 000 starts · Outcome) with nowrap cells, and fix the numbers: $ lost = units lost × $/unit (no /1000), total shown as '$333 k per 1 000 starts'; note text '24 h ≈ 2.6 months, 48 h ≈ 5 months'; T_use slider 25-95 °C.

defects.where: site/widgets/rack-explorer.js:208 (updateHall, rUsd)
defects.what: ×1000 unit slip: '$' + fmt(racks * 3.5, 1) + ' B' — 3.5 is $ millions per rack, so 557 racks prints '$1 949.5 B', 21 racks prints '$73.5 B', 8 695 racks prints '$30 432.5 B'. The module's figure for this case is ~$2.2–2.7 billion.
defects.fix: rUsd.textContent = '$' + fmt(racks * 3.5 / 1000, 2) + ' B' (or keep millions and label ' M' below ~1 B). Cross-check: 640 racks → $2.2 B.

defects.where: site/widgets/rack-explorer.js:120-122, 201-203, 194 (note text)
defects.what: Invented '× 1.15 overhead' factor is not in Module 19 and breaks the cross-check: at the defaults (100 MW feed, 130 kW/rack, PUE 1.2) the widget shows 557 racks / 40 104 GPUs, while the module's worked example gives ~640 racks / ~46 000 GPUs (100 000 kW ÷ 1.2 ÷ 130). PUE already accounts for facility overhead.
defects.fix: Remove the 1.15 multiplier (racks = floor(hallMW*1000/PUE/rackKW)) so the defaults reproduce the module's ~640 racks, ~46 000 GPUs, ~$2.2 B; if a non-GPU IT share is wanted, expose it as its own labelled slider defaulting to 0 % and cite it as an assumption, not as a module figure. Update the .w-note formula accordingly.

defects.where: site/widgets/rack-explorer.js:54 (viewBox '0 0 700 300') + all drawL* functions; 360 px renders
defects.what: At 360 px the SVG is ~300 px wide, so every label renders at 4.3–4.9 px (11.5 user units × 0.43) and the package/rack drawing is a ~130 px postage stamp. Criterion 4 (text ≥ 11 px) and 5 (drawings scale) fail; the harness misses it because it reads the unscaled font-size.
defects.fix: Make the drawing responsive: observe el width with ResizeObserver and redraw with a viewBox whose width equals the rendered px width (e.g. W = clientWidth, H chosen per level), placing shapes as fractions of W and keeping font sizes as absolute px constants (≥ 11.5). Use a stacked 1-column layout below ~500 px (rack elevation on top, callouts below) so labels stay ≥ 11 px.

defects.where: site/widgets/rack-explorer.js:46-52 (hov) and every label drawn after its rect
defects.what: Hover does not work where users point: label <text> elements sit on top of the rects and intercept the pointer (elementFromPoint at a block centre returns 'text'; stroke is never set on Die A, compute block, spine). When hover does fire at an edge, the highlight is stroke var(--accent) on var(--accent)-filled parts (dies, GPUs, compute trays, row racks) — invisible. The supplier/'who builds it' text exists only in native <title> tooltips: delayed, unstyled, and absent on touch, so the widget's key extra teaching layer is effectively hidden.
defects.fix: Set pointer-events:none on all label text (or attach hover to a <g> that wraps rect+text). Highlight with a stroke that contrasts with every fill (var(--ink) 2 px, plus raising opacity of siblings to 0.6). Show the supplier line in an HTML panel under the SVG (e.g. a .w-note that updates on mouseenter/focus/click and stays on tap) instead of <title>; make hover targets focusable (tabindex=0) for keyboard.

defects.what: The schematics do not teach at a glance and leave large blank areas: L1 fills 46 % of the SVG width, L4 (the rack, the title's namesake) 25 % — three slabs and a bar. Unlabelled parts everywhere: L1 interposer, substrate and the NV-HBI seam (a 14-unit line smaller than its caption); L2 the two VRM rectangles, no LPDDR5X beside Grace, C2C links unlabelled; L3 two empty boxes 'Superchip 1/2' with unlabelled cold-plate strip and four unlabelled NIC chips, no DPU, no manifold/quick-disconnects; L4 compute drawn as one slab (no trays, switches not in the middle of the rack where the module says they sit, no spine fan-out, no coolant manifold/CDU, no busbar); L5 eight identical unlabelled bars.
defects.fix: Redraw per the redesign below: each level's drawing spans ≥ 85 % of the SVG width, every part labelled in place, the rack drawn as a tray-by-tray elevation with switches in the middle and spine fan-out lines.

defects.where: drawL5 (lines 119-138), min/max slider shots
defects.what: The hall drawing does not respond to the sliders: 100 MW and 1 000 MW both render the same 48 purple boxes plus a '+N more pods' caption, while 10 MW shows 3 boxes in a large empty panel. The boxes are unlabelled ('pod' is only in the tooltip) and the pod unit is the admittedly 'illustrative' 8-rack row from level 5, so the hall is built on an invented figure.
defects.fix: Tile racks, not pods: n = racks, tile size = fit(n) so the grid area is proportional to hall IT power (cap at ~1 000 tiles then draw density), label '1 tile = 1 NVL72 rack (72 GPUs)', and draw substation → PUE loss → IT power as a labelled flow with the numbers. Motivate the row grouping from the module instead: in-row CDU ~1–2 MW → 8–15 racks per CDU.

defects.where: drawL0/L1/L2/L3 fills: var(--accent) vs var(--warn); drawL5 substation
defects.what: Identical-looking colours for different parts: --warn (#F0B429 dark / #C98A00 light) is nearly the same hue as --accent (#F2B13B / #B8770A), so power shelves look like compute trays, VRMs look like GPUs, substation looks like a rack.
defects.fix: Assign distinct tokens: GPU dies/packages --accent, HBM and NVLink switches --accent2, Grace CPU/NICs --si, copper spine/cables --cu, coolant/cold plates/CDU --ok, power shelves/VRM/substation --bad or a --line2 outline with hatch. Add a small in-place legend only as a supplement to in-place labels.

defects.what: Four SVG labels at 10.5 px ('18 chips, 130 TB/s', '6–8 power shelves', 'Substation', 'Cooling plant') are below the 11 px floor even at 760 px.
defects.fix: Use ≥ 11.5 px and widen the blocks to fit (see rack redraw).

defects.where: line 97 ('72 GPUs + 36 Grace' in a 100-unit block)
defects.what: Label is 99 px wide inside a 100 px block and touches/spills past both edges (measured 1 px spill; visibly cramped in both themes).
defects.fix: Make the rack ≥ 200 units wide in the redraw, or split into two lines.

defects.where: updateHall lines 200, 206
defects.what: Readout precision/units: PUE prints '1' at the minimum (fmt strips zeros) while other positions show '1.2'/'1.6'; HBM capacity prints '7 463.8 TB' / '116 513 TB' instead of PB.
defects.fix: PUE: Number(hall.pue).toFixed(2). HBM: show PB when ≥ 1 000 TB (racks*13.4/1000 → '7.5 PB'), TB otherwise.

defects.where: LEVELS spec, line 10 (Weight '~78 kg (est., 1.4 t ÷ 18 trays)') and 'Weight: —' rows on levels 1, 2, 5
defects.what: Tray weight assigns the whole rack mass (and 1.4 t, not the 1.36 t used elsewhere) to the 18 compute trays only, ignoring switch trays, power shelves and spine — an unsupported estimate. Three levels show an empty 'Weight —' row.
defects.fix: Drop the tray weight (or say 'part of the 1.36 t rack') and skip spec rows whose value is '—' in renderSpec.

defects.where: line 193-194 (.w-note) — formula placement
defects.what: The formula is in a .w-note rather than the spec's .w-formula, and the note asserts the 1.15 factor is from Module 19 ('(Module 19)'), which it is not.
defects.fix:
Move the formula to
racks = (hall MW × 1000 ÷ PUE) ÷ kW per rack
and keep the $3.5 M/rack and 2 miles/rack citations in the note.

defects.where: drawL0 line 62 label 'HBM' ×8; drawL4 racks (lines 108-112)
defects.what: Repeated bare labels convey no numbers: eight 'HBM' boxes without capacity, eight racks without an 'NVL72' label or internal structure.
defects.fix: Label one stack 'HBM3E 24 GB' and a bracket '×8 = 192 GB'; draw each row rack as a mini elevation (compute/switch/power bands) with one 'NVL72 ×8' label.

result.redesign:
Keep the six-level step-through, dots, counter, spec table and hall sliders, but redraw every level so the drawing fills the SVG (≥85 % width) and is a recognisable schematic with parts labelled in place. Parametrise the draw functions on the rendered width (ResizeObserver → viewBox width = px width; fonts fixed ≥ 11.5 px; stacked layout under ~500 px) so labels stay legible at 360 px. Put pointer-events:none on all text, hover-highlight with an ink stroke, and show supplier text in an HTML panel under the SVG on hover/focus/tap instead of <title>. Colour code: GPU --accent, HBM/NVLink switch --accent2, Grace/NIC --si, copper --cu, coolant --ok, power --bad (not --warn, which is indistinguishable from --accent).

L1 Blackwell package (plan view, ~90 % width): outer ABF substrate (label), CoWoS-L interposer inside it (label '~100 mm CoWoS-L interposer: organic RDL + LSI bridges'), two dies labelled 'Blackwell die A/B ~800 mm², TSMC 4NP', a hatched seam between them labelled 'NV-HBI 10 TB/s' with a small 'LSI bridge' rectangle under the seam, eight HBM3E stacks (four above, four below) with one labelled 'HBM3E 24 GB' and a bracket '×8 = 192 GB (8 TB/s)'; scale bar '100 mm'.

L2 GB200 superchip (Bianca board, full width): board outline labelled 'Bianca board'; centre Grace CPU (--si) '72 Arm cores' with two LPDDR5X strips beside it '480 GB LPDDR5X, ~500 GB/s'; left/right a miniature of the L1 package (dies + HBM dots) labelled 'Blackwell GPU ×2'; double arrows GPU↔Grace labelled 'NVLink-C2C 900 GB/s'; a row of small VRM phases beside each package labelled 'VRM ~16–30 phases (MPS/Infineon)'; rear-edge connector strip labelled 'NVLink ports → spine'; '~2 700 W'.

L3 compute tray (plan view of a 1U MGX tray, full width): two Bianca boards drawn as mini GPU–CPU–GPU groups; semi-transparent cold plates over each package labelled 'cold plate (CoolIT/Boyd)'; coolant supply/return manifold to the rear with two quick-disconnect symbols 'QD (Stäubli/CPC)'; four NIC chips 'ConnectX-7/8 ×4 (800G)' and one 'BlueField-3 DPU'; arrow 'front ⇄ rear, 1U'; '4 GPUs + 2 Grace, ~5.4 kW'.

L4 NVL72 rack (front elevation, ≥60 % of SVG height, 2-column on desktop: rack left, callouts right): power shelves at top '6–8 × 33 kW shelves → DC busbar'; 9 compute trays, then 9 NVLink switch trays in the MIDDLE labelled '9 switch trays, 18 NVLink-5 chips, 130 TB/s', then 9 more compute trays — each tray a distinct 1U slot so '18 compute trays = 72 GPUs + 36 Grace' is countable; a copper spine bar at the rear with fan-out lines from every compute tray to the switch block labelled 'NVLink spine ~5 000 copper cables, ~2 miles' and a bracket 'copper reach ~1–1.5 m → switches in the middle'; a coolant manifold on the other side with supply/return arrows to a CDU icon '25–45 °C, to CDU'; dimension notes '~2.2 m, ~1.36 t, 120–132 kW'. Hovering the spine should highlight the fan-out lines.

L5 row (full width): eight mini rack elevations (compute/switch/power bands) labelled 'NVL72 ×8 (illustrative)'; an in-row CDU with a supply/return loop drawn to each rack labelled 'in-row CDU ~1–2 MW → 8–15 racks'; a leaf-switch block with dashed optical links from each rack labelled '800G optics → Quantum-X800 / Spectrum-X leaf'; busbar/power feed line.

L6 hall: a labelled flow 'substation N MW → ÷ PUE → IT MW → ÷ kW per rack = racks' with the live numbers, then a tile grid where 1 tile = 1 NVL72 rack (tiles shrink with count, grouped in rows with a CDU tick per ~10 racks) so 10 MW, 100 MW and 1 000 MW look different; substation and cooling plant drawn as labelled blocks at the edges. Fix readouts: drop the ×1.15 factor (defaults → ~640 racks, ~46 000 GPUs), $ in billions (÷1000), HBM in PB, PUE to 2 decimals, formula in .w-formula. No animation is needed; the widget is a step-through, but slider changes should re-tile the hall immediately.

issues.what: The designed wide layout is never shown on the real course page. On http://localhost:8790/?qa=1#/m/02 at 1100 and 1400 px viewports the widget stage is 658 px wide (article max-width 760 minus 2x32 padding, 2 px widget border and 2x18 widget-body padding), but relayout() switches to 'wide' only when cw >= 670. Desktop readers therefore get the phone layout (viewBox 460x990) scaled 1.43x: 18.6 px labels larger than the body text, a 1416 px-tall SVG with the inset and time bar stacked under the puller, and the abbreviated narrow labels ('gate valve', 'chamber / water-cooled', no 'furnace chamber', no heater ~150 kW / 1,500-1,600 C, no '4 habit lines', no 'via purge tube', the scale-break zigzag still drawn on the body but its explanatory label dropped, no 'Main view: 1 px ...' note). The agent's harness shots were taken in widget-test.html where the stage is 686 px, so they do not represent the site.
issues.fix: In site/widgets/cz-puller.js relayout(): switch to wide at a threshold the real page meets (e.g. cw >= 600) and derive the wide font from the real width so rendered text stays >= 11 px, e.g. fs = Math.max(12.5, Math.round(11.2 * 760 / cw * 2) / 2) (gives 13 at 658 px), or shrink the wide viewBox to ~700 wide; give the left label column a few px of margin so 13 px labels are not squeezed. Verify with node qa/render.js page '#/m/02' (page mode) as well as widget mode, and look at the resulting PNGs.

issues.what: The animation loop can die permanently and Play then lies. The IntersectionObserver callback does visible = es[0].isIntersecting; when one delivery batches two entries [false, true] (any viewport/device-metrics change; Puppeteer's captureBeyondViewport element screenshot triggers it 100% of the time) visible sticks at false, ensureLoop() never schedules rAF, and clicking Play flips the label to 'Pause' while nothing moves for the rest of the session. Reproduced with an instrumented replay of qa/scenarios/cz-puller.json: rAF count froze at 838 right after the 'phase4-body-start' shot; consequently the harness PNGs phase4-body-mid (9:44), end-of-run (51:24, 350 kg grown / 50 kg left, button 'Pause') and phase1-meltdown-mid (0:00) are identical to their start states, so the scenario never actually rendered the mid-body, tail or end-of-run states that the change claims to exercise (the claimed 361 kg / 39 kg end state only appears when the loop is alive; I confirmed those numbers with a separate run).
issues.fix: Use the latest entry: visible = es[es.length - 1].isIntersecting (or reduce over entries). Additionally make the loop self-healing: in the Play handler and ensureLoop(), re-check visibility directly (io.takeRecords() or a bounding-rect test) instead of trusting the cached flag, and disable/relabel Play if the loop cannot run. Re-run the scenario afterwards and confirm phase4-body-mid, end-of-run and phase1-meltdown-mid PNGs differ from their start frames.

issues.what: Text clipped at the SVG edge: the time-bar cursor label 'now 51:24' / 'now 52:17' / 'now 53:04' extends to x=691 of a 686 px SVG at 760 (last digit cut off) throughout the tail phase and at end of run, because draw() clamps its x to insW - 62 while the 9-character mono string is ~68 px wide, and the inset sits at x=512 in a 760 viewBox. The harness did not flag it because ANALYZE only runs at the final scenario state (phase 3).
issues.fix: Clamp using the measured text width (nowTxt.getComputedTextLength()) - x = Math.min(insW - w, Math.max(0, cxT - 20)) - or switch text-anchor to 'end' once the cursor passes ~70% of the bar; keep the label inside the inset column.

issues.what: Labels touching edges: in phase 1 the left label 'chunks, 400 kg' has 0 px margin to the SVG's left edge (textLength-squeezed to exactly the available width), and the inset's 'meniscus' label starts 1 px outside the inset rect so the 'm' sits on the inset border.
issues.fix: Give the left label column a 4-6 px inset (xL = cx - rCh - 14 and avail = xL - 6) and start the inset 'meniscus' label at x >= 6 inside the inset (or anchor it 'start' beside the meniscus curve).

issues.what: Inset physics label contradicts the module: 'dislocations glide out at ~55°' with the animated neck lines drawn at ~53° from the pull axis (dx=4, dy=-3), while course/modules/02-crystal-growth.md says {111} glide planes lie at ~35.3° to the <100> axis (54.7° is the angle of the plane normal). The static seed dislocation lines are drawn at ~30-35° from vertical, so the inset is internally inconsistent too.
issues.fix: Label it '{111} glide planes ~35° to the pull axis' (or '~55° to the melt surface') and draw the animated neck lines at ~35° from vertical (e.g. dx=2.5, dy=-3.5).

issues.what: Terminology and note nits: narrow mode labels the valve 'gate valve' while the module and the wide layout say 'isolation valve'; the HTML note says the body is shortened 'so 2.3 m fits' while the crystal-length readout reaches 2.43 m; v/G at 1.5 mm/min prints '5×10⁻³' while other values print one decimal ('2.7', '1.7').
issues.fix: Use 'isolation valve' in both modes (it fits at the narrow font), say '2.4 m', and format v/G with fmt(vG, 1) forced to one decimal (or toFixed(1)).

result.praise: The drawing itself is a genuinely good teaching schematic: chamber split with isolation valve, argon path with purge tube, meander-slot heater, hatched susceptor, quartz crucible, melt gradient, crystal with neck/crown/body/tail, meniscus curves, crucible shaft with lift and rotation, all labelled in place; the five material colours stay distinct in light and dark; the phase-1 chunk pile slumping onto a rising melt, the crucible rising while the interface stays fixed, and the magnified Dash-neck inset with the 3 mm dimension are exactly what a non-expert needs. The numbers cross-check against module 02 (343 kg per 2 m body, 0.11 mm/min lift at 0.8 mm/min, 416 MPa at 300 kg, 41.7 h body, 361 kg / 39 kg left at the true end, v/G regime thresholds), effective font sizes are 11.2-11.3 px at both widths, and the harness report is clean apart from the test page's own favicon 404.

issues.what: SVG label text is below the 11 px rendered-size floor (WIDGET_SPEC rule 8, QA criterion 4; '8–9 px inside SVG' is a listed common failure). The harness tinyText check reads computed font-size in SVG user units and ignores viewBox scaling, so it reports nothing, but measured via getScreenCTM: at the 760 px harness width the drawing (viewBox 720 rendered at 686 px, scale 0.953) draws 63 of 73 labels at 10.48 px (FSS=11: every tool/rack/utility box label, 'city water', 'OHT rail', 'supply plenum…', right-gutter callouts) and the other 10 at 11.43 px; on the real site (.article 760 − 2×32 padding − 2×18 widget-body padding → SVG 658 px, scale 0.914) box labels are ~10.05 px and even the level headings fall to 10.97 px. At 360 px (viewBox 420 rendered at 286 px, scale 0.681) 34 labels render at 8.85 px and 8 at 9.87 px, so the builder's '360 px renders with ~11 px text' claim is false (reference widgets render 11.0–11.6 px at 760 and 9.9–11.5 px at 360).
issues.fix: Size fonts for the rendered scale, not the viewBox. Wide layout: raise FSS 11 → 12.5 and FS 12 → 13.5 (≥ 11.4 px at scale 0.914), then re-check the 64/76-wide boxes ('gas & VMB', 'chemical delivery', 'ASU: bulk N₂' at 12.5 px bold ≈ 62–68 px) by widening boxes to ~72 px with 4 px gaps or shortening labels. Compact layout: either narrow the viewBox to ~330 units (drop the left gutter and put level names in-band, keep 2 tools / 3 racks / 4 utilities) so 13 user units ≈ 11 px, or keep 420 and use FS/FSS ≥ 16.5/16 with single-line box labels ('UPW', 'N₂ (ASU)', 'power', 'scrub', 'pumps', 'gas/VMB', 'RF'). Verify with rendered = fontSize × (svg.clientWidth / viewBox.width) ≥ 11 at both 686 px and 286 px before re-submitting; do not rely on the harness tinyText field.

issues.what: Air-dot columns run straight through solid objects: cols x=260 and x=454 (compact x=254) pass through both OHT vehicles and their hanging FOUPs; the 'OHT vehicle lowering a FOUP onto a load port' label halo cuts the hoist belts it sits on; the 'FFU ceiling: EC fan + ULPA filter per module' label halo cuts the downflow arrows at x=260/357.
issues.fix: Keep vehicles ≥ 30 units from any dot column (e.g. pair-0 vehicle centre at ac−28 or move cols to 300/420 and 246/476 for the FOUP shelves), place the vehicle caption to the right of the belts (x = ac + 14, y = 175) or under the lowered FOUP, and position the FFU caption in a gap between arrow columns (e.g. x 270–350).

issues.what: Builder claims 'the gutter ISO tag follows' the explorer, but dyn.tagBall/dyn.tagSub only change fill and font-weight; at ISO 4 or ISO 6 the ballroom gutter still reads 'ISO 5' while highlighted, and at ISO 7/8 it stays 'ISO 7–8'.
issues.fix: In update(): when zone is 'ball' set dyn.tagBall.textContent = 'ISO ' + st.N (restore 'ISO 5' otherwise); when zone is 'sub' set dyn.tagSub.textContent = 'ISO ' + st.N (restore 'ISO 7–8' otherwise), or drop the claim.

issues.what: The two band hotspots (Cleanroom ballroom, Sub-fab) have no visible hover/focus state, unlike the 26 part hotspots (QA criterion 6: hover targets have a visible hover state); hovering the ballroom only changes the info panel.
issues.fix: Give bandHot the same pointerenter/leave + focus/blur toggle as hot() with a lighter tint (fill var(--accent), fill-opacity .06, stroke var(--accent) 1.5 px) so the band visibly responds.

issues.what: Crossing-time readout loses precision at the slider maximum: 0.50 m/s shows '8 s' (and '≈ 8 s' in the formula box) while other values show '8.9 s' / '13.3 s'.
issues.fix: Use tCross.toFixed(1) + ' s' for the readout and the formula string instead of fmt(tCross, 1).

issues.what: The info panel has minHeight 58 px (two lines) but every hover fills three lines (~90 px), so the readouts, ladder and formula boxes jump down on each hover and back up when nothing is selected.
issues.fix: Set the info panel minHeight to the 3-line height (~88 px at 13 px/1.5 line-height) or give it a fixed height with overflow hidden so hovering never reflows the widget.

issues.what: qa/scenarios/fab-anatomy.json assumes the widget starts paused (its first click is meant to Play). That is only true when prefers-reduced-motion is on, which this harness machine reports; on a machine without it the widget autoplays, the first click pauses it, and the 'airflow-1s'/'airflow-2.7s' shots show a static state while 'paused' shows motion.
issues.fix: Take the two motion shots before any click (wait 1200 / shot, wait 1500 / shot: they show motion wherever autoplay is on) and name the click-driven shots by toggle ('toggle-1', 'toggle-2'), or document in the scenario that it expects a reduced-motion environment.

issues.what: ISO 2 at 0.5 µm is shown as '4 ‡' with the note 'ISO 14644-1 does not tabulate this limit', but the module's table (and ISO 14644-1:1999) list 4 for ISO 2; only the 2015 edition dropped entries under 10. The footnote wording may confuse a reader cross-checking the module.
issues.fix: Reword the ‡ note: 'ISO 14644-1:2015 no longer tabulates limits under 10 particles (older editions listed 4 for ISO 2); the value shown is the formula.'

result.praise: The drawing is a genuinely teachable cross-section: six levels labelled in place with numbered gutter names and right-gutter callouts, MAU/AMC filter/fans, FFU grid, OHT rail with a vehicle actually lowering a FOUP, four green EFEM mini-environments with docked FOUPs, perforated floor on pedestals, waffle slab with openings, sub-fab racks wired through the slab, a full utility level with outside feeds and a grade line; the recirculating airflow loop (down, through floor and slab, across the sub-fab return plenum, up both shafts, back into the fan deck) reads correctly with static arrows when paused. Every number and hover fact matches module 05 (ISO formula with 3-s.f. rounding, 7.2/h and 0.071/h landing rates, 8.9 s → 405 ACH, scanner/OHT/UPW/power figures), the ISO explorer highlights the right zone and moves the ladder marker for all eight classes, extremes give sane output, the harness report is clean in both themes, hotspots are keyboard-focusable, remount is clean, and cleanup cancels rAF and disconnects both observers.

issues.what: SVG text renders below the 11 px bar at every tested width, and the builder's claim 'all SVG text stays >= 11 px rendered at 360 px' is false. Measured (getBoundingClientRect width / viewBox width x font-size) in site/widgets/amhs-sim.js: at the harness's 360 px width the widget body is 324 px and the SVG is 286 px wide, so the 360-unit narrow viewBox scales by 0.794 and all 19 schematic labels render at 8.7-9.5 px and the chart labels at 9.5 px; at the 760 px harness width the 720-unit wide viewBox scales by 0.953 so the 17 labels set at 11 units render at 10.5 px; at a 600 px container (the spec says desktop is ~560-760 px) the wide layout renders at 8.0-8.8 px, and at the 480 px breakpoint it would be ~6.8 px. The harness's tinyText check reads computed font-size in user units, so it cannot see this. The 18 px widget-body padding on each side was not accounted for.
issues.fix: Lay out against the measured pixel width instead of fixed 720/360 viewBoxes: in relayout(w) set L.vw = w (the el.clientWidth passed in) and scale bay/loop geometry to it (or at minimum set the narrow viewBox to ~288 wide and the wide viewBox to ~660 wide, matching the real page: 760 max-width article - 2x32 padding - 2x18 body padding), so that 11 viewBox units = 11 rendered px; the chart SVG (330 units) needs the same treatment at 360 px (renders 286 px -> 9.5 px). yield-calculator.js does this (its viewBox width equals the rendered width, giving exactly 11.0 px at 360). Re-measure with fontSize x (svg.getBoundingClientRect().width / viewBox.width) at 360, 600 and 760 after the change.

issues.what: The belt hoist is drawn diagonally and vehicles stack on one point. Every bay has a single rail stop at the bay centre (bayBox: bay.d = loop.dTop(cx) etc., lines 61/71), but the hoist targets a random tool's load port (v.tool = 0-2, line 213), so for 2 of 3 tools the 'belt' line and the FOUP travel ~68 units sideways (visible in every playing screenshot: Etch, Deposition, CMP, Metrology bays; zoom-schematic-dark.png, zoom-schematic-playing-light.png). A belt hoist lowers vertically onto the load port (module 05: 'belts unwind to lower the gripper several metres to the load port'), and the widget's own note says vehicles 'stop above a load port'; the drawing contradicts both, so a non-expert reads it as vehicles swinging FOUPs sideways. Because all vehicles bound for one bay stop at the identical rail point, two vehicles also render on top of each other (crop-hot-hoist.png: hot vehicle and a normal vehicle superimposed at the Metrology stop, each hoisting in a different diagonal direction).
issues.fix: Give each tool its own rail stop: in bayBox compute t.d = loop.dTop(t.port.x) / loop.dBottom(t.port.x) for the horizontal layout and loop.dLeft(t.port.y) / loop.dRight(t.port.y) for the vertical one, pick v.tool before travelling, and in step() use L.bays[v.target].tools[v.tool].d as the arrival distance, so the vehicle stops directly above (beside) its load port and the hoist line is perpendicular to the rail; keep bay.d only for nextBay ordering. This also spreads simultaneous arrivals across three stops per bay. Optionally add a small minimum spacing so vehicles do not overlap on the rail.

issues.what: renderTools() is only called from the animation frame, so while paused (the default under prefers-reduced-motion, which is what headless Chrome reports on this machine) moving the utilization slider updates the queue shelves and readouts but leaves the tool busy/idle pattern stale: the u = 60 % screenshot (amhs-sim-760-dark-u-60.png) still shows 2 of 3 tools busy in every bay, which contradicts the '60 %' the learner just set.
issues.fix: Call renderTools() at the end of update() (after st.u is re-read) so the busy fraction tracks the slider even when paused.

issues.what: Hard-coded colour: the shelf-overflow badge text at line 163 uses fill: '#fff' (spec rule 1: never hard-code hex; the harness happens to whitelist #fff). The branch is also unreachable: max L_q is 0.98 x 49 x 1.5 = 72.0 lots, below the shelf capacity of 76 (wide, 19x4) and 84 (narrow, 6x14), so the '+N' badge can never appear.
issues.fix: Either delete the full > cap branch, or keep it and use a token (e.g. fill: 'var(--panel)' or 'var(--ground)') for the badge text and lower the shelf capacity so the overflow badge actually fires above ~u = 95 % to strengthen the 'queues explode' visual.

result.praise: The model is exactly right and every readout reproduces module 05's worked examples to the digit (4 h / 5x / 90 d / 296 053 wafers / 11 842 FOUPs / 6 579 deliveries per h / 548 vehicles busy; u = 90 and 95 % give X = 10 and 20; 20k wspm gives 59 211 WIP), the Kingman formula, X-factor, Little's law and the AMHS arithmetic are all shown live with the assumptions and the single-server caveat spelled out, the operating-curve chart with its asymptote label and the verdict text keyed to the module's utilization table make the 'queues explode' point clearly, both themes are legible with token-only colours, and the widget survives double mount, breakpoint resizes while playing, slider extremes and unmount mid-animation with zero console errors.

issues.what: Output-plot (I_D vs V_D) labels collide. The 'saturation (pinch-off)' text is placed with no collision check (site/widgets/mosfet-iv.js lines 249-252: sx = min(mid.x+8, 182), text ~120 px wide) so it runs into the right-hand V_G label column: it overlaps '0.8 V'/'0.6 V'/'1.0 V' in ~200 of 576 scanned slider states (e.g. the scenario's own leaky extreme V_T 0.2/SS 100/DIBL 150/V_D 1.0: '(pinch-off)' over '0.8 V'), and in the PLANAR PRESET (one of the three required presets, shot preset-planar in both themes) the label is drawn across the live curve and the operating-point marker sits on top of it, reading 'pi●h-off'. The 'V_G =' header (line 261, y = P2.T-4) is not part of the family-label de-collision, so '1.0 V' prints over 'V_G =' whenever the 1.0 V curve saturates near the top of the scale (planar preset: 27x4 px overlap; V_T 0.6/SS 80/DIBL 0/V_D 0.05: 27x12 px, illegible). Family labels are spaced 13 px (line 258) but 12 px mono text is ~14.5 px tall, so '0.6 V'/'0.4 V' overlap by 2-3 px in 96 states. Also, when there is no room left of the locus, 'linear' falls back to the RIGHT of the locus under 'saturation' (line 251), i.e. the linear label lands in the saturation region (V_T 0.6/SS 80/DIBL 0/V_D 0.05).
issues.fix: Reuse the collision-aware put() from drawLog for the output plot (make it take a per-plot 'placed' list and plot bounds). Pre-register boxes for the op-point marker, every family label and the 'V_G =' header (or drop the header and rely on the title 'one per V_G'), clamp sx so sx + textWidth <= P2.W - P2.R - 4, and give 'linear'/'saturation' candidates on their own side of the locus only (linear: left/above, saturation: right/below), never mirrored. Raise family label spacing to 15 px, shift the stack up if the last label exceeds Y2B, and include the header in that stack.

issues.what: Transfer-plot labels print on top of each other. put() (line 203) falls back to the FIRST candidate when every candidate collides, so 'I_on 289.8 µA' and 'V_D = 50 mV' are drawn over each other (67x17 px, unreadable) at V_T 0.5 / SS 100 / DIBL 0 / V_D 0.7; same for V_T 0.5/SS 100/DIBL 75/V_D 0.7 (67x15), V_T 0.35/SS 60/DIBL 0/V_D 1.0 (56x3), V_T 0.6/DIBL 150/V_D 1.0 etc. (30 of 576 scanned states), and 'V_T = 0.43 V' touches 'I_on 2.03 mA' at V_T 0.5/DIBL 75/V_D 1.0. In the default state the 'I_on 1 mA' label sits directly on the dashed V_D = 50 mV curve (legible only via the halo).
issues.fix: Give the 'V_D = 50 mV' label more candidates (along the dashed curve at k = 40, 50, 62, 75 and below it with dy up to +42, plus a spot mid-curve where the dashed and solid curves diverge, which is the informative place anyway) and make the fallback choose the candidate with the smallest overlap area instead of the first. For I_on prefer candidates above-left of the marker when V_D >= 0.6 so it clears the dashed curve.

issues.what: V_D doubles as V_DD, so the linear-region demo the spec asks for (V_D = 0.05 V, scenario shot vd-0.05-linear-region) makes the I_on/I_off readouts degenerate: I_on (V_G = V_D = 0.05 V) = 2.8 nA next to I_off = 550.6 pA, ratio '5.2 x 10^0' in red, and the transfer plot labels 'I_on 2.8 nA' beside 'I_off'; at V_T 0.6/V_D 0.05 it reads I_on = 32.3 fA, ratio 6.8. A learner reads this as 'lowering the drain voltage broke the transistor'.
issues.fix: Either keep V_DD fixed (0.7 V, or a small V_DD select 0.6/0.7/0.8/1.0 V) for the I_on/I_off readouts and markers while V_D stays free, or keep the coupling and add one sentence to the readout/state text: 'I_on is taken at V_G = V_DD; a 0.05 V supply cannot turn the device on, which is why V_DD cannot fall much below 0.6-0.7 V'.

issues.what: Terms are not defined on first use: 'DIBL' is never expanded to drain-induced barrier lowering anywhere in the widget (caption, slider, formula, state text all use the acronym), 'SS' is never spelled out as subthreshold swing in visible text, and k, T, q in 'SS = (kT/q)·ln 10 · m' are unnamed (kT/q = 25.9 mV at 300 K only appears in a code comment).
issues.fix: Slider labels 'Swing SS (subthreshold swing)' and 'DIBL (drain-induced barrier lowering)', and extend the formula line: 'k Boltzmann's constant, T = 300 K, q electron charge, kT/q = 25.9 mV'.

issues.what: The live V_G curve (thick accent2 line, e.g. 0.70 V) in the output plot has no label in the V_G column; only the fixed family 0.4/0.6/0.8/1.0 V is labelled, so the reader must guess what the highlighted curve is.
issues.fix: Push the live value (e.g. '0.70 V' in accent2, bold) into the labels array before the de-collision pass so it is labelled like the others.

issues.what: When I_off drops below the 1 pA axis floor (ideal extreme V_T 0.6/SS 60: 4.7 fA and 5.5 fA) the I_off ring is clamped onto the x-axis at 1 pA while its label says '5.5 fA', and the solid curve runs flat along the axis for the first ~0.13 V.
issues.fix: Hide the I_off ring when ioff < I_MIN and label it '< 1 pA (5.5 fA)', or extend the log axis to 1 fA (11 decades) so the curve and marker stay real.

issues.what: In the OFF state (V_G = 0-0.2 V) the cross-section keeps the label 'channel: inversion layer (electrons)' and a faint inversion polygon (fill-opacity up to ~0.6 at 0.2 V) while the state text says 'no inversion layer has formed'.
issues.fix: Below V_T switch the label to 'channel (no inversion yet: leakage only)' and fade the polygon to 0 below V_T - 2·SS; keep the 2-3 leakage electrons.

issues.what: Scenario robustness: this machine's headless Chrome reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, so the widget (correctly) starts paused; the scenario's final 'paused' shot is therefore actually the playing state and 'electrons-1.5s' is static. Not a widget bug (motion verified working with reduced-motion emulated off), but the scenario names do not match what they capture here. Also note subscripts are 10 px tspans in a 340-unit viewBox, i.e. ~8.4 px at the 360 px render (main labels ~10.1 px); consistent with the reference widgets, so not failed on it.
issues.fix: In the scenario, click 'Play electrons' first only if the button text is 'Play electrons' is not expressible, so instead click the sweep button (which forces playing) before the 1.5 s wait, and rename the final shot 'toggled-play-pause'. Optionally bump subscript tspans to 10.5-11.

result.praise: The physics is right and cross-checked: the EKV-style unified curve gives exactly SS = n·59.6 mV/dec below threshold, square-law/velocity-saturated above, V_Dsat = (V_G-V_T)/n with the pinch-off locus drawn through the knees, V_T(V_D) = V_T - DIBL·(V_D - 0.05 V), and the calibration reproduces the module's numbers (FinFET 1.00 mA/µm on, 1.7 nA/µm off, ratio 5.9e5; GAA 0.6 nA/µm, 1.7e6; planar 64 nA/µm, 1.4e4; 40 mV/V at 0.7 V gives 2.9x more leakage, matching the module's '~3x'). The cross-section is a genuinely legible labelled schematic (n+ pockets, metal gate, ~1 nm EOT oxide, depletion region that deepens with V_G and bulges from the drain with V_D/DIBL, inversion layer that tapers to pinch-off, leakage electrons trickling in OFF), the end-view inset makes the 1/3/4-side gating point at a glance, per-state explanations are good, both themes and 360 px render cleanly with token colours only, the animation runs/pauses correctly and respects reduced motion, remounting and cleanup are clean, and the collision-avoiding label placer on the transfer plot works in most states. This is close; the fail is the label collisions in the output plot (visible in the planar preset) and the transfer-plot fallback.

issues.what: Dashed reference line is drawn straight through the "B200 · 208 B" label in the DEFAULT first frame (T = 2.0) at 760 px in both themes (zoom shows the dashes over "208 B"; in light theme ink-on-ink makes the digits unreadable) and through "B200" at 360 px. Same pass-2 fallback also puts the line through "MC68000 · 68 k" (T = 1, 760), "Cerebras WSE-2" (T = 1, 360) and "8080 · 6 k" (T = 4). Fails QA criterion 4 (text never collides) on the first frame.
issues.fix: In place(): before allowing a line crossing (pass 2), add a further-out candidate ring (x±14, y±22, 'a'/'b' with 18–20 px offsets) for pri ≤ 1 labels; and give every in-place chip label a knockout halo (paint-order="stroke" stroke="var(--panel)" stroke-width="3") so a label that must cross the line or an overlay curve stays legible. Re-render the idle 760/360 frames and zoom on the top-right cluster to confirm.

issues.what: In-chart tooltip lands in the far top-left corner fallback, 300–420 px from the hovered dot, for 14 of 30 chips: the default H100 (first frame in both themes/widths), 4004, 8080, Sandy Bridge and every chip from 2017 on (GV100, A12, Rome, M1, A15, WSE-2, M1 Ultra, H100, 7950X, MI300X, B200). The scenario's own hover shots (WSE-2, 4004, B200, Rome) all show a box floating in the 1971–1985 / 1–10 T void, reading like a stray annotation; at 360 the first-frame box covers the 2017–2019 dots. Cause: corner fallback cost 1 beats any near-dot spot that covers one pri-1 + one pri-2 label (1.5), even though covered labels are hidden anyway.
issues.fix: In showTip(): exclude the selected chip's own label from the coverage cost (it duplicates the tooltip), raise the corner-fallback penalty to ~4 (or drop the corner fallbacks and take the cheapest near-dot candidate), and if the chosen box is >40 px from the dot draw a 1 px leader line (var(--line2)) from the box edge to the dot. Verify with a loop that hovers every [data-chip] and asserts box-to-dot gap < 40 px.

issues.what: Clock overlay at 760 px (both themes): the Dennard annotation's second line "V_DD stuck near 1 V, clocks stall at 3–5 GHz" runs across the right axis line and into the "10 MHz" tick label (per-state analysis reports overlap ["10 MHz","Dennard scaling ends ~2005…"]; zoom shows the axis stroke through "GHz"). The harness missed it because it only analyses the final scenario state.
issues.fix: In drawOverlay()/ann(): measure the annotation bbox and, if its right edge exceeds L + pw − 4, either anchor it to the left of the 2005 marker (left = true, text-anchor end) or re-wrap into three lines ("Dennard scaling ends ~2005:", "V_DD stuck near 1 V,", "clocks stall at 3–5 GHz"). Also render V_DD as V<tspan baseline-shift="sub" font-size="8">DD</tspan> (and V<sub>DD</sub>/V<sub>T</sub> in the HTML note) instead of a literal underscore.

issues.what: Both rotated right-axis titles ("clock frequency (approx.)", "cost per transistor, 1971 = 1 (approx.)") extend 3 px beyond the SVG's right edge (bbox right 689 px vs viewBox width 686) at 760 and 360 px, so glyph tops are clipped; the per-state check flags "svg text clipped" in both overlay states.
issues.fix: Set the rotated title's baseline at x = W − 12 (or use dominant-baseline="hanging" with x = W − 3) so the full glyph box stays inside the viewBox; re-check with getBoundingClientRect against the svg rect.

issues.what: Overlay curves cross labels that the placement never sees as obstacles: the green cost line passes through "×2 every 2.0 yr" at 760 px and through "Core 2 Duo" and "×2 every 2.0 yr" at 360 px; at 360 the "7 nm" knot label is placed on top of the flat cost line beneath the 2 nm knot so it reads as belonging to the wrong knot.
issues.fix: Sample the overlay polyline (cost curve, clock running-max line) into 4×4 cells and push them into lineCells before placing chip labels and knot labels; for knot labels at narrow widths keep only 28 nm and 2 nm (or stack them in a small key) when the knots are < 12 px apart.

issues.what: GPU dots use var(--accent) and the whole clock overlay (diamonds, dotted running-max line, axis, Dennard note) uses var(--warn); these tokens are near-identical in both themes (#F2B13B vs #F0B429 dark, #B8770A vs #C98A00 light), so the clock series reads as "GPU-coloured" and only the hollow-diamond shape separates them.
issues.fix: Use a visually distinct token for the clock overlay (e.g. var(--bad) or var(--cu)); keep the sweep cursor on --accent or switch it to --ink so it is not confused with GPU data either.

issues.what: At 360 px the formula block wraps "N₀ = 2 300" between the "2" and "300" (the thin space U+2009 is a legal break), so it reads "N₀ = 2 / 300 (Intel 4004)" in both themes.
issues.fix: Use a narrow no-break space (U+202F) or   inside numbers in the formula/readout strings, or wrap the number in <span style="white-space:nowrap">.

issues.what: During the sweep the "×2 every T yr" line label stays at full opacity out at ~2018 while the dashed line is still clipped at the cursor (see play-early/play-mid), which breaks the progressive reveal.
issues.fix: In applyCursor() dim the reference-line label (opacity 0.15) until the cursor passes the year it is anchored at, the same way dots and chip labels are dimmed.

result.praise: Data and physics are solid: all 30 chips match the spec numbers and public die/node/clock figures, the least-squares doubling time (2.10 yr, 29 chips, wafer-scale excluded) verifies independently, readouts (98 MTr/mm², 25.1 doublings, 0.73×, 617 B at 2027) are exact, the cost knots are correctly normalised from the Module 20 $/100M-transistor table, and the Dennard/cost notes track Module 11 §1.4 and Module 20 faithfully. No console errors (the only 404 is the test page's favicon), no hard-coded colours, no NaN at any slider/overlay extreme, Play/Pause/Resume/Replay states are correct and paused by default, keyboard focus reaches every dot, and remount mid-animation, theme flip and resize all pass cleanly. The 360 px layout, per-chip notes and the wafer-scale square are well done; the widget is close to passing once the label/tooltip placement is tightened.

issues.what: The payoff state is wrong at the defaults (30 mJ/cm², 110 °C, 60 s, PTD). The header promises '40 nm lines & spaces' and the readout 'LER ≈ 4 nm', but the developed cross-section shows nothing like it.
