DOM probe of the remaining resist height per 12 nm column (x = nm from the centre of the middle exposed space; nominal space = |x| < 20): at 760 px the lines are staircases of 49/80/62 nm and 67/80/91 nm height and only two columns (±6) clear to the substrate; at 560 px (a normal desktop width) the two columns at the very centre of the brightest exposed region (±6 nm, I = 0.95) keep 91 nm of resist — a pillar standing where the light is brightest — while columns at −30/−18 and +54/+66 clear; at 360 px the central space never reaches the underlayer (−6:9, +6:49, −18:32, +18:80 nm left). NTD at the same settings leaves 60–72 nm wide 'lines' and 8–20 nm 'spaces', so PTD and NTD are not complements. Root causes, from the code: (1) the latent image has almost no contrast — PAG conversion 1−exp(−E·I/25) is 45 % at the nominal edge (I = 0.5), 25 % at I = 0.24 (inside the line) and 6 % at the line centre, and every acid then deprotects all sites within R_DEP = 7 nm along its whole ±L random walk, a ~30 nm swath, so 3–5 of 8 sites per column are deprotected in the MIDDLE of the unexposed lines (probe at 560 px: column −42 nm = 3/8, column −54 = 5/8) while the middle of the exposed space is only 4/8; the 3×3 fraction f sits near 0.5 everywhere and develop becomes a coin flip; (2) develop is time-limited, not contrast-limited: T_SHOW = 1.6·FILM/R_MAX = 0.8 s (the module's puddle is 30–60 s), so any cell with f slightly below 0.5 half-dissolves and columns stop part-way (the staircases), and lines lose 20–50 % of their height while the module says protected resist dissolves at < 1 nm/s vs 100–1 000 nm/s.
issues.fix: (a) Make the chemistry threshold-like, as the module describes the quencher doing: convert I(x) to a local acid density, subtract a quencher budget (≈ the acid produced at I ≈ 0.35–0.4 for E = 30) so dark-region acids are neutralised before they deprotect, and tie each acid's reach to the walk only (R_DEP ≈ 3–4 nm: it deprotects the cell it is in as it wanders) so deprotection follows acid density instead of smearing 30 nm. Target at defaults: f ≈ 1 for |x − space centre| < ~18 nm, f ≈ 0 beyond ~22 nm, ±1 cell raggedness; at 10 mJ/cm² the spaces stay closed, at 60 the lines shrink to 1–2 cells, the 130 °C/120 s bake erases the lines, the 90 °C/30 s bake leaves partial deprotection. (b) Make develop contrast-limited: give it the real 30–60 s (T_SHOW ≥ 20·FILM/R_MAX, or simply: cells with f > 0.5 (PTD) / f < 0.5 (NTD) clear completely, the others lose ≤ 1 nm) with a steep sigmoid at f = 0.5 so PTD and NTD are exact complements; keep the ragged ±1-cell edge as the LER cue. (c) Verify with a DOM probe of column heights (fill=var(--si), fill-opacity 0.22) at 360, 560 and 760 px for both tones and all six scenario settings: at defaults every remaining line must be 3–4 cells (36–48 nm) wide at full 100 nm height and every space cleared to the underlayer over ≥ 3 cells; the three identical exposed regions must look alike.

issues.what: Deprotected (green) sites survive positive-tone develop standing in TMAH, contradicting the step text ('dissolves the deprotected, polar polymer … leaves protected polymer'). At 60 mJ/cm² the remaining stumps are single columns of green sites under one orange cap (x ≈ 470 in the 2× crop); at 130 °C/120 s a pillar of green sites stands at x ≈ 180 and the 'deprotected (polar)' callout literally points at a green site inside standing resist; at defaults green dots sit inside every remaining line. Cause: develop descends strictly column-wise (cum += tau per row) and stops at any slow cell, never removing soluble material under a cap; the lateral rule only handles a single slow cell between two fast columns.
issues.fix: Treat develop as a 2-D front: after computing per-cell rates, run a BFS/flood from the developer (top row and every cleared cell, 4-connectivity) so any soluble cell reachable through cleared neighbours dissolves in the shown time, and detached caps/islands are removed with the material under them; then pick the 'deprotected (polar)' callout target only among sites in cells that are still standing because they are protected (or hide that callout in the develop step).

issues.what: Callout leader lines cross other labels because near() accepts targets up to 240 px away: at 130 °C/120 s the 'quencher (base)' leader runs straight up through 'PAG (acid generator)' and 'protecting group'; at 360 px the 'polymer chain' and 'protecting group' leaders cross the whole film to targets at the far right, skimming the 'deprotected (polar)' label (rc-s3-ptd-done-360-light).
issues.fix: Cap the search radius at ~70–90 px, prefer targets to the right of/below the label, and hide the callout (vis(g,false)) when nothing is within range instead of stretching a leader across the drawing.

issues.what: Develop status reads 'TMAH 0.26 N · 47 %' with no noun — it is animation progress (p·100), not '% cleared' as claimed; the module gives puddle times of 30–60 s.
issues.fix: Show develop time instead: 'TMAH 0.26 N · 14 s / 30 s' (and 'n-butyl acetate · … s') so the third step has the same t / T readout style as the bake.

issues.what: Falling photon ticks start at y = 22 and are drawn over the aerial-image plot and across the 'exposed'/'unexposed' label row (visible in s1-paused and the non-reduced first frame at x ≈ 200 and 520), i.e. shapes over text.
issues.fix: Start photons at the film top (y ≈ Y0) or wrap the photon lines in a <g> with a clipPath limited to the film rectangle; keep the flash halo at the PAG.

issues.what: Colour reuse for different things: PAG dots and the developer liquid are both --accent2 (in the develop step unconverted PAG dots sit in a developer of the same hue, weakest in the light theme), and photons and acid share --accent; the standard lists identical colours for different materials as a failure.
issues.fix: Draw the developer with --line or --muted at low opacity (or a hatched pattern) and give photons a distinct look from the acid dot (e.g. thin --euv line vs filled --accent circle), then update the legend.

issues.what: The leftmost and rightmost exposed regions (aerial-image peaks at ±160 nm at 760 px, ±80 nm at 360 px) get no 'exposed' label because of the ±26 px guard, yet they deprotect and clear, so unlabeled cleared regions appear at both SVG edges.
issues.fix: Either shift the pattern phase so the SVG edges fall inside unexposed lines, or allow the edge labels (shorter text or a smaller guard) so every cleared region is labelled.

issues.what: Catalytic chain length readout spans ≈ 80 (90 °C/30 s) to ≈ 4 800 (130 °C/120 s) while the module says 'hundreds to a few thousand' (gain 10²–10³); the k(T) doubling per 10 °C is an assumption not stated in the module.
issues.fix: Scale k so the slider range lands in ~100–3 000, or add '(assumed Arrhenius, doubling per 10 °C)' to the formula box.

issues.what: The step-1 explanation is three sentences (spec asks for 1–2), and 'glass transition' in step 2 is used but only loosely defined.
issues.fix: Trim step 1 to two sentences and add a parenthetical to step 2: 'glass transition (the temperature above which the rigid polymer softens enough for small molecules to move)'.

result.praise: Mechanically clean: no widget console errors (the single 404 is the harness favicon, reproduced on yield-calculator), no hard-coded colours, no overlapping/clipped/tiny SVG text at 760 or 360 px in either theme, all SVG text measured at 11 px. Formulas and defaults match module 07 exactly (D = 0.8 nm²/s at 110 °C doubling per 10 °C, L = √(2Dt) = 9.8 nm, 13.9 nm at 120 s, 27.7 nm at 130 °C/120 s, 3.5 nm at 90 °C/30 s, chain ≈ 600, LER ≈ 4 nm, 0.26 N TMAH, n-butyl acetate NTD, RLS line). Reduced motion is genuinely respected (headless Chrome reports reduce, and the widget starts paused on completed states with 'Replay step'); with no-preference emulated it autoplays from mid-exposure and on every step change, pauses off-screen and resumes when scrolled back. Prev/Next/dots/counter/tooltips/hover state all work, exposure and bake animations are attractive and readable, and the hot/cold/under/over-exposure extremes tell the right qualitative story. The problem is confined to the latent-image contrast and the develop model, which is where the teaching payoff lives.

issues.what: Cross-section SVG: the angle label 'θ = 20.0°' is clipped off the left edge (only '| = 20.0°' is visible) whenever θ ≳ 14°. This includes the 'Collector rim, 20°' preset, in both themes and at 760 and 360 px (harness ANALYZE reports 'clipped: θ = 20.0° left=-6'). Cause: drawStack() line ~173 anchors the label text-anchor:end at x = xHit + r·cos(a1−0.5) + 2 ≈ 40 px with xHit = 58, so a ~50 px label runs past x = 0. The θ arc itself (r = 26 → 9 px of arc at 20°) is also too small to read as an angle mark. Evidence: qa/shots/verify-bragg/bragg-mirror-760-dark-theta-max-20.png, bragg-mirror-760-light-preset-collector-rim.png, x-360-dark-theta20.png.
issues.fix: Draw the θ arc between the normal and the reflected (right-hand) beam instead, with r ≈ 34, and place the label with text-anchor:start at x = xHit + 10, y = ySurf − r − 4 (or, if you keep it on the incident side, move xHit to ≥ 90 and clamp x so that x − textWidth ≥ 2). Re-run with the collector-rim preset and check the ANALYZE overflow list is empty at 360 px too.

issues.what: Chart at 360 px with 'System passband R¹¹' checked: the label 'R¹¹ FWHM 0.33 nm (2.4 %)' (drawn at x0+6, y0+26) collides with '13.5 nm ± 1 %' (drawn at X(13.635)+4, y0+26) — the rendered text reads '(2.4 %)5 nm ± 1 %'. Harness ANALYZE reports overlaps [['13.5 nm ± 1 %','R¹¹ FWHM 0.33 nm (2.4 %)']] in both themes. At 760 px they are ~10 px apart, so this is a mobile-only failure of criteria 4/5. Evidence: qa/shots/verify-bragg/x-360-dark-sys.png, x-360-light-sys.png.
issues.fix: Put the R¹¹ readout on its own row (e.g. y0 + 40, or bottom-left of the plot just above the axis at y1 − 8), or right-align it to x1 when the peak is left of centre; alternatively move the '13.5 nm ± 1 %' label to sit below the top edge inside the band only when the band is wider than the label, otherwise drop it to the axis row. Verify at 360 px with the checkbox on.

issues.what: Readouts become nonsensical when the Bragg peak leaves the 12–15 nm sweep grid, which is reachable with θ = 20° and d ≤ ~6.6 nm (λ_B = 2d·√(n̄²−sin²θ) = 11.68 nm at d = 6.5): peakOf() takes the plot-edge sample as the peak, so the widget prints 'peak reflectance 41.2 %', 'peak wavelength 12.00 nm', 'FWHM ≥ 0.09 nm (0.7 %)', the chart labels 'peak 41.2 % at 12.00 nm', and the formula box claims 'The computed peak sits 2.7 % above the Bragg estimate'. The true peak is ~68 % near 11.8 nm. Evidence: qa/shots/verify-bragg/x-760-dark-n80-d65-g5-th20.png (also x-360-*).
issues.fix: Either sweep a wider grid than you plot (e.g. compute 11.0–16.0 nm, plot 12–15, and clamp the peak/FWHM markers to the visible range with an 'off-plot' note), or detect ip === 0 || ip === NL−1 in peakOf() and then show 'peak < 12 nm (off-plot)' / '> 15 nm', blank the FWHM and the shift sentence, and omit the peak marker and FWHM bar. Also consider limiting the θ slider so λ_B stays ≥ 12 nm, but the guard in peakOf is the robust fix.

issues.what: Preset semantics: the default 'Production mirror' (d = 6.97 nm, the module's worked-example estimate) peaks at 13.62 nm, i.e. 0.9 % off 13.5 nm with R@13.5 = 71.3 %, while 'Tuned to 13.5 nm' (d = 6.91) is what a production mirror actually is. 'Period +1 %' (7.04) is then +1 % relative to an already-detuned stack, so the module's lesson ('1 % period error moves the peak 0.135 nm, a quarter of the passband') lands on the wrong baseline (R@13.5 drops from 71 % to 65 % instead of from 73 % to ~65 %).
issues.fix: Rename the first preset to something like 'Module estimate, d = 6.97 nm' (keep it as a preset, it motivates the 0.8 % shift text), make 'Tuned to 13.5 nm' the initial state (st.d = 6.91), and define 'Period +1 %' as 6.98 nm relative to the tuned mirror. Update the scenario file's reset value accordingly.

issues.what: 'Collector rim, 20°' preset shows R@13.5 = 5.4 % with no explanation that real collectors are laterally graded (larger d toward the rim) so 13.5 nm stays on-peak at every angle; a learner will conclude the rim of a real collector reflects 5 %. The widget already contains the fix (at 20° the d slider at ~7.4 nm re-centres the peak) but never says so.
issues.fix: When st.th > 5°, append one sentence to the formula box, e.g. 'At θ = 20° the peak moves to 12.72 nm; real collectors grade the period across the surface (here d ≈ 7.4 nm would be needed) so every zone reflects 13.5 nm.' Compute the needed d as st.d × 13.5 / sw.lamPk.

issues.what: The FWHM readout '0.72 nm (5.3 %)' contradicts the module's headline '~0.5 nm (~4 %)' at face value; the reconciliation (ideal sharp-interface model vs. interdiffused real stacks) is only in the long note at the bottom. Physics is correct for the stated model (independent Abelès calculation agrees to 0.001 nm), so this is a labelling issue.
issues.fix: Label the readout 'FWHM (ideal stack)' or add '(ideal; real ≈ 0.5 nm)' to the FWHM stat span, so a reader cross-checking against the module is not misled.

issues.what: Material colours swap lightness between themes: Mo stripes are var(--ink) at 0.6 opacity, so Mo is the light stripe in dark mode and the dark stripe in light mode; only the two leader labels disambiguate. Not a contrast failure, but the dense absorber should look the same in both themes.
issues.fix: Use a theme-stable pair, e.g. Mo = var(--muted) at 0.9 opacity (mid grey in both themes) and Si = var(--si) at 0.35, or add the material names to the legend row.

result.praise: The physics is exemplary: an independent Abelès/characteristic-matrix calculation reproduces every readout (peak R, peak λ, FWHM, R at 13.5 nm, the 20° shift, the 15/80-pair values and the R¹¹ passband 0.33 nm / 2.4 %) to the last printed digit, and the explanation of the 0.8 % peak shift (absorption favouring the long-λ stop-band edge, nodes in Mo) is correct and a genuinely good teaching point beyond the module's simple estimate. The standing-wave overlay is the best part of the widget — at 10–15 pairs the antinodes visibly sit in Si and the nodes in Mo, and detuning shows the wave leaking into the substrate. Hover-to-probe, adaptive label placement on the chart, halo text, ResizeObserver redraw at container width, paused-by-default sweep with IntersectionObserver, and a clean remount/cleanup all check out with no console errors and no hard-coded colours.

issues.what: Every SVG text in both drawings renders below 11 px at the harness's 360 px render. The #box there is 324 px wide and each w-grid2 column SVG is 286 px wide, so the 330-unit viewBox is scaled by 0.867: the 11.5 px labels render at 10.0 px and the 11 px annotations/mono strings at 9.5 px (38 of 38 text elements < 11 px, measured with svg.getBoundingClientRect().width / viewBox.width × font-size). The harness's tinyText check reads the unscaled CSS font-size and so misses it; the builder's claim 'text stays ≥ ~11 px at 360 px' is not true. Recently accepted step-throughs stay ≥ 11 px at the same render (damascene 11.3 px with 13 px fonts on a 330 viewBox; ald-cycle 11.9 px; yield-calculator 11 px with a 286 viewBox). At native 1x the mono 'dose 20–40 mJ/cm² · ~0.1 s per 26 × 33 mm field' line and the module labels are hard to read.
issues.fix: In site/widgets/litho-track.js raise all SVG font sizes so that size × (286/330) ≥ 11: use 13 for sans labels (mt/T/TC defaults and the station labels) and ≥ 12.7 for the MONO annotations and the 'interface'/'lens'/'ASML NXT' strings, then re-space the leader-label stack (13.5 → ~15.5 px pitch, and the 250 px bottom bound) and the multi-line annotation blocks (14 px line pitch → ~16) so nothing overlaps; alternatively shrink both viewBoxes to 286 wide and re-lay out. Verify by measuring rendered size at the 360 render (scale = svg.clientWidth / viewBox.width), not by the harness's CSS-size check.

issues.what: qa/scenarios/litho-track.json never exercises the throughput slider: the selector '#box .w-controls:nth-of-type(2) input[type=range]' matches nothing (nth-of-type counts all sibling <div>s; the second div is the w-grid2), so the 'wph-min-150' and 'wph-max-320' shots both show 275 wph and the builder's claim of testing wph min/max is unverified by the scenario. (Checked manually: 150 wph → 24 s takt, 4 plates, 3 cups, 3 600 passes/day, 3.6 L ≈ $7 200; 320 wph → 11.3 s, 8 plates, 6 cups, 7 680/day, 7.7 L ≈ $15 360; all sane.)
issues.fix: Use '#box .w-controls:last-of-type input[type=range]' (or give the throughput input an aria-label such as 'Scanner throughput' and select '#box input[aria-label="Scanner throughput"]'), re-run the harness and confirm the two shots differ.

issues.what: Step dots have no visible hover state: hovering dot 9 renders identically to its neighbours (only a delayed native title tooltip, invisible on touch). QA standard 6 asks for a visible hover state; damascene.js and ald-cycle.js add an accent outline.
issues.fix: Add pointerenter/pointerleave handlers that set outline '2px solid var(--accent)' with outlineOffset '2px' (as damascene.js line 42), or append a scoped <style> rule '.w-step-dot:hover{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px}'.

issues.what: The 'Replay animation' button is inserted/removed under the legend only on steps 3 and 9, so entering or leaving those steps shifts the calculator and throughput sections down/up by ~40 px (compare s02-barc vs s03-spin-done shots).
issues.fix: Keep the button in the flow and toggle visibility:hidden (reserving its space), or place it in the step-nav row next to Play/Pause, disabled on non-animated steps.

issues.what: 'narrowest safe line at this thickness' is silently floored at 40 nm: at 5,000 rpm (63 nm) the collapse-safe width t/2.5 is 25 nm but the readout still says 40 nm, so the stat does not respond to the slider below 100 nm and the reader cannot tell why.
issues.fix: Either show t/2.5 directly with the label 'collapse-safe line width (t / 2.5)' and note the 40 nm 193i half-pitch floor in the formula line, or relabel the stat '(≥ 40 nm, the 193i single-exposure limit)'.

issues.what: The cross-section SVG leaves its top ~35–40 % empty on steps 6 (topcoat), 8 (PEB) and 10 (rinse): the stack is anchored at the bottom and the two-line annotation sits just above it, so 90–100 of the 262 viewBox rows are blank (standard 2: 'no large blank areas').
issues.fix: Draw the annotation block from a fixed top line (y≈40) for steps without an upper drawing, or set the SVG viewBox height per step (e.g. 262 for steps 1–4/7/9/11, ~190 for 5/6/8/10) so the drawing fills the box.

issues.what: Small teaching/accuracy nits: (a) after EBR the resist still runs edge-to-edge in every later step, so the 1.5–2 mm edge exclusion the step describes never appears; (b) the 'after HMDS: θ ≈ 65°' drop is drawn as an exact hemisphere (90°); (c) step 2 says '1 nm of thickness variation becomes several nm of CD error' whereas the module says 'a few nanometers of thickness variation'; (d) several labels sit at the SVG edge with zero margin ('load port' starts at x=0, 'deprotected: soluble' and 'ASML NXT' end at x≈330, the full-width mono 'aspect ratio t/CD = … (keep ≤ 2.5 or lines fold)' line) — not clipped now but no slack for font fallback or the size bump above.
issues.fix: (a) inset the resist/topcoat rects by ~4 px per side from step 4 onward and label 'edge exclusion 1.5–2 mm'; (b) draw the primed drop as a shallower arc (e.g. 'a 16 12 0 0 1 28 0' clipped to a ~65° contact); (c) change to 'a few nm of thickness variation becomes several nm of CD error'; (d) move edge labels inward by 4–6 px and shorten the aspect-ratio line (e.g. 'AR = t/CD = 2.5 (≤ 2.5 or lines fold)').

issues.what: At 360 px the viscosity <select> truncates its option text ('2 cP (thin ArF immersio…').
issues.fix: Shorten the option names, e.g. '2 cP · thin ArF', '5 cP · ArF/KrF', '12 cP · thick KrF', '30 cP · i-line', and keep the explanation in the formula line.

result.praise: Strong, module-faithful build: every number cross-checks against module 07 (Meyerhofer scaling with 100 nm @ 2,000 rpm → 82 nm @ 3,000; ±0.5 nm per 1 %; AR 2.5 collapse limit and 3.6 MPa; 0.26 N / 2.38 wt % TMAH with 100–1,000 vs <1 nm/s; λ/2n ≈ 57 nm; HMDS reaction and 0→65°; BARC n≈1.8/κ≈0.4; dose 20–40 mJ/cm², 26×33 mm fields at 0.1 s; PEB 5–20 nm and 10²–10³ gain; takt 13.1 s → 7 plates; $2/wafer-layer; NXT:2150i ≥310 wph). My per-step analysis (11 steps × 3 stack settings × 760/360) found zero text overlaps, clipping or overflow; the stack scales cleanly from 63 nm to 548 nm resist; wph 150–320 gives sane integers; reduced motion jumps to end states with opt-in Replay and Play defaulting to paused; remount twice mid-play and cleanup are clean with no console errors; all colours are tokens and both themes are legible at 760. The first frame (exposure with mask, rays, full stack, wafer in the scanner) is genuinely informative, the moving amber wafer marker plus lit modules makes the cell map easy to follow, and the cross-section's in-place leader labels with step-specific annotations (spin-down, EBR nozzles, hot plate on pins, latent image, acid blur, dissolving spaces, capillary pull, CD/pitch dimensions) teach the process well.

issues.what: The bisection-cut label box (drawOverlay, site/widgets/nvlink-topology.js lines 153-160) is centred in the GPU-to-switch gap with a width computed from character count, and collides with graph content whenever the gap is narrower than the label: at 360 px with HGX H100 or HGX B200 + cut on, the box completely covers GPU 4 and half of chip 2 (their numbers are hidden); at 360 px NVL72 + cut on, it clips the right edge of GPU numbers 32 and 36 and overlaps the switch-tray box of S4; at 760 px with either HGX preset + cut on, it sits on top of the highlighted from-GPU -> chip 1 and chip 1 -> to-GPU path lines and hides them. Verified in zoomed 2x crops in both themes (the harness only toggles the cut at 760 px on NVL72, so its overlap check never saw these states). Violates criteria 4 (text never collides) and 5 (works at 360 px).
issues.fix: Do not float the label in the gap. Reserve a second bottom line for it: set `bot` in layout() to 40 (or 24 + 16 when st.cut) and draw the bisection text centred under the '1 296 links' caption, e.g. `bisection cut (dashed): 36 <-> 36 GPUs, 64.8 TB/s across the cut` in var(--bad), keeping only the dashed line in the graph. Alternatively keep the in-gap box but measure it (getComputedTextLength after append) and, when `bw > (L.sx0 - L.gx1) - 8`, fall back to the bottom-line placement. Also add scenario steps that toggle the cut on the HGX presets so the state is screenshotted.

issues.what: Legend text 'from-GPU ports (one link per chip)' (line 68) is hard-coded but is only true for the NVL72 presets; on HGX H100 each highlighted line stands for 5/4/4/5 links per chip and on HGX B200 for 9 links per chip, so the legend contradicts the path note and the chip tooltips.
issues.fix: Make the legend item dynamic in update(): reuse the perTxt computation (`1 link` / `9 links` / `5/4/4/5 links`) and set the legend span text to `from-GPU ports (${perTxt} per chip)`; keep the span in a variable so update() can set textContent.

issues.what: At 360 px the 'Aggregate NVLink bandwidth of one domain, compared' bars (lines 71, 241-246) are only 32 px wide because the nowrap label 'Vera Rubin NVL72 (roadmap)' consumes the grid row, so the bar chart conveys nothing (7.2 TB/s renders as a 2 px sliver next to a 16 px bar).
issues.fix: At narrow widths (W < 400, or a container query on cmp's width) switch the grid to two rows per system: label + value on one line, full-width bar underneath (gridTemplateColumns: '1fr auto' with the bar spanning both columns); or drop whiteSpace: nowrap on the labels and use short names ('VR NVL72*'). Aim for bar tracks >= 120 px at 360 px.

issues.what: Vera Rubin note (line 25) says 'A two-rack "NVL72x2" stopgap was floated and dropped in 2026 - copper still stops at ~1.5 m.' Module 19 attributes the NVL72x2 back-to-back stopgap to the delayed Kyber / Rubin Ultra rack and says it was dropped after customer pushback (midplane-PCB manufacturability), not to Vera Rubin NVL72 and not because of copper reach.
issues.fix: Reword to match the module: 'Kyber (Rubin Ultra, 2027-28) is the next step; a back-to-back NVL72x2 stopgap for it was dropped after customer pushback.' Keep the copper-reach sentence separate and factual ('copper still reaches only ~1-1.5 m, so the domain stays one rack').

issues.what: The 'all other links' legend swatch (line 70: 12 x 2 px at opacity 0.4) is practically invisible in both themes, and the 1 296-line mesh it refers to (lines 107-109, one path at 0.2 opacity) renders as a grey wash with moire diamonds in the dark theme rather than as recognisable lines, so the 'every GPU is wired to every switch tray' structure is carried only by the highlighted pair.
issues.fix: Raise the swatch to 3 px / opacity 0.7. For the mesh, consider drawing tray-level bundles (18 trays x 9 switch trays = 162 lines at ~0.3 opacity) as the base layer, which reads as an all-to-all bipartite graph, and keep the per-chip fan-out only for the highlighted from/to GPUs.

issues.what: st.hover is not reset when the graph is redrawn by the ResizeObserver (line 277), so if the user is hovering a GPU during a resize the old hovered index stays in effect (path note and highlight show the stale hovered GPU instead of the selected 'from' GPU) until the next mouseenter/leave.
issues.fix: Set `st.hover = -1` at the top of drawGraph() (or in the RO callback before calling drawGraph).

result.praise: Strong widget overall: the bipartite graph plus rack/baseboard inset teaches the NVL72 topology at a glance; all numbers match Module 19 exactly (1.8 TB/s per GPU, 129.6 TB/s aggregate, 64.8 TB/s bisection, 1 296 links = 18 x 72 switch ports, 5 184 cables vs the quoted ~5 000, HGX H100 5/4/4/5 spread with 144/256 ports, HGX B200 exactly full at 144/144); formula box, readouts with units, comparison bars, hover/click/from/to/swap, same-GPU edge case, roadmap starring and the Play/Pause + reduced-motion + IntersectionObserver behaviour all work as claimed with no console errors, no hard-coded colors, and legible 11 px text at 1:1 viewBox scale in both themes and at 360 px. Choosing Vera Rubin NVL72 (formerly 'NVL144', one rack) over the spec's 'two-rack NVL144' is the right call per the module and the note explains the renaming.

issues.what: Default CCP state (500 W bias, 20 mTorr, 1000 W source) lands in the widget's own 'λ < s → collisional: ions scatter … Anisotropy degrades' tier: s = 6.0 mm vs λ = 2.7 mm, 2.2 collisions/crossing, 11 % unscattered, ±19.5°. This contradicts module 09's Key Numbers ('Sheath thickness ~0.1 to a few mm — thinner than the ion mean free path, so ions arrive within a few degrees of vertical') and the widget's own framing of CCP as 'the platform for dielectric etch' at 10–200 mTorr. Worse, the model puts the CCP in the collisional tier across its ENTIRE nominal window at default bias (10 mTorr: s/λ = 1.06; 20: 2.2; 50: 5.9; 200: 26.6), and even at 10 mTorr/200–300 W bias only reaches ~50 % unscattered. A learner therefore never sees a CCP make the straight ion beam the module describes; the first frame teaches the opposite of the module's headline point (QA criteria 2 and 3: 'cross-check key defaults against the course module'). (site/widgets/plasma-reactor.js: MODES.ccp.def, calc(), tier thresholds at line ~262.)
issues.fix: Make the default CCP state (and most of its 10–100 mTorr window at moderate bias) collisionless or mostly collisionless, e.g. (a) use the collisional-sheath thickness when λ < s (the note already admits the collisionless Child–Langmuir sheath is too thick there), and/or (b) raise CCP density per kW (dual-frequency 60 MHz CCPs reach ~10¹⁰–10¹¹) or lower ETA / raise A_EFF so V_dc at 500 W is a few hundred volts, and/or (c) pick CCP defaults such as 300 W / 10 mTorr; then re-tune tier thresholds (e.g. collisional only when s/λ > 1.5). Also consider noting that charge-exchange collisions create slow ions that re-accelerate along E, so anisotropy degrades gradually rather than being 'lost'. Re-render and confirm the default 'Now:' sentence reads collisionless/mostly collisionless for CCP.

issues.what: Text collides with a shape in every frame, both themes and both modes: the 'walls grounded' label (x 38→~130 in viewBox units, baseline y 428) runs into the blocking-capacitor top plate (x 125–145, y 426) and the RF feed line at x = 135; the final 'd' visibly overlaps the plate (confirmed in a 3× zoom of the bottom of the chamber SVG). Spec rule 8 / QA criterion 4 ('text must not overlap shapes or other labels'). The harness misses it because it only checks text-vs-text.
issues.fix: Move the ground symbol and label away from the RF feed: e.g. draw the ground symbol at the chamber's bottom-left corner but put the label above it (txt(14, 408, 'walls grounded') outside the wall) or anchor the label to the right of the ground symbol at y ≈ 442 below the capacitor plates; alternatively shift the whole RF feed (CX) 25 px right for the capacitor/generator stack only. Re-zoom to verify no glyph touches the plate or feed line.

issues.what: At the 360 px render the chamber SVG (viewBox 360 wide) is only ~288 px wide, so its 12.5 px labels render at ~10 px and the 12 px mono values (n, Tₑ, Vₚ, 's = X mm', 'E') at ~9.6 px — under the 11 px minimum at rendered size (spec rule 8). The harness's tiny-text check reads the attribute value, not the scaled size, so it reports nothing.
issues.fix: Scale chamber font sizes with the container (e.g. fs = 12.5 × clamp(360 / el.clientWidth, 1, 1.25) in the ResizeObserver, re-setting font-size on the text nodes), or follow yield-calculator.js and set the viewBox width equal to the CSS pixel width at narrow widths so labels stay 11–12 px.

issues.what: The ion-angle model saturates: θ = θ₀ + (1−e^(−s/λ))·20° caps at ~±21°, so 2.2 collisions/crossing (±19.5°, 20 mTorr) and 26.6 collisions (±21.5°, 200 mTorr) produce visually identical 'Ion angles at the wafer' curves. The pressure → angular-spread lesson the spec asks for is barely visible between 20 and 200 mTorr, and a 26-collision sheath should be close to isotropic, not ±21°.
issues.fix: Let the spread keep growing with s/λ toward a diffusive limit (e.g. broad component half-width 20° + 30°·(1−e^(−s/λ·0.25))), or better, draw a two-component IAD: f₀ × narrow Gaussian (θ₀) plus (1−f₀) × broad pedestal — this is physically truer and makes 2 vs 26 collisions look different. Also consider making the 'mostly collisionless' tier boundary s/λ ≤ 0.5 (currently it is used down to 37 % unscattered).

issues.what: At low-source/high-bias extremes the collisionless Child–Langmuir law gives sheath thicknesses of 21.5 mm (CCP 1500 W/100 W) and 28.6 mm (CCP 500 W/100 W), which the readouts, 'Now:' text and formula block state as fact. The module says sheaths are '0.1 to a few mm' and the widget's own mode text says the plates are 'a few centimetres apart', so a 2–3 cm sheath contradicts both.
issues.fix: When s > λ use the collisional sheath law (s ∝ λ_i^(1/5) … or simply s_coll ≈ s_CL·(λ/s_CL)^(0.4)) which is much thinner, and/or add a density floor from bias power (the 2 MHz bias sustains its own plasma), and clamp the displayed s to ≤ ~10 mm with a note 'sheath would fill most of the gap' if exceeded.

issues.what: In the 'Sheath vs. mean free path' gauge the bar value labels are drawn across the vertical 10 mm / 100 mm gridlines (visible for '6.0 mm' at default and clearly for '21.5 mm' / '28.6 mm' in the extreme shots, both themes).
issues.fix: Shorten the gridlines to tick marks below the bars (y 66–72) instead of running from y 26 to 66 behind the labels, or give the value text a panel-coloured background rect.

issues.what: Top-right source labels float away from what they name: '60 MHz source' is end-anchored at x = 360, flush against the SVG's right edge with zero margin, ~100 px away from the '~' generator symbol at x = 228; in ICP mode 'ICP coil · 13.56 MHz' and 'quartz window' sit at the top-right with no leader to the copper coil turns or the dashed window, and the coil has no visible connection to any generator.
issues.fix: Place the 60 MHz label beside the generator symbol (e.g. txt(240, 30, '60 MHz source', {anchor:'start'})) and end-anchor any right-edge text at x ≤ 356; in ICP mode add short leaders from the two labels to the nearest coil turn (x 218, y 42) and the window rect (y 57), or place 'quartz window' inside/just below the dashed rect and put a small '~' generator on the coil.

issues.what: Scenario and slider cosmetics: (1) qa/scenarios/plasma-reactor.json starts with {click: play}, which only works because this headless environment reports prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (widget starts paused); in a normal environment the same click PAUSES the animation and every subsequent 'playing' shot is a frozen frame. (2) The log pressure slider has step 0.01, so setMode writes 1.30103 which snaps to 1.30 → on first touch the readout jumps from '20 mTorr (2.67 Pa)' to '20 mTorr (2.66 Pa)' and 5 mTorr becomes 4.99.
issues.fix: (1) Drop the initial Play click and instead rely on the pre-simulated first frame, or add a second scenario shot documenting the toggle either way; (2) use step 0.001 on the pressure slider (or round st.p to 3 significant figures) so preset values round-trip exactly.

result.praise: The physics chain is genuinely correct and fully cited with live numbers: λ = kT/(√2πd²p) reproduces 2.7 mm at 20 mTorr, Bohm velocity 2.5–3.3 km/s, Γ = 0.61·n·u_B ≈ 2×10¹⁵ cm⁻²s⁻¹ and 0.26–0.35 mA/cm² at 10¹⁰ cm⁻³ match the module's worked example, the 1500 W CCP bias lands at 1.24 keV (module: −1,200 V self-bias), ICP spans 25–187 eV (module: 20–200 eV), λ_D ≈ 130–160 µm, and the Child–Langmuir form is the standard one. Every readout has units and sane precision with no NaN/Infinity at any slider extreme; the harness report is clean (no overlaps, overflow, tiny-text flags or hard-coded colours; the only console entry is the harness page's favicon 404). Both themes are legible, the 360 px layout collapses to one column without spilling, the CCP↔ICP toggle rebuilds the top of the chamber (showerhead + 60 MHz generator vs quartz window + copper coil turns) with aria-pressed, Play/Pause reflects state, reduced motion starts paused on a pre-simulated meaningful frame, remounts do not multiply rAF loops, and the loop stops completely offscreen. The 'Now:' sentence and the ICP bias-max frame (a row of ions falling straight through a 0.77 mm sheath) are exactly the kind of teaching visual the standard asks for.

issues.what: SVG text renders below the 11 px minimum in BOTH layouts (WIDGET_SPEC rule 8, QA criterion 4). Measured font-size × (rendered SVG width / viewBox width): at the 760 px harness width the SVG is 686 px wide and text is 10.4 px (mono, fs 11.5) / 10.8 px (sans, fs 12); at 640–700 px windows 10.1–10.4 px; on the real page (article 760 max − 64 padding − 36 widget-body padding ≈ 658 px SVG) 10.4/10.8 px; at 360 px (SVG 286 px, fs 12.5/13) only 9.4 px / 9.8 px. The harness tinyText check passes only because it reads user units, not rendered px. Root cause in site/widgets/implanter-beamline.js relayout() (line ~352): fs = 11.2·VBW/cw uses el.clientWidth, which includes the widget-body's 36 px horizontal padding so the SVG is narrower than cw; the 11.2 target is itself < 11; mono text is fs − 0.5; and Math.round(...·2)/2 rounds down.
issues.fix: In relayout() size from the real SVG width (stage.clientWidth, or el.clientWidth − 36) and target ≥ 11.5 px for the smaller (mono) size, e.g. const sw = stage.clientWidth || cw − 36; const vbw = m === 'wide' ? 760 : 380; fs = Math.min(20, Math.max(12, Math.ceil(2 * 12 * vbw / sw) / 2)); keep fsm = fs − 0.5 (≥ 11.5 user units at 760 means ≥ 11 px rendered). Expect fs ≈ 14 in wide mode at 658–686 px and ≈ 16 in narrow at 286 px; then re-check that 'suppression electrode'/'ground electrode', '+200 kV → 230 keV', 'End station · ~10⁻⁶ torr', 'Faraday cup', and the mass-panel row labels still fit without overlap (nudge label anchors or shorten to 'suppression'/'ground' if needed), and verify with getComputedStyle(text).fontSize × svgWidth/viewBoxWidth ≥ 11 at 360 and 760.

issues.what: Slider extremes give non-sensible readouts: dose 1e12 cm⁻² at 30 mA shows beam time '0 s' (actual 3.8 ms; see qa/shots/implanter-beamline-760-dark-dose-min-1e12.png), and 10 µA at 1e16 shows '≈ 0 wph' (actual 0.02 wph). fmtTime() (line 111) rounds sub-second values to 0 and the wph formatter (line 124) rounds to 0.
issues.fix: In fmtTime add a ms branch: s < 1 ? fmt(s * 1000, s < 0.01 ? 2 : 1) + ' ms' : … ; for wph show two significant figures without a 0-decimal round when < 1 (e.g. '≈ 0.02 wph', or '< 0.1 wph').

issues.what: Analyser-field readout and the in-drawing label disagree in rounding: at B⁺ 5 kV the readout says '0.096 T' while the SVG says 'B = 0.10 T for ¹¹B⁺'; at P⁺ 5 kV '0.162 T' vs 'B = 0.16 T'.
issues.fix: In updateTexts() (line 274) format B with the same rule as updateReadouts: phys.B.toFixed(phys.B < 0.2 ? 3 : 2).

issues.what: Hovering any part changes the info panel from 2 to 3 lines (83 → 104 px measured at 760 px), so the note, dose controls and readouts jump ~21 px on every hover/unhover.
issues.fix: Give the info div a minHeight that fits the longest part text at each width (e.g. minHeight '104px' at ≥ 600 px, ~'150px' below), or fix its height and let the text scroll; keep the hotspot info from reflowing the page.

issues.what: Off-scale ('hit the wall') ions do not stop at a wall: their radius is clamped to R ± 40 px with a shifted arc centre, so the heavy-ion path (r = 130) leaves the drawn 90° sector past its exit face and its red flash lands in empty space at wide (242, 282), beside the lower slit plate under 'm/Δm ≈ 80' (visible in qa/shots/…-species-B.png and the 360 px shots as a stray red dot right of the slit), while the light-ion path stops mid-pole at (162, 202).
issues.fix: In makePath()/drawWafer() end off-scale trajectories where they cross the pole gap boundary (distance 56 or 124 from the magnet centre (CX, MY)), or draw the beam-pipe wall arcs at those radii and stop the dashed path and flash there so the 'wall' is visibly a wall.

issues.what: Hotspot highlight borders cut through labels: the End-station hotspot (580–714 × 170–330) passes through 'tilt 7°' and bisects 'Faraday cup' (overlaps 14 px and 13 px), and the magnet hotspot's bottom edge touches the 'Analyser magnet' label (see scratch hover crops / qa/shots/…-hover-wafer.png).
issues.fix: Shrink or extend the hotspot rects so their edges clear text: e.g. end-station hot(580,170,708,330) plus a separate Faraday rect starting at x 712, and move 'tilt' label inside or outside the box consistently; magnet hot(60,140,204,288).

result.praise: Physics is right and matches the module: B = √(2mV/q)/r gives 0.50 T for ⁴⁹BF₂⁺ at 30 kV and r = 0.35 m; the 90°-sector + drift dispersion x ≈ (r+L)·Δm/2m with a ±3.75 mm slit is a consistent m/Δm ≈ 80; ⁷⁴Ge⁺ lands 4.0 mm from ⁷⁵As⁺, ¹⁰B⁺ 27 mm from ¹¹B⁺; BF₂⁺ boron share 11/49 → 6.7 keV; t = Q·q·A/I gives 5.7 s for 1e15 at 20 mA; isotope ratios (Ge, B) are the real abundances. All spec elements are present and labelled in place (source with gas inlet/cathode/plasma, suppression + ground electrodes, Cu/Si analyser magnet with live B, resolving slit, column with live V_col → keV, scanner, corrector, end station with tilted 300 mm wafer, tilt arc, Faraday cup) plus a genuinely good mass-landing panel with row-stacked labels that never overlap across all five species. Narrow 360 px relayout (x/y swap) works with no horizontal overflow; hover/focus/tap hotspots work in both layouts; reduced motion starts paused on a warmed-up frame; rAF stops off-screen and resumes; unmount/remount mid-animation is clean; tokens only; the only harness 'error' is the test page's favicon.ico 404, not the widget. Rerun the harness and the rendered-size check after the font fix and this should pass.

issues.what:
readGlossary() drops every glossary entry emitted as a loose list item. The current course/modules/21-glossary-and-reference.md has worked-example blockquotes between list items, so marked/build.js renders 111 of the 281 entries as

  • term … (Module NN)

    • . Lines 75-76 of site/widgets/glossary-flashcards.js require li.firstElementChild to be STRONG, so those items are skipped silently. Verified by rendering the current md with marked and mounting: the widget reports '170 terms read live from the Module 21 glossary', the deck map jumps from C straight to N (letters D-M missing), and the per-module bar counts are wrong, with no warning to the user. site/content.js is stale (built before the worked examples were added and it does not yet contain this widget's placement), so the integrator's required `node build.js` will trigger this on the first real deployment. The spec wording is 'list items whose first is the term', not 'whose first child is '.
issues.fix:
In readGlossary(), treat a leading

as the item's container: `let host = li; let first = li.firstElementChild; if (first && first.tagName === 'P') { host = first; first = host.firstElementChild; } if (!first || first.tagName !== 'STRONG') return;` then collect definition nodes from first.nextSibling to the end of host AND, when host !== li, the remaining siblings of the

inside li (so any trailing text/paragraphs are kept); apply the leading-dash strip and the trailing '(Modules? NN, NN)' regex to the last text node of that combined node list. Re-test by mounting with COURSE built from the current md (marked.parse of course/modules/21-glossary-and-reference.md) and assert 'Card 1 / 281' and letters A-Y all present in the A->Z deck map; consider adding that check to the scenario or a comment in the file so the loose-list case is not regressed.

issues.what: At 360 px with the real 241-term glossary (20 modules, pitch ~16 px) the staggered per-bar value labels of neighbouring modules collide when the two bars differ in height by roughly one stagger step: '10 14' (modules 02/03), '20 22' (12/13), '10 12' (14/15) and '19 20' (16/17) render touching and read as 1014 / 2022 / 1012 / 1920 in both themes (0.9 px horizontal overlap, 10-11 px vertical overlap; visible in the 2x crops qa/shots/gf-verify/live/zoom-bars-360-*.png). The harness misses it because its overlap threshold is 2 px. Fails criterion 4 (text never collides) in the widget's main data state on a phone.
issues.fix: In drawBars(), when `stagger` is true (pitch0 < 19 px) either omit the per-bar value labels entirely and rely on the y-axis ticks plus the existing <title> tooltip, or place them collision-aware: track the previous label's x-range and y; if the new label's x-range overlaps it and |dy| < 12 px, lift the new label by another 11-12 px (and extend PT accordingly). Alternatively label only the selected bar and bars with n >= maxN/2 at narrow widths. Re-render at 360 px with content.js injected (the default harness only exercises the 50-term fallback, whose two-digit labels are sparse enough to hide this).

issues.what: Quiz masking leaves the answer visible when the term is glued to a suffix: HBM's definition still shows 'HBM3E and HBM4 are current', LELE shows 'LELELE', CVD shows 'LPCVD … PECVD … SACVD', CoW/WoS show 'CoWoS'. The regex in maskNode() requires a non-alphanumeric character after the word, so 'HBM3E' is not masked. 8 of 241 live terms are affected (4 real giveaways).
issues.fix: For all-caps/acronym tokens (>=3 chars matching /^[A-Z0-9]+$/) build the alternative without the trailing (?![A-Za-z0-9]) lookahead, or mask the whole alphanumeric token that contains the acronym: e.g. replace `/(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])(HBM)[A-Za-z0-9]*/gi` so 'HBM3E' becomes '____'. Keep the word-boundary rule for ordinary words so 'bumps' and 'masks' are not over-masked.

issues.what: The deck-map hover cue (stroke var(--accent), 2 px) is identical to the current-card outline, so while hovering a square the user cannot tell which of the two accented squares is the current card (qa/shots/gf-verify/live/zoom-map-hover-760-dark.png shows two identical yellow outlines).
issues.fix: Use a distinct hover style for `.fc-map rect.cell:hover`, e.g. `stroke: var(--ink); stroke-width: 2` or `filter: brightness(1.25)`, and keep the accent outline exclusively for the current card; optionally add a hover style for `.fc-bars rect.bar` too since bars are also clickable.

issues.what: The fallback note hard-codes 'reads the full glossary of ~240 terms'; the current module 21 md has 281 entries, so the number will be wrong after the next build.
issues.fix: Drop the count: 'On the Module 21 page the trainer reads the full glossary.' or compute nothing and keep the sentence generic.

issues.what: Deck-map squares and module bars are click-only SVG rects (no tabindex/keydown), so those two navigations are not keyboard-accessible (spec rule 11). The Prev/Next buttons and Letter/Module selects cover the same functions, so this is not blocking.
issues.fix: Add `tabindex: 0`, `role: 'button'` and a keydown handler (Enter/Space -> same click action) on `.cell` and `.bar` rects, with a visible `:focus-visible` outline, or leave as is and note that the selects/buttons are the accessible path.

result.praise: Solid, complete implementation of the spec: both Flashcards and Quiz me modes work end to end with right/wrong highlighting and verdicts; letter, module (with course titles) and order filters all behave; progress persists in localStorage under s2g:flash with a working Reset; the deck map and stacked per-module chart are genuinely useful mastery views and the bar-click filter is a nice touch; inline HTML from definitions is preserved; the fallback deck is verbatim course text with an honest note; formula box and readouts are correct (mastery = knew / (knew + missed), 25 % chance level); tokens only, both themes legible, reduced motion respected, ResizeObserver debounced with cleanup, no globals, remount-safe, zero console errors, and the scenario file is thorough. The main gap is that the harness never exercises the live-glossary path, which is where the parser and the 360 px bar labels break.

issues.what: Displayed per-layer arithmetic does not multiply out for the two computed resistances: the ladder row shows 'Water film 0.007 K/W' but the band is '+8.8 °C' (actual R = 0.00733), and 'Coolant warms 0.004 K/W' with '+4.9 °C' (actual R = 0.0041). The hover text writes it out explicitly: 'ΔT = 1200 W × 0.007 K/W = 8.8 °C' and '× 0.004 K/W = 4.9 °C', which a learner checking the ΔT = P·R lesson will see as 8.4 and 4.8.
issues.fix: In site/widgets/heat-path.js compute() (line 54, mk() sub label) and paintHover() (line 127, the 'math' string) format R with enough digits that P·R reproduces the shown ΔT, e.g. use a 4-decimal formatter (f4 => (+n).toFixed(4)) for R_film and R_cal (or for all layers), so the row reads '0.0073 K/W' and the hover reads 'ΔT = 1200 W × 0.0073 K/W = 8.8 °C'.

issues.what: At GPU power 1400 W / 40 °C inlet the ΣR readout shows '0.032 K/W' coloured red against a budget that also displays '0.032 K/W' (actual 0.0324 vs 0.0321), so the widget appears to flag 0.032 > 0.032.
issues.fix: In update() (line 280) either show ΣR and the budget with 4 decimals, or colour the stat red only when the values differ after rounding to the displayed precision (e.g. compare f3(res.sumR) > f3(res.budget)).

issues.what: The 'Coolant warms' layer has no visible hover state in the cross-section panel: its hit target is a transparent rect (drawA lines 181 and 207) that is not registered with hl(), so only the ladder band highlights while the hoses/supply/return labels do not.
issues.fix: Register the supply/return pipe paths (or the supply/return pills' rects) with hl(elm, 'cal') so paintHover() outlines them, or give the transparent rect a stroke via hl() so the hovered region is outlined in panel A like every other layer.

issues.what: The CDU's plate heat exchanger is drawn as two large zigzags that read as the letter 'W' (easily misread as 'watts') and the 'water in Cu microchannels →' label pill covers most of the 28 px microchannel cavity, so the channel geometry is barely visible under it.
issues.fix: In drawA (lines 189 and 170–173) draw the exchanger as a small labelled 'HX' block with alternating thin stripes (or add a tiny 'HX' text beside it), and move the microchannel label above or below the cavity (or shrink it to 'microchannels →' at the cavity's right edge) so the fins and water remain visible.

issues.what: Wording nits: the ΣR label reads 'ΣR junction → coolant inlet (budget (85 − 40) ÷ 1200 = 0.037 K/W)' with nested parentheses, and in air mode the rack stat says 'heat from an NVL72 rack of 72 such GPUs' even for the H100 air preset (no NVL72 of H100s exists).
issues.fix: Use a separator instead of nesting, e.g. 'ΣR junction → coolant inlet · budget (85 − 40) ÷ 1200 = 0.037 K/W', and in air mode label the stat 'heat from a 72-GPU rack of such GPUs (+ CPUs + switches)'.

result.praise: Strong widget. The cross-section is a recognisable, in-place-labelled package/cold-plate/CDU (and heatsink/CRAH) stack with the junction correctly on the flipped die face, and the temperature ladder makes the series-resistance idea visible at a glance. The physics is right and chains cleanly: ΔT = P·R per layer, half the coolant rise counted against the junction, CDU approach = P_rack/UA, and the numbers match module 19 (0.033 K/W budget quoted, dried TIM2 +0.010 K/W = +12 °C at 1,200 W pushes T_j from 78.9 to 90.9 °C, rack flow 161 L/min at a 9.8 °C rise vs the module's 160 L/min at 10 °C). Every slider extreme in both modes gives sane, readable output; no SVG text overlaps, clipping or pill overflow at 760 or 360 px in either theme (verified mechanically at seven extreme states beyond the scenario); reduced-motion starts paused, the rAF loop stops when paused or off-screen and resumes on return, remounting twice is clean, and there are no console errors or hard-coded colours.

issues.what: 3-deck string-stacking animation (step 4) teaches the wrong process. In site/widgets/nand-3d-build.js line 113, depth = clamp(a*(built-1)*DH - (built-1-i)*DH, 0, DH) drills the TOP deck first (deck 3 during a∈[0,0.5]) and then continues down into deck 2 (a∈[0.5,1]) as one continuous 2-deck-deep hole, while line 111 leaves deck 2 unlined until a>=1 and line 122-125 puts the carbon hard mask on deck 3 while deck 2 is being drilled. The annotation (line 155-156) reads 'etching… 5.8 / 6.3 µm' while the drawn hole spans almost two decks. This is exactly the single deep etch that string stacking exists to avoid; physically deck 2 is etched and lined before deck 3 is deposited. It affects the SK hynix 321-layer (flagship) and YMTC presets and the '3 decks' select whenever motion is allowed or 'Replay animation' is clicked (reduced-motion harness shots hide it; my mid-frames three-s4-mid1/2 confirm it). 2-deck case is correct.
issues.fix: Etch only the topmost deck and show all lower decks already lined: depth = (i === built-1) ? a*DH : DH; lined = s >= 3 && !(s === 4 && i === built-1 && a < 1); keep the hard mask on topBuilt. (Or animate sequentially deck-by-deck, etching then lining deck 2 before deck 3 appears, and scale the depth readout per deck.)

issues.what: Two pairs of legend colours are indistinguishable in both themes: polysilicon uses --accent (#F2B13B dark / #B8770A light) and the Al₂O₃/TiN liner uses --warn (#F0B429 / #C98A00); tungsten uses --ink at 0.72 opacity (≈#AAB0B9 dark / ≈#5A6270 light) and the carbon hard mask uses --muted (#97A3B3 / #5E6B7A). In the 'Inside one hole' panel at steps 8-9 the liner ring around the W band is the same orange as the poly channel two layers away, so a reader who consults the legend reads the liner as polysilicon. 'Identical-looking colors for different materials' is an explicit failure in WIDGET_QA_STANDARD.md.
issues.fix: Use --accent2 (violet) for the Al₂O₃/TiN liner (legend line 316 and drawB line 183), and give the hard mask a distinct treatment (e.g. --line fill with a dashed --muted stroke, or drop it from the legend since it is labelled in place at line 125).

issues.what: Panel B 'pitch 42 nm' label (drawB line 187) sits beside the second word-line band with no bracket, so it reads as if the word-line band were 42 nm; a non-expert cannot see that the pitch spans one oxide + one nitride band.
issues.fix: Draw a small bracket/dimension line to the left of the bands spanning from the top of one oxide band to the top of the next (42 nm × BPX = 67 px) and anchor the label to it.

issues.what: Deck-junction zoom (step 4, drawB lines 198-208) is hard to read: the 'plug' is a full-width orange band from BX1 to BXMAX that looks like a word line, and the caption says 'upper hole lands ~25 nm off-centre' while the drawing keeps the upper half at the reference and shifts the LOWER half by the overlay.
issues.fix: Confine the plug rect to the span between the upper and lower poly channels (x from BX1+T_BLOCK+T_TRAP+T_TUN)·PXNM to the lower channel's right edge), and either shift the upper half by ov instead of the lower or reword the caption to 'holes of the two decks are ~25 nm off-centre'.

issues.what: At step 1-3 with few layers per deck the array panel is mostly empty: at 32 layers (1 or 2 decks) the drawn stack is 56 px of a 340-unit panel and the rest is a dashed ghost outline plus blank space (layers-min-32 shot); at the default 143×2 the first frame is a 90 px stack under a 95 px empty ghost box.
issues.fix: Raise the minimum deck height (e.g. 80-90 px) and/or let the ghost boxes shrink so the drawn deck takes a larger share of the vertical space at low layer counts.

issues.what: Panel B rotated layer labels ('blocking oxide ~5 nm', 'SiN charge trap ~6 nm', 'tunnel oxide ~6 nm') are 14 units tall inside 14.5-17.4 unit wide layers (PXNM 2.9); their bounding boxes overlap by 1-2 px and touch the band edges; at 360 px they are 11 px glyphs inside 11.5 px bands (m360 shots) — legible but at the limit.
issues.fix: Raise PXNM to ~3.4 (hole half at 130 nm still fits if BXMAX clip is kept) or drop the '~N nm' suffix from the rotated text and list thicknesses in the left column.

issues.what: Step explanations run to 3 long sentences (~75-90 words; steps 1 and 8) against the spec's 1-2 sentences; at 360 px step 1 alone is 11 lines of text before the drawing.
issues.fix: Trim each step's d to two sentences and move tool names / secondary facts to the toolLine or the w-note.

issues.what: Step 2 zoom label 'fluorocarbon polymer walls' describes something that is not drawn (the hole is a plain panel-coloured rect), and the 'inter-deck plug' label (line 151) is shown during the step-4 etch animation before any plug exists.
issues.fix: Draw a thin --muted stripe along the hole wall at step 2 (or drop the label), and gate the 'inter-deck plug' label on the upper deck being lined.

result.praise: Physics and numbers check out against module 15 §10-12: SK hynix preset gives 345 tiers, 13.8 µm, 76:1 AR, 1.14 bn strings; default 143×2 (Samsung V9) gives 12.7 µm, 93:1, 63 min, 352 chambers, 26 litho passes, all consistent with the formulas shown in .w-formula. All spec elements are present (nine steps incl. slit, nitride strip, W fill, staircase, string stacking; layer/pitch/hole/deck/cryo controls; five vendor presets). No console errors (only the test page's favicon 404), no hard-coded colours, no clipped text, SVG text ≥11.1 px at 360 px, controls wrap cleanly at 360 px, reduced-motion is honoured (paused + 'Play animation'), autoplay and Replay work with motion allowed, remount/cleanup is safe. The 2-deck etch, nitride-strip and W-fill animations and the staircase/slit/BEOL frames are clear and read well in both themes.

issues.what: Rule-of-ten caption prints a nonsense stage cost on the Chiplet preset: per-die cost is 10 s × $0.030/s ÷ 8 = $0.0375, so the caption reads "final test (a package, substrate and assembly slot) ~$0, board test ~$4, system test ~$38, the field ~$375" (site/widgets/wafer-sort-sim.js line 291 uses fmt(perDie*10, 0)). "$0" contradicts the very point the caption makes (each stage costs ~10× more) and violates QA criterion 3 (sane precision) in a one-click preset state. Confirmed in qa/shots/wafer-sort-sim-760-*-preset-chiplet-8-sites.png and by DOM readback.
issues.fix: In paint() format every rule-of-ten stage with the same adaptive rule already used for cpg, e.g. `const money = v => '$' + fmt(v, v < 10 ? 2 : 0);` and write `${money(perDie)} … ${money(perDie*10)}, board test ~${money(perDie*100)}, system test ~${money(perDie*1000)}, the field ~${money(perDie*10000)}` so sub-$10 values show two decimals ($0.38, $3.75) and larger ones stay whole dollars.

issues.what: hms() rounds the small unit independently of the large one, so it prints "4 h 60 min" (Chiplet preset, 8 sites, Test time = 103 s) and "9 h 60 min" (207 s), and can print "N min 60 s"; the elapsed-time line in the progress text passes through the same states while animating. Found by sweeping the test-time slider 1–300 s via puppeteer (<local-scratch>/wss-probe.js).
issues.fix: Line 39: round to the smallest displayed unit first, then carry: `const hms = s => { s = Math.round(s); if (s >= 3600) { const m = Math.round(s / 60); return Math.floor(m / 60) + ' h ' + String(m % 60).padStart(2, '0') + ' min'; } if (s >= 60) return Math.floor(s / 60) + ' min ' + String(s % 60).padStart(2, '0') + ' s'; return s + ' s'; };`

issues.what: The longest side-view call-out "probe tips, 2–8 gf each" ends 2.5 px from the SVG's right edge at every width (label column is a fixed LBL = 140 px; measured right edge 683.5 of viewBox width 686 at 760 px, 603.5 of 606, 283.5 of 286). It is not clipped with the web fonts loaded, but a fallback font a few percent wider will clip the last character. "probe card, 16 sites" in the wafer panel is similarly 1.8 px from the edge in the stacked layout.
issues.fix: Set LBL = 152 (and labelX = ox + Wb - LBL + 6) so the column has ≥ 12 px of slack, or shorten the label to "probe tips, 2–8 gf" (the "each" is already in the PARTS.tips info text); for the wafer panel give cardLbl x = ox + Wa - 6.

issues.what: Speed-bin wording: "Bin 1 · pass, fast (low V_min)" / "Bin 3 · pass, slow (high V_min)" and legend "pass, fast/slow". In module 14 a lower V_min at the target clock means less power at the same speed (the flagship, better-SKU bin), not a faster die; the widget's own note says exactly that, so the labels contradict it.
issues.fix: Rename to e.g. "Bin 1 · pass, best SKU (low V_min)" / "Bin 3 · pass, lowest SKU (high V_min)" with legend "pass, low V_min" / "pass, high V_min", keeping the short labels in sync in BINS[].short.

issues.what: The side-by-side layout needs W ≥ 640 px, but on the real page the widget body is only ~658 px at full article width and drops below 640 (stacked) as soon as the browser window is narrower than ~1000 px. In the stacked state the wafer stays capped at r = 150 and sits centred with ~150 px of empty margin on each side (wmid720 render at W = 606), and the "edge exclusion 3 mm" caption floats bottom-left with no leader to the dashed ring it names.
issues.fix: Either let the wafer panel shrink so the wide layout holds down to ~560 px (e.g. `const wide = W >= 560; const Wa = wide ? Math.min(300, Math.round(W * 0.45)) : W;` and r = min(150, (Wa-20)/2) already adapts), or in the stacked state let r grow to min(170, (Wa-20)/2) and add a short dashed leader from the "edge exclusion 3 mm" text to the ring at its lower-left.

issues.what: Two side-view leaders run through other parts: the "space transformer" leader passes through the downward-looking camera's lens dot, and the "probe card + stiffener" leader skims the right head-plate block (visible at 3× zoom of every 760 px shot). Cosmetic, but the camera's orange dot then reads as a point on the leader.
issues.fix: Move the downward camera to camX = X(0.66) so it sits left of the leader fan, and anchor the ST leader at its right end plus 3 px (`['st', X(0.32) + 3, 88]`) or route ST/camera leaders with a small horizontal jog (x2 = labelX - 5 on the same y, then to the label).

result.praise: Physics and economics match module 14 throughout: Y = e^-A·D0 with A in cm² (800 mm² at 0.10/cm² → 44.9 %, 69 candidate dies), tester cost $0.108/s and 240 s single-site → $25.92/die and 4 h 38 min per wafer, mobile 16-site 25 s at $0.05/s → $0.08/die, 0.4 s index and 90 s load/align, overtravel 50–75 µm, 2–8 gf, scrub 10–25 µm, ±1 µm stage, 775 µm wafer, −40 to +150 °C chuck, ~12 000 probes, ~350 N, 78 µm thermal growth. Harness report is clean (no console errors beyond the harness favicon 404, no overlaps, no clipped or tiny text, no hard-coded colours) at 760/360 in both themes; controls wrap and readouts stack at 360 px; every slider extreme gives sensible numbers (3 133 dies, 209 h, 1.4 % yield → 0.9 good dies, $250/good die). First frame is meaningful (45 % of a wafer already sorted, side view in contact), reduced-motion starts paused with a working Play/Pause, hover and keyboard focus highlight each part with a clear explanation, die <title> tooltips work, auto-start of the next wafer works, and repeated remount, resize and slider changes while playing throw nothing. The live cross-section strip of the current die row on the wafer in the side view is a genuinely nice teaching touch.

issues.what: At 360 px (SVG field W = 286 px) the Step 3 label "Δx = 150 nm (drawn to scale)" (site/widgets/hybrid-bond.js line 150, mono 12.5 px starting at x = LZ+6 = 90) runs off the right edge of the cross-section and is cut off ("...(drawn to scal"). This happens for every alignment value at phone width; the harness did not flag it because its 360 px analysis only runs on the idle Step 1 frame. Violates QA criteria 4 (nothing cut off at the SVG edge) and 5 (works at 360 px).
issues.fix: In drawX() for s === 2 use a short label when narrow, e.g. txt(LZ + 6, yT + 27, narrow ? 'Δx = ' + st.err + ' nm' : 'Δx = ' + st.err + ' nm (drawn to scale)', ...), or anchor it 'end' at W - 4; keep the '(drawn to scale)' remark in the strip line. Re-render at 360 px on Step 3 (add a 360 px Step 3 shot to the scenario or check manually).

issues.what: The CMP-dishing slider's low end contradicts module 17. The module says the dishing window is 2–5 nm because "too little and the dielectric will not seal" / "recess the pad by less and the copper touches before the dielectric has sealed". The widget only models the too-much side: at 1 or 1.5 nm dishing the readout (update(), lines 292–300) and the Step 5 strip (line 173) turn green and say "pads meet, pressed by 3.3 nm", teaching that less dishing is simply better. Slider extreme gives a physically wrong verdict (criterion 3).
issues.fix: Add a low-dishing branch: e.g. const tooLittle = st.dish < 2; in update() colour rCu with var(--warn)/var(--bad) and set rCuLbl to 'too little dishing (< 2 nm): Cu touches before the oxide has sealed; keep 2–5 nm'; mirror it in the Step 5 strip line (and optionally a Step 1 hint in the sL1 strip). Add a scenario shot at dishing 1 nm on Step 5.

issues.what: At 360 px on Step 3 the two alignment crosses are drawn at mx = LZ - 10 = 74 px (line 146–147) and collide with the 12 px "SiO₂ / SiCN" labels that end at about x = 66–70 px; the top cross (offset by Δx) and the bottom cross both touch/overlap the 'N'. Text overlapping shapes (criterion 4).
issues.fix: When narrow, place the marks clear of the label: e.g. const mx = narrow ? LZ + 2 : LZ - 10 and start the pad loop at LZ + pp/4 (unchanged) so the marks sit in the gap before the first pad; or shorten the dielectric label to 'SiO₂' when narrow. Check that the dashed vertical link between the marks still clears the label.

issues.what: With the particle switched on at Step 4 (index 3) the bond-wave rAF loop runs forever with nothing to animate: go() sets st.playing = anim && !reduced regardless of the particle (line 255), frame() keeps advancing phase (line 319) and drawX() rebuilds ~86 SVG nodes every frame (measured ~60–180 rAF/s continuously, still running after 8 s), while the Play/Pause button is hidden (line 253) so the user cannot stop it. Wastes CPU while the widget is visible (spec rule 5).
issues.fix: In go(): st.playing = anim && !reduced && !(st.step === 3 && st.particle). In update(): if (st.step === 3) { st.playing = !reduced && !st.particle; syncPlay(); if (st.playing) start(); } so toggling the particle on stops the loop and toggling it off restarts it.

issues.what: Small layout/wording nits: (a) Step 3 leaves a ~45 px empty band at the top of the cross-section at every width (title at y = 13, top die starts at y ≈ 60 because gap = 44); (b) at 360 px the dishing bracket on Step 1 shows only a red 'I' with no 'N nm' label for pitch ≤ 6 µm (pp - pw < 44, line 134), so the notch is unlabelled in place; (c) during the anneal ramp the strip briefly reads 'marginal: needs the sideways-constraint boost' (T ≈ 100–190 °C) even at the default 3 nm dishing, which reads as a warning about the recipe rather than a transient; (d) the roadmap note says '9 µm: SoIC as shipped…' while the slider reads 10 µm; (e) at 360 px with the particle on at Step 5, the 'Cu (17 ppm/°C) outgrows SiO₂ (0.5) → rises' line at y = fL3 + 18 = 90 sits on the top-die edge (yTS ≈ 90), descenders touching the silicon band.
issues.fix: (a) On Step 3 put the Δx / budget line or the tool line in the free zone above the top die (fL1) instead of inside the gap; (b) relax the label test to pp - pw >= 30 or place the 'N nm' label above the face when it does not fit in the recess; (c) only show the marginal/open verdict once T has reached its final value (ph >= 0.6), show 'heating…' before; (d) use '≥ 9 µm:' or key the note on the slider value; (e) when part && narrow, drop the fL3 + 18 line or move the free-zone lines up by 6 px.

result.praise: Strong widget overall: the cross-section is a real, in-place-labelled schematic (Si bodies, SiO₂/SiCN, Cu pads with via stubs, real dishing notches, silanol dots that appear after activation and are consumed by the bond wave, segmented dielectric-only bond line, heat tint and Cu rise closing the recess, to-scale particle with the die riding on it) and every step visibly changes the drawing. Physics checks out against module 17: 1/p² (27 778/mm² at 6 µm), ±p/20 budget (±300 nm), 0.78 µm/°C wafer growth (±0.38 °C), α·ΔT·t = 4.3 nm Cu rise, Tong–Gösele void (7.7 mm WoW / 0.98 mm CoW at 1 µm; 2.4 mm at 0.1 µm, matching the module's 'several mm', '~1 mm or less' and 'mm-scale' statements), ISO 1 limit and tool names all correct; formulas cited. Harness report is clean at 760 and 360 in both themes (no overlaps, clipping at idle, tiny text, hard-coded colours, or console errors beyond the page-level favicon 404). Animation behaviour verified with reduced-motion emulated off: Play/Pause reflects state, bond wave loops and anneal runs once (T ramp 25→275 °C, pads meet then fuse), rAF drops to 0 when paused, when scrolled off-screen, after the anneal finishes and after cleanup; remount is clean. Reduced-motion frames (wave at 64 %, finished anneal) are informative and Play/Replay still work. Light theme contrast is good throughout and 360 px controls wrap correctly.

issues.what: Unpainted gap between pad and copper in the over-polish state (site/widgets/cmp-planarize.js drawXS, the `waf` polyline uses `Math.max(s, d)`). Wherever the copper top `s` is below the pad but the pad does not follow it (the narrow-line dishing Da on every array line, and the 10 % of Dw the pad does not follow in the wide line), the slurry-film polygon is built down to the field/dielectric level instead of down to the copper, so the sliver between pad and copper shows the page --ground colour: black caps on every narrow line and a black crescent under the pad in the wide-line dish in dark theme, white caps/crescent in light theme. It is visible in every end-of-run render (760 dark/light end-overpolish, width-min/max, density-10, 360 px end) and becomes prominent scallops at density 90 % (lines 0.9 µm wide, Da ≈ 10 nm) and at 360 px (vertical ×52). A non-expert reads it as voids on top of the lines.
issues.fix: In drawXS change `waf.push(px + ',' + Y(Math.max(s, d)).toFixed(1))` to `waf.push(px + ',' + Y(s).toFixed(1))` so the slurry film always fills from the pad down to the copper surface (s ≤ p holds in every branch: bulk s = min(h0, pl) ≤ pl; wide s = −Dw·para ≤ −0.9·Dw·para; narrow s = d − Da·para ≤ d; field s = d). Re-render density-90-end and the 360 end shot to confirm the caps are slurry-coloured (var(--si) band), not ground-coloured.

issues.what: During the first ~7 s the 'Cu overburden: N nm left over the field' chip and the eddy-current readout report the pad-plane height (660 → 600 nm) while the chip beside it says the field copper is '600 nm + plating topography'; at t = 0 the widget says both '660 nm left over the field' and '600 nm'. The readout label 'time to clear 660 nm' is consistent with the model, but the 'over the field' wording is wrong until the humps are gone.
issues.fix: Report Math.min(m.plane, OB) as the field thickness in the chip, the sensor text and the status line (or reword the chip to 'pad plane N nm above the barrier' while plane > OB).

issues.what: The explanatory chip 'at high density the whole array sinks as a block: erosion beats dishing' is chosen purely by E > Dw + 5, so it appears at ρ = 50 % whenever the wide line is narrow (width-min-end shot, w = 0.2 µm: erosion 11 nm vs dishing 3 nm) even though density is not high.
issues.fix: Gate that branch on st.rho >= 0.7 (or on E > dishSat(psi, w)) and let the w < 1 case fall through to the 'pad bridges every narrow line' text.

issues.what: Soft-landing status text (plane < 95 nm) says 'Rate and pressure are lowered so the barrier is exposed gently' but the readouts, formula and the drawing keep the same RR and P (single-rate model, as the note admits), so the numbers contradict the sentence.
issues.fix: Reword to 'On the real tool platen 2 would now lower rate and pressure; this model keeps one rate' or actually scale RR by ~0.5 in the soft-landing phase and show it in the readout.

issues.what: Label placement over the feature being described: 'field level = top of dielectric' chip sits inside the right end of the wide-line dish after endpoint (covers the dish edge at 760 and most of it at 360), and the 'erosion N nm' chip sits over the line tops; in the side view the 'wafer, 300 mm, face-down' baseline is at padTop−4 so its comma descenders touch the slurry-film line on the pad.
issues.fix: Move the field-level chip down to Y(0)+30 or to the far-right field strip when tOver > 0; place the erosion chip at Y(-m.E) + 30; raise the wafer label 3 px (padTop − 7) and shift the retaining-ring/membrane labels up by the same amount.

issues.what: Caption is three sentences (WIDGET_SPEC rule: one sentence under the title).
issues.fix: Trim caption to one sentence, e.g. 'Press Play and watch the pad shave the copper flat at Preston's rate, the eddy-current endpoint fire at the barrier, then the wide line dish and the dense array erode during over-polish.'

result.praise: Strong widget overall: the harness report is clean (no overlaps, no clipping, no tiny text, no hard-coded colors, only the generic /favicon.ico 404), both themes and 360 px lay out correctly, and runtime behaviour verified in headless Chrome is solid (autoplays under no-preference motion, starts paused at t≈5 s under reduced motion, remount gives unique ids cmpN-pad/cmpN-hatch, cleanup cancels the loop with no errors, IntersectionObserver pauses it off-screen and resumes, Replay/Reset/time-scrub clamp correctly when tEnd shrinks). Physics matches module 12: RR = Kp·P·v with v = ω·r_offset (uniform for matched rpm, rotation directions consistent in the top view), 499 nm/min at 1.5 psi/80 rpm, 79 s to clear 660 nm (module: ~1.2 min for 600 nm at 500 nm/min), 1 psi = 6.9 kPa, slurry chemistry (H2O2/glycine/BTA/silica), grooved polyurethane pad, ~750 mm platen, eddy-current + reflectance/torque endpoint, 10–30 nm spec, 70–80 % density cap, and the resistance-rise arithmetic all check out; extremes (0.5 psi/30 rpm, 5 psi/120 rpm, ρ 10/90 %, w 0.2/10 µm) give sane numbers. The two-view tool schematic and the auto-zooming cross-section with in-place labels genuinely teach at a glance.
